children.text: Chapter 1
vimalakalāśrayābhinavasṛṣṭimahā jananī bharitatanuś ca pañcamukhaguptarucir janakaḥ
children.translated_text: May the great mother, the source of Abhinava's stainless creation, resting in the pure kalā, and the father, whose body is full and whose hidden five-faced radiance is beautiful,

children.text: tadubhayayāmalasphuritabhāvavisargamayaṃ hṛdayam anuttarāmṛtakulaṃ mama saṃsphuratāt ||
children.translated_text: make my heart shine forth: the incomparable nectar-family, consisting of the emanative outpouring of awareness that flashes from the union of those two.

children.text: vitatas tantrāloko vigāhituṃ naiva śakyate sarvaiḥ
children.translated_text: The extensive <s>Tantrāloka</s> cannot be plunged into by everyone.

children.text: ṛjuvacanaviracitam idaṃ tu tantrasāraṃ tataḥ śṛṇuta ||
children.translated_text: Therefore listen now to this <s>Tantrasāra</s>, composed in straightforward words.

children.text: śrīśambhunāthabhāskaracaraṇanipātaprabhāpagatasaṃkocam
children.translated_text: Contemplate this lotus-heart of <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, whose contraction has been dispelled by the radiance falling from the solar feet of venerable <s>Śambhunātha</s>,

children.text: abhinavaguptahṛdambujam etad vicinuta maheśapūjanahetoḥ ||
children.translated_text: for the sake of the worship of <s>Maheśa</s>.

children.text: iha jñānaṃ mokṣakāraṇaṃ bandhanimittasya ajñānasya virodhakatvāt dvividhaṃ ca ajñānaṃ buddhigataṃ pauruṣaṃ ca tatra buddhigatam aniścayasvabhāvaṃ viparītaniścayātmakaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Here, knowledge is the cause of liberation, because it is opposed to ignorance, which is the cause of bondage. Ignorance is of two kinds: located in the intellect and belonging to the person. Of these, that located in the intellect has the nature either of uncertainty or of a contrary certainty.

children.text: pauruṣaṃ tu vikalpasvabhāvaṃ saṃkucitaprathātmakaṃ tad eva ca mūlakāraṇaṃ saṃsārasya iti vakṣyāmo malanirṇaye ||
children.translated_text: But personal ignorance has the nature of conceptual construction and consists in contracted manifestation; and that, as we shall say in the determination of impurity, is the root cause of saṃsāra.

children.text: tatra pauruṣam ajñānaṃ dīkṣādinā nivartetāpi kiṃ tu dīkṣāpi buddhigate anadhyavasāyātmake ajñāne sati na sambhavati heyopādeyaniścayapūrvakatvāt tattvaśuddhiśivayojanārūpāyā dīkṣāyā iti ||
children.translated_text: There personal ignorance may indeed be removed by initiation and the like. Yet initiation too is not possible while there is intellectual ignorance in the form of lack of ascertainment, since initiation, whose form is the purification of the principles and conjunction with <s>Śiva</s>, is preceded by certainty about what is to be rejected and what is to be accepted.

children.text: tatra adhyavasāyātmakaṃ buddhiniṣṭham eva jñānaṃ pradhānam tad eva ca abhyasyamānaṃ pauruṣam api ajñānaṃ nihanti vikalpasaṃvidabhyāsasya avikalpāntatāparyavasānāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore knowledge that is of the nature of ascertainment and established in the intellect is primary; and that very knowledge, when repeatedly cultivated, also destroys personal ignorance, because the practice of awareness in conceptual form culminates in the state beyond conceptual construction.

children.text: vikalpāsaṃkucitasaṃvitprakāśarūpo hy ātmā śivasvabhāva iti sarvathā samastavastuniṣṭhaṃ samyaṅniścayātmakaṃ jñānam upādeyam ||
children.translated_text: For the self is of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>, namely the light of consciousness unconstricted by conceptual constructions. Thus knowledge that is a correct certainty grounded in all things in every way is to be accepted.

children.text: tac ca śāstrapūrvakam ||
children.translated_text: And that knowledge is preceded by scripture.

children.text: śāstraṃ ca parameśvarabhāṣitam eva pramāṇam ||
children.translated_text: And scripture spoken by <s>Parameśvara</s> alone is authoritative.

children.text: aparaśāstroktānām arthānāṃ tatra vaiviktyena abhyupagamāt tadarthātiriktayuktisiddhanirūpaṇāc ca tena aparāgamoktaṃ jñānaṃ tāvata eva bandhāt vimocakam na sarvasmāt sarvasmāt tu vimocakaṃ parameśvaraśāstraṃ pañcasrotomayaṃ daśāṣṭādaśavasvaṣṭabhedabhinnam ||
children.translated_text: Since the meanings taught in other scriptures are accepted there in a distinct way, and since a determination established by reasoning beyond their meanings is also made, the knowledge taught in other traditions frees one only from so much bondage, not from all of it. But the scripture of <s>Parameśvara</s>, consisting of the five streams and divided into the ten, eighteen, and sixty-four divisions, frees one from all bondage.

children.text: tato 'pi sarvasmāt sāraṃ ṣaḍardhaśāstrāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Even from all that, the essence is the scriptures of the <s>Ṣaḍardha</s> system.

children.text: tebhyo 'pi mālinīvijayam ||
children.translated_text: And even from those, the <s>Mālinīvijaya</s> is the essence.

children.text: tadantargataś cārthaḥ saṃkalayyāśakyo nirūpayitum ||
children.translated_text: Yet the meaning contained within it cannot be set forth by merely collecting it together without difficulty.

children.text: na ca anirūpitavastutattvasya muktatvaṃ mocakatvaṃ vā śuddhasya jñānasyaiva tathārūpatvāt iti ||
children.translated_text: And one who has not determined the real nature of things has neither liberation nor the power to liberate, since pure knowledge alone has such a nature.

children.text: svabhyastajñānamūlatvāt parapuruṣārthasya tatsiddhaye idam ārabhyate ||
children.translated_text: Because the supreme human aim is rooted in thoroughly practiced knowledge, this work is begun for the accomplishment of that aim.

children.text: ajñānaṃ kila bandhahetur uditaḥ śāstre malaṃ tat smṛtaṃ pūrṇajñānakalodaye tad akhilaṃ nirmūlatāṃ gacchati ||
children.translated_text: Ignorance is declared in scripture to be the cause of bondage; it is remembered there as impurity. When the full kalā of knowledge arises, all that goes to utter uprooting.

children.text: dhvastāśeṣamalātmasaṃvidudaye mokṣaś ca tenāmunā śāstreṇa prakaṭīkaromi nikhilaṃ yaj jñeyatattvaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When the self-awareness in which every impurity has been destroyed arises, there is liberation. Therefore by means of this scripture I make manifest all that may be the knowable reality.

children.text: tatra iha svabhāva eva paramopādeyaḥ sa ca sarvabhāvānāṃ prakāśarūpa eva aprakāśasya svabhāvatānupapatteḥ sa ca nānekaḥ prakāśasya taditarasvabhāvānupraveśāyoge svabhāvabhedābhāvāt deśakālāv api ca asya na bhedakau tayor api tatprakāśasvabhāvatvāt iti eka eva prakāśaḥ sa eva ca saṃvit arthaprakāśarūpā hi saṃvit iti sarveṣām atra avivāda eva ||
children.translated_text: Now here, one's own nature alone is supremely to be accepted. And that is precisely the form of light belonging to all entities, because what is not light cannot coherently be one's own nature. Nor is it many: since light cannot admit the nature of anything other than itself, there is no difference of own-nature. Nor do place and time differentiate it, because they too have the nature of being illuminated by it. Thus light is one alone, and that itself is consciousness, for consciousness has the nature of illuminating objects; on this point there is no disagreement among anyone.

children.text: sa ca prakāśo na paratantraḥ prakāśyataiva hi pāratantryam prakāśyatā ca prakāśāntarāpekṣitaiva na ca prakāśāntaraṃ kiṃcit asti iti svatantra ekaḥ prakāśaḥ svātantryād eva ca deśakālākārāvacchedavirahāt vyāpako nityaḥ sarvākāranirākārasvabhāvaḥ tasya ca svātantryam ānandaśaktiḥ taccamatkāra icchāśaktiḥ prakāśarūpatā cicchaktiḥ āmarśātmakatā jñānaśaktiḥ sarvākārayogitvaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ ity evaṃ mukhyābhiḥ śaktibhiḥ yukto 'pi vastuta icchājñānakriyāśaktiyuktaḥ anavacchinnaḥ prakāśo nijānandaviśrāntaḥ śivarūpaḥ sa eva svātantryāt ātmānaṃ saṃkucitam avabhāsayan aṇur iti ucyate ||
children.translated_text: And that light is not dependent on another, for dependence is simply the condition of being illuminated, and being illuminated depends on another light; but there is no other light at all. Therefore the one light is independent. Precisely because of its freedom, since it lacks limitation by place, time, or form, it is pervasive, eternal, and by nature all-formed and formless. Its freedom is the power of bliss; its relish of that is the power of will; its nature as light is the power of consciousness; its reflective awareness is the power of knowledge; and its possession of all forms is the power of action. Thus, although endowed with these principal powers, in reality it is the unlimited light endowed with the powers of will, knowledge, and action, resting in its own bliss, of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>. That very light, through its freedom, manifests itself as contracted and is called the atomic soul.

children.text: punar api ca svātmānaṃ svatantratayā prakāśayati yena anavacchinnaprakāśaśivarūpatayaiva prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: And again it manifests its own self freely, whereby it appears precisely as the unlimited light whose nature is <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: tatrāpi svātantryavaśāt anupāyam eva svātmānaṃ prakāśayati sopāyaṃ vā sopāyatve 'pi icchā vā jñānaṃ vā kriyā vā abhyupāya iti traividhyaṃ śāmbhavaśāktāṇavabhedena samāveśasya tatra caturvidham api etad rūpaṃ krameṇa atra upadiśyate ||
children.translated_text: There too, by the force of freedom, it manifests its own self either without any means or with a means. Even when there is a means, the means may be will, knowledge, or action; thus realization is threefold, divided into <s>Śāmbhava</s>, <s>Śākta</s>, and <s>Āṇava</s>. Here this fourfold form will be taught in sequence.

children.text: ātmā prakāśavapur eṣa śivaḥ svatantraḥ svātantryanarmarabhasena nijaṃ svarūpam
children.translated_text: This self is <s>Śiva</s>, whose body is light and who is free; in the delighted force of freedom, his own nature

children.text: saṃchādya yat punar api prathayeta pūrṇaṃ tac ca kramākramavaśād athavā tribhedāt ||
children.translated_text: he conceals, and then again makes it fully manifest, either according to sequence and non-sequence or according to the threefold division.

children.text: Chapter 2
atha anupāyam eva tāvat vyākhyāsyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now first we shall explain the state that is without any means.

children.text: yadā khalu dṛḍhaśaktipātāviddhaḥ svayam eva itthaṃ vivecayati sakṛd eva guruvacanam avadhārya tadā punar upāyavirahito nityoditaḥ asya samāveśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When, indeed, one pierced by firm <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power) himself discerns in this way after grasping the guru's word only once, then his <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption) is again without means and ever arisen.

children.text: atra ca tarka eva yogāṅgam iti kathaṃ vivecayati iti cet ucyate yo 'yaṃ parameśvaraḥ svaprakāśarūpaḥ svātmā tatra kim upāyena kriyate na svarūpalābho nityatvāt na jñaptiḥ svayaṃprakāśamānatvāt nāvaraṇavigamaḥ āvaraṇasya kasyacid api asaṃbhavāt na tadanupraveśaḥ anupraveṣṭuḥ vyatiriktasya abhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: Here, if it is asked, 'Since reasoning alone is a limb of yoga, how does he discern?', the answer is given: this <s>Parameśvara</s>, whose form is self-luminous, is one's own self. What can be accomplished there by a means? Not the attainment of one's true nature, because it is eternal; not cognition, because it shines by itself; not the removal of a covering, because no covering at all is possible; and not entry into it, because there is no separate entrant.

children.text: kaś cātra upāyaḥ tasyāpi vyatiriktasya anupapatteḥ tasmāt samastam idam ekaṃ cinmātratattvaṃ kālena akalitaṃ deśena aparicchinnam upādhibhir amlānam ākṛtibhir aniyantritaṃ śabdair asaṃdiṣṭaṃ pramāṇair aprapañcitaṃ kālādeḥ pramāṇaparyantasya svecchayaiva svarūpalābhanimittaṃ ca svatantram ānandaghanaṃ tattvaṃ tad eva ca aham tatraiva antar mayi viśvaṃ pratibimbitam evaṃ dṛḍhaṃ viviñcānasya śaśvad eva pārameśvaraḥ samāveśo nirupāyaka eva tasya ca na mantrapūjādhyānacaryādiniyantraṇā kācit ||
children.translated_text: And what means could there be here, since even that cannot coherently be separate? Therefore all this is one reality consisting only of consciousness, unmeasured by time, unlimited by place, unstained by limiting adjuncts, unconstrained by forms, not indicated by words, not elaborated by means of knowledge; and the reality that is independent, a mass of bliss, and the cause of the manifestation of everything from time up to the means of knowledge by its own will alone, is precisely 'I'. In that very reality, within me, the universe is reflected. For one who discerns this firmly at all times, the <s>samāveśa</s> belonging to <s>Parameśvara</s> is indeed without means, and for him there is no restriction by mantra, worship, meditation, observance, and the like.

children.text: Chapter 3

yad etat prakāśarūpaṃ śivatattvam uktam tatra akhaṇḍamaṇḍale yadā praveṣṭuṃ na śaknoti tadā svātantryaśaktim eva adhikāṃ paśyan nirvikalpam eva bhairavasamāveśam anubhavati ayaṃ ca asya upadeśaḥ sarvam idaṃ bhāvajātaṃ bodhagagane pratibimbamātraṃ pratibimbalakṣaṇopetatvāt idaṃ hi pratibimbasya lakṣaṇaṃ yat bhedena bhāsitam aśaktam anyavyāmiśratvenaiva bhāti tat pratibimbam mukharūpam iva darpaṇe rasa iva dantodake gandha iva ghrāṇe mithunasparśa iva ānandendriye śūlakuntādisparśo vā antaḥsparśanendriye pratiśrutkeva vyomni ||
children.translated_text: When one is unable to enter into that undivided circle of <s>Śiva</s>-reality, whose nature has been said to be luminosity, then, seeing the power of freedom itself as predominant, one experiences the non-conceptual <s>Bhairava</s>-absorption. And this is the instruction for him: this whole multitude of entities is only a reflection in the sky of awareness, because it possesses the characteristics of a reflection. For this is the mark of a reflection: what appears as differentiated, while unable to exist so, appears only through mixture with another; that is a reflection, like the form of a face in a mirror, flavor in water held at the teeth, smell in the nose, the touch of sexual union in the organ of bliss, the touch of a spear, lance, and the like in the inner organ of touch, or an echo in space.

children.text: na hi sa raso mukhyaḥ tatkāryavyādhiśamanādyadṛṣṭeḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that flavor is not primary, since its effects, such as curing illness, are not observed.

children.text: nāpi gandhasparśau mukhyau guṇinaḥ tatra abhāve tayor ayogāt kāryaparamparānārambhāt ca ||
children.translated_text: Nor are smell and touch primary qualities, because, when the possessor of the quality is absent there, those two are impossible, and because they do not initiate a chain of effects.

children.text: na ca tau na staḥ dehoddhūlanavisargādidarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: Yet those two are not nonexistent, because rubbing the body and emission and the like are observed.

children.text: śabdo 'pi na mukhyaḥ ko 'pi vakti iti āgacchantyā iva pratiśrutkāyāḥ śravaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Sound too is not something primary, because an echo is heard as if coming from someone speaking.

children.text: evaṃ yathā etat pratibimbitaṃ bhāti tathaiva viśvaṃ parameśvaraprakāśe ||
children.translated_text: Thus, just as this appears reflected, so too does the universe appear in the luminosity of <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: nanu atra bimbaṃ kiṃ syāt mābhūt kiṃcit ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, what would the original image be here? Let there be none at all.

children.text: nanu kim akāraṇakaṃ tat hanta tarhi hetupraśnaḥ tat kiṃ bimbavācoyuktyā hetuś ca parameśvaraśaktir eva svātantryāparaparyāyā bhaviṣyati viśvapratibimbadhāritvāc ca viśvātmakatvaṃ bhagavataḥ saṃvinmayaṃ hi viśvaṃ caitanyasya vyaktisthānam iti tad eva hi viśvam atra pratīpam iti pratibimbadhāritvam asya tac ca tāvat viśvātmakatvaṃ parameśvarasya svarūpaṃ na anāmṛṣṭaṃ bhavati citsvabhāvasya svarūpānāmarśanānupapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: But is it causeless? Well then, the question is about a cause; what need is there for the expression 'original image'? And the cause will be precisely the power of <s>Parameśvara</s>, whose other name is freedom. Because he bears the reflection of the universe, the Blessed One has a universal nature consisting of consciousness, for the universe is the place where consciousness becomes manifest. Indeed that very universe is here reflected, and so he bears its reflection. And that universal nature of <s>Parameśvara</s> cannot be unapprehended as his own nature, because for one whose nature is consciousness it is impossible not to apprehend one's own nature.

children.text: svarūpānāmarśane hi vastuto jaḍataiva syāt āmarśaś ca ayaṃ na sāketikaḥ api tu citsvabhāvatāmātranāntarīyakaḥ paranādagarbha uktaḥ sa ca yāvān viśvavyavasthāpakaḥ parameśvarasya śaktikalāpaḥ tāvantam āmṛśati ||
children.translated_text: For if one's own nature were not apprehended, there would in reality be mere insentience. And this apprehension is not conventional; rather, it necessarily accompanies the mere fact of being consciousness, and is said to contain the supreme resonance. It apprehends the whole aggregate of powers of <s>Parameśvara</s> that establishes the entire ordering of the universe.

children.text: tatra mukhyās tāvat tisraḥ parameśvarasya śaktayaḥ anuttarecchonmeṣa iti tad eva parāmarśatrayam a i u iti etasmād eva tritayāt sarvaḥ śaktiprapañcaḥ caryate anuttara eva hi viśrāntir ānandaḥ icchāyām eva viśrāntiḥ īśanam unmeṣa eva hi viśrāntir ūrmiḥ yaḥ kriyāśakteḥ prārambhaḥ tad eva parāmarśatrayam ā ī ū iti ||
children.translated_text: There, to begin with, the principal powers of <s>Parameśvara</s> are three: the unsurpassed, will, and opening. This is the triad of reflective awareness: a, i, u. From this very triad the whole expansion of powers proceeds. For in the unsurpassed there is repose as bliss; in will there is repose as lordship; and in opening there is repose as wave, which is the beginning of the power of action. This is the triad of reflective awareness: ā, ī, ū.

children.text: atra ca prācyaṃ parāmarśatrayaṃ prakāśabhāgasāratvāt sūryātmakaṃ caramaṃ parāmarśatrayaṃ viśrāntisvabhāvāhlādaprādhānyāt somātmakam iyati yāvat karmāṃśasya anupraveśo nāsti ||
children.translated_text: Here the earlier triad of reflective awareness, because the luminous aspect is its essence, is solar in nature; the latter triad of reflective awareness, because repose, innate delight, is predominant, is lunar in nature, so long as there is no entrance of the portion of action.

children.text: yadā tu icchāyām īśane ca karma anupraviśati yat tat iṣyamāṇam īśyamāṇam iti ca ucyate tadā asya dvau bhedau prakāśamātreṇa raśrutiḥ viśrāntyā laśrutiḥ ralayoḥ prakāśastambhasvabhāvatvāt iṣyamāṇaṃ ca na bāhyavat sphuṭam sphuṭarūpatve tad eva nirmāṇaṃ syāt na icchā īśanaṃ vā ataḥ asphuṭatvāt eva śrutimātraṃ ralayoḥ na vyañjanavat sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when action enters into will and lordship, so that it is called 'being willed' and 'being ruled', then this has two divisions: with mere luminosity there is the r-sound, and with repose there is the l-sound, because r and l have the nature of pillars of manifestation. And what is being willed is not distinct like an external object; if it had a distinct form, it would be a creation itself, not will or lordship. Therefore, precisely because of its indistinctness, there is only the sound of r and l, not a settled state like a consonant.

children.text: tad etad varṇacatuṣṭayam ubhayacchāyādhāritvāt napuṃsakam ṛ ṝ ﾱ ﾲ iti ||
children.translated_text: This set of four phonemes, because it bears the hue of both, is neuter: ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, ḹ.

children.text: anuttarānandayoḥ icchādiṣu yadā prasaraḥ tadā varṇadvayam e oṃ iti ||
children.translated_text: When there is an extension of the unsurpassed and bliss into will and the other powers, then there are the two phonemes e and oṃ.

children.text: tatrāpi punar anuttarānandasaṃghaṭṭāt varṇadvayam ai au iti ||
children.translated_text: There too, again, from the conjunction of the unsurpassed and bliss there are the two phonemes ai and au.

children.text: sā iyaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ tad eva ca varṇacatuṣṭayam e ai o au iti ||
children.translated_text: This is the power of action; and that very set of four phonemes is e, ai, o, au.

children.text: tataḥ punaḥ kriyāśaktyante sarvaṃ kāryabhūtaṃ yāvat anuttare pravekṣyati tāvad eva pūrvaṃ saṃvedanasāratayā prakāśamātratvena bindutayā āste am iti ||
children.translated_text: Then again, at the end of the power of action, until everything that has the nature of an effect is about to enter into the unsurpassed, it first remains as the point, as the essence of awareness and as mere luminosity: aṃ.

children.text: tatas tatraiva anuttarasya visargo jāyate aḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, there itself, the visarga of the unsurpassed arises: aḥ.

children.text: evaṃ ṣoḍaśakaṃ parāmarśānāṃ bījasvarūpam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Thus the group of sixteen reflective awarenesses is said to have the nature of seed.

children.text: tadutthaṃ vyañjanātmakaṃ yonirūpam ||
children.translated_text: What arises from that, having the nature of consonants, has the form of the womb.

children.text: tatra anuttarāt kavargaḥ śraddhāyāḥ icchāyāḥ cavargaḥ sakarmikāyā icchāyā dvau ṭavargas tavargaś ca unmeṣāt pavargaḥ śaktipañcakayogāt pañcakatvam ||
children.translated_text: There, from the unsurpassed comes the ka-class; from faith, from will, comes the ca-class; from will as connected with action come the two classes, the ṭa-class and the ta-class; from opening comes the pa-class. Because of conjunction with the five powers, there is fivefoldness.

children.text: icchāyā eva trividhāyā yaralāḥ unmeṣāt vakāraḥ icchāyā eva trividhāyāḥ śaṣasāḥ visargāt hakāraḥ yonisaṃyogajaḥ kṣakāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: From will itself in its threefold form come ya, ra, la; from opening comes va; from will itself in its threefold form come śa, ṣa, sa; from visarga comes ha; and from conjunction with the womb comes kṣa.

children.text: ity eva eṣa bhagavān anuttara eva kuleśvararūpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus this Blessed One, the unsurpassed itself, has the form of <s>Kuleśvara</s>.

children.text: tasya ca ekaiva kaulikī visargaśaktiḥ yayā ānandarūpāt prabhṛti iyatā bahiḥsṛṣṭiparyantena praspandataḥ vargādiparāmarśā eva bahis tattvarūpatāṃ prāptāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And he has one single Kaula power of emission, by which, as he vibrates from the form of bliss onward through this much, up to external creation, the reflective awarenesses beginning with the classes of letters themselves attain the condition of external principles.

children.text: sa ca eṣa visargas tridhā āṇavaḥ cittaviśrāntirūpaḥ śāktaḥ cittasaṃbodhalakṣaṇaḥ śāṃbhavaḥ cittapralayarūpaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: And this emission is threefold: the atomic, whose form is the repose of consciousness; the śākta, characterized by the awakening of consciousness; and the śāṃbhava, whose form is the dissolution of consciousness.

children.text: evaṃ visarga eva viśvajanane bhagavataḥ śaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus emission itself is the power of the Blessed One in generating the universe.

children.text: ity evam iyato yadā nirvibhāgatayā eva parāmarśaḥ tadā eka eva bhagavān bījayonitayā bhāgaśaḥ parāmarśe śaktimān śaktiś ca ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when there is reflective awareness of this much only as undivided, there is the one Blessed One alone; when there is reflective awareness by parts as seed and womb, there are the possessor of power and the power.

children.text: pṛthak aṣṭakaparāmarśe cakreśvarasāhityena navavargaḥ ekaikaparāmarśaprādhānye pañcāśadātmakatā ||
children.translated_text: When there is separate reflective awareness of the groups of eight, there is, together with the lord of the wheel, the group of nine classes; when predominance is given to the reflective awareness of each single phoneme, there is the state consisting of fifty.

children.text: tatrāpi sambhavadbhāgabhedaparāmarśane ekāśītirūpatvam ||
children.translated_text: There too, when reflective awareness takes account of possible divisions of parts, there is the form of eighty-one.

children.text: vastutas tu ṣaṭ eva parāmarśāḥ prasaraṇapratisaṃcaraṇayogena dvādaśa bhavantaḥ parameśvarasya viśvaśaktipūrṇatvaṃ puṣṇanti ||
children.translated_text: In reality, however, there are only six reflective awarenesses; becoming twelve through the conjunction of expansion and withdrawal, they nourish the fullness of the Lord's universal power.

children.text: tā eva etāḥ parāmarśarūpatvāt śaktayo bhagavatyaḥ śrīkālikā iti niruktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These very powers, because they have the form of reflective awareness, are etymologically declared to be the blessed venerable <s>Kālikās</s>.

children.text: ete ca śaktirūpā eva śuddhāḥ parāmarśāḥ śuddhavidyāyāṃ parāpararūpatvena māyonmeṣamātrasaṃkocāt vidyāvidyeśvararūpatāṃ bhajante ||
children.translated_text: And these pure reflective awarenesses, which are themselves forms of power, in pure knowledge, because of a mere contraction consisting in the opening of māyā, assume the forms of knowledge and the lords of knowledge, as both supreme and non-supreme.

children.text: māyāyāṃ punaḥ sphaṭībhūtabhedavibhāgā māyīyavarṇatāṃ bhajante ye paśyantīmadhyamāvaikharīṣu vyāvahārikatvam āsādya bahīrūpatattvasvabhāvatāpattiparyantāḥ te ca māyīyā api śarīrakalpatvena yadā dṛśyante yadā ca teṣām uktanayair etaiḥ jīvitasthānīyaiḥ śuddhaiḥ parāmarśaiḥ pratyujjīvanaṃ kriyate tadā te savīryā bhavanti te ca tādṛśā bhogamokṣapradāḥ ity evaṃ sakalaparāmarśaviśrāntimātrarūpaṃ pratibimbitasamastatattvabhūtabhuvanabhedam ātmānaṃ paśyato nirvikalpatayā śāṃbhavena samāveśena jīvanmuktatā ||
children.translated_text: But in māyā, with their divisions of difference made manifest, they assume the condition of māyīya letters. Having attained conventional operation in paśyantī, madhyamā, and vaikharī, they extend as far as assuming the nature of external principles. And although they are māyīya, when they are seen as comparable to a body, and when they are revived by these pure reflective awarenesses, described in the stated ways and comparable to the place of life for them, then they become potent; and, being such, they bestow enjoyment and liberation. Thus, for one who sees the self as consisting merely in the repose of all reflective awarenesses, containing the reflected divisions of all principles, beings, and worlds, there is liberation while living through non-conceptual śāṃbhava absorption.

children.text: atrāpi pūrvavat na mantrādiyantraṇā kācid iti ||
children.translated_text: Here too, as before, there is no constraint at all by mantra and the like.

children.text: Chapter 4
tatra yadā vikalpaṃ krameṇa saṃskurute samanantaroktasvarūpapraveśāya tadā bhāvanākramasya sattarkasadāgamasadgurūpadeśapūrvakasya asti upayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, when one gradually refines conceptual construction for the sake of entering into the nature just stated, then there is use for the sequence of cultivation, preceded by true reasoning, true scripture, and the instruction of a true guru.

children.text: tathā hi vikalpabalāt eva jantavo baddham ātmānam abhimanyante sa abhimānaḥ saṃsārapratibandhahetuḥ ataḥ pratidvandvirūpo vikalpa uditaḥ saṃsārahetuṃ vikalpaṃ dalayati iti abhyudayahetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: For, by the force of conceptual construction itself, living beings conceive the self as bound. That conception is the cause of the obstruction of saṃsāra; therefore, when a contrary conceptual construction arises, it splits apart the conceptual construction that is the cause of saṃsāra, and is therefore a cause of prosperity.

children.text: sa ca evaṃrūpaḥ samastebhyaḥ paricchinnasvabhāvebhyaḥ śivāntebhyaḥ tattvebhyo yat uttīrṇam aparicchinnasaṃvinmātrarūpaṃ tad eva ca paramārthaḥ tat vastuvyavasthāsthānaṃ tat viśvasya ojaḥ tena prāṇiti viśvam tad eva ca aham ato viśvottīrṇo viśvātmā ca aham iti ||
children.translated_text: And it has this form: that which transcends all the principles, ending with <s>Śiva</s>, whose natures are limited, and which has the form of nothing but unlimited consciousness, that alone is the highest reality; that is the ground of the ordering of things; that is the vigor of the universe; by that the universe lives; and that very thing is I. Therefore I am both beyond the universe and the self of the universe.

children.text: sa ca ayaṃ māyāndhānāṃ na utpadyate sattarkādīnām abhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: And this does not arise for those blinded by māyā, because true reasoning and the rest are absent.

children.text: vaiṣṇavādyā hi tāvanmātra eva āgame rāgatattvena niyamitā iti na ūrdhvadarśane 'pi tadunmukhatāṃ bhajante tataḥ sattarkasadāgamasadgurūpadeśadveṣiṇa eva ||
children.translated_text: For Vaiṣṇavas and the others, being bound by the principle of passion within just that much scripture, do not become inclined toward the higher vision even when they see it; therefore they are hostile to true reasoning, true scripture, and the instruction of a true guru.

children.text: yathoktaṃ pārameśvare
children.translated_text: As has been said in the <s>Pārameśvara</s>:

children.text: vaiṣṇavādyāḥ samastās te vidyārāgeṇa rañjitāḥ
children.translated_text: All those Vaiṣṇavas and the others are colored by passion for their knowledge;

children.text: na vindanti paraṃ tattvaṃ sarvajñajñānavarjitāḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: devoid of omniscient knowledge, they do not find the supreme reality.

children.text: tasmāt śāṃbhavadṛḍhaśaktipātāviddhā eva sadāgamādikrameṇa vikalpaṃ saṃskṛtya paraṃ svarūpaṃ praviśanti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore only those pierced by the firm śāṃbhava descent of power, having refined conceptual construction through the sequence beginning with true scripture, enter into the supreme self-nature.

children.text: nanu itthaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ vikalpyarūpaṃ syāt maivam vikalpasya dvaitādhivāsabhaṅgamātre caritārthatvāt paraṃ tattvaṃ tu sarvatra sarvarūpatayā svaprakāśam eva iti na tatra vikalpaḥ kasyaicit upakriyāyai khaṇḍanāyai vā ||
children.translated_text: But, one may object, in this way the supreme reality would have the form of something conceptually constructed. Not so: conceptual construction has fulfilled its purpose merely in breaking the impression of duality. The supreme reality, however, is self-luminous everywhere as all forms; therefore in regard to it no conceptual construction can serve either to assist or to refute anything at all.

children.text: tatra atidṛḍhaśaktipātāviddhasya svayam eva sāṃsiddhikatayā sattarka udeti yo 'sau devībhiḥ dīkṣita iti ucyate ||
children.translated_text: There, in one pierced by an exceedingly firm <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power), true reasoning arises of itself, by being innate and perfected; he is called one initiated by the goddesses.

children.text: anyasya āgamakrameṇa ityādi savistaraṃ śaktipātaprakāśane vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the case of another, according to the sequence of scripture and so on, we shall explain this in detail in the exposition of <s>śaktipāta</s>.

children.text: kiṃ tu guror āgamanirūpaṇe vyāpāraḥ āgamasya ca niḥśaṅkasajātīyatatprabandhaprasavanibandhanasamucitavikalpodaye vyāpāraḥ tathāvidhavikalpaprabandha eva sattarka iti uktaḥ sa eva ca bhāvanā bhaṇyate asphuṭatvāt bhūtam api artham abhūtam iva sphuṭatvāpādanena bhāvyate yayā iti ||
children.translated_text: But the teacher's function is the determination of scripture; and scripture's function is the arising, without uncertainty, of appropriate conceptual cognition, bound up with the production of an uninterrupted series of cognitions of the same kind. Such a series of conceptual cognitions itself has been called true reasoning; and that itself is also called cultivation, because, being indistinct, an already existent reality is made present as though it were not yet existent, by bringing it to clarity.

children.text: na ca atra sattarkāt śuddhavidyāprakāśarūpāt ṛte anyat yogāṅgaṃ sākṣāt upāyaḥ tapaḥprabhṛteḥ niyamavargasya ahiṃsādeś ca yamaprakārasya pūrakādeḥ prāṇāyāmavargasya vedyamātraniṣṭhatvena ka iva saṃvidi vyāpāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: And here, apart from true reasoning, whose form is the manifestation of pure knowledge, no other limb of yoga is directly a means. What operation can austerity and the rest, the class of observances, or nonviolence and the rest, the forms of restraint, or inhalation and the rest, the class of breath-control, have in consciousness, since they rest only on what is knowable?

children.text: pratyāhāro 'pi karaṇabhūmim eva sātiśayāṃ kuryāt dhyānadhāraṇāsamādhayo 'pi yathottaram abhyāsakrameṇa nirvartyamānā dhyeyavastutādātmyaṃ dhyātuḥ vitareyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Withdrawal of the senses too would only make the level of the instruments more excellent; and meditation, concentration, and absorption, when successively produced through the sequence of practice, would bestow on the meditator identity with the object meditated upon.

children.text: abhyāsaś ca pare tattve śivātmani svasvabhāve na sambhavaty eva ||
children.translated_text: But practice with respect to the supreme reality, the self whose nature is <s>Śiva</s>, is simply not possible.

children.text: saṃvidrūḍhasya prāṇabuddhidehaniṣṭhīkaraṇarūpo hi abhyāsaḥ bhārodvahanaśāstrārthabodhanṛttābhyāsavat saṃvidrūpe tu na kiṃcit ādātavyaṃ na apasaraṇīyam iti katham abhyāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For practice is the fixing of what has become established in consciousness upon breath, intellect, and body, as in the practice of carrying a load, understanding a treatise, or dancing. But in what has the form of consciousness there is nothing to be acquired and nothing to be removed; so how could there be practice?

children.text: kiṃ tarkeṇāpi iti cet uktam atra dvaitādhivāsanirāsaprakāra eva ayaṃ na tu anyat kiṃcid iti ||
children.translated_text: If one asks, 'What even is the use of reasoning?', this has been stated here: it is precisely a method for removing the impression of duality, and not anything else.

children.text: laukike 'pi vā abhyāse cidātmatvena sarvarūpasya tasya tasya dehādeḥ abhimatarūpatāprakaṭīkaraṇaṃ taditararūpanyagbhāvanaṃ ca iti eṣa eva abhyāsārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even in ordinary practice, because this or that thing such as the body has the nature of consciousness and contains every form, the aim of practice is just this: making its intended form manifest and making the other forms recede.

children.text: paratattve tu na kiṃcit apāsyam iti uktam ||
children.translated_text: But with respect to the supreme reality, as has been said, there is nothing at all to be set aside.

children.text: dvaitādhivāso 'pi nāma na kaścana pṛthak vastubhūtaḥ api tu svarūpākhyātimātraṃ tat ato dvaitāpāsanaṃ vikalpena kriyata ity ukteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor is the so-called impression of duality any separate real entity; rather, it is merely the non-recognition of one's own nature. Therefore it is said that the removal of duality is accomplished by conceptual cognition.

children.text: ayaṃ paramārthaḥ svarūpaṃ prakāśamānam akhyātirūpatvaṃ svayaṃ svātantryāt gṛhītaṃ krameṇa projjhya vikāsonmukham atha vikasat atha vikasitam ity anena krameṇa prakāśate tathā prakāśanam api parameśvarasya svarūpam eva tasmāt na atra yogāṅgāni sākṣāt upāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the ultimate truth: one's own nature, though shining, has by its own freedom assumed the form of non-recognition; gradually casting that off, it appears in the sequence 'turning toward expansion,' then 'expanding,' and then 'fully expanded.' Such manifestation too is simply the own nature of <s>Parameśvara</s>. Therefore the limbs of yoga are not direct means here.

children.text: tarkaṃ tu anugṛhṇīyur api sattarka eva sākṣāt tatra upāyaḥ sa eva ca śuddhavidyā sa ca bahuprakāratayā saṃskṛto bhavati tadyathā yāgo homo japo vrataṃ yoga iti tatra bhāvānāṃ sarveṣāṃ parameśvara eva sthitiḥ nānyat vyatiriktam asti iti vikalparūḍhisiddhaye parameśvara eva sarvabhāvārpaṇaṃ yāgaḥ sa ca hṛdyatvāt ye saṃvidanupraveśaṃ svayam eva bhajante teṣāṃ suśakaṃ parameśvare arpaṇam ity abhiprāyeṇa hṛdyānāṃ kusumatarpaṇagandhādīnāṃ bahir upayoga uktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They may, however, support reasoning; yet true reasoning alone is the direct means there, and that itself is pure knowledge. It becomes refined in many forms, such as sacrifice, oblation, recitation, observance, and yoga. Among these, sacrifice is the offering of all entities into <s>Parameśvara</s> alone, in order to establish the conceptual conviction that all entities abide in <s>Parameśvara</s> and that nothing else exists apart from him. And because those entities which are agreeable easily enter consciousness of themselves, the external use of agreeable flowers, libations, perfumes, and the like is taught with the intention that they are easily offered into <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: sarve bhāvāḥ parameśvaratejomayā iti rūḍhavikalpaprāptyai parameśasaṃvidanalatejasi samastabhāvagrāsarasikatābhimate tattejomātrāvaśeṣatvasahasamastabhāvavilāpanaṃ homaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oblation is the immediate dissolution of all entities, so that only that radiance remains, in the fire-radiance of <s>Parameśvara</s>-consciousness, which is intended as delighting in the devouring of all entities, in order to attain the fixed conceptual conviction that all entities consist of the radiance of <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: tathā ubhayātmakaparāmarśodayārthaṃ bāhyābhyantarādiprameyarūpabhinnabhāvānapekṣayaiva evaṃvidhaṃ tat paraṃ tattvaṃ svasvabhāvabhūtam iti antaḥ parāmarśanaṃ japaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, recitation is the inward reflective awareness, for the arising of a recognition that has both aspects, that the supreme reality is of this kind and is one's own nature, quite independently of differentiated entities that are objects of knowledge, such as external, internal, and so forth.

children.text: sarvatra sarvadā nirupāyaparameśvarābhimānalābhāya parameśvarasamatābhimānena dehasyāpi ghaṭāder api avalokanaṃ vratam ||
children.translated_text: Observance is the seeing of even the body, even a pot and the like, with the conviction that they are equal to <s>Parameśvara</s>, so as to obtain everywhere and always the identification with <s>Parameśvara</s> that is without any means.

children.text: yathoktaṃ śrīnandiśikhāyām sarvasāmyaṃ paraṃ vratam iti ||
children.translated_text: As is stated in the venerable <s>Nandiśikhā</s>: 'Equanimity toward all is the supreme observance.'

children.text: itthaṃ vicitraiḥ śuddhavidyāṃśarūpaiḥ vikalpaiḥ yat anapekṣitavikalpaṃ svābhāvikaṃ paramārthatattvaṃ prakāśate tasyaiva sanātanatathāvidhaprakāśamātratārūḍhaye tatsvarūpānusaṃdhānātmā vikalpaviśeṣo yogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when the natural supreme reality, which does not depend on conceptual cognition, is made manifest by various conceptual cognitions that are portions of pure knowledge, then yoga is the special conceptual cognition whose nature is the investigation of that reality's own form, for the sake of becoming established in the mere eternal manifestation of that very kind.

children.text: tatra parameśvaraḥ pūrṇasaṃvitsvabhāvaḥ pūrṇataiva asya śaktiḥ kulaṃ sāmarthyam ūrmiḥ hṛdayaṃ sāraṃ spandaḥ vibhūtiḥ trīśikā kālī karṣaṇī caṇḍī vāṇī bhogo dṛk nityā ityādibhiḥ āgamabhāṣābhiḥ tattadanvarthapravṛttābhiḥ abhidhīyate tena tena rūpeṇa dhyāyināṃ hṛdi āstām iti ||
children.translated_text: There <s>Parameśvara</s>, whose own nature is full consciousness, is described by scriptural terms that proceed according to their respective meanings: his power is fullness itself; it is called family, capacity, wave, heart, essence, vibration, glory, <s>Trīśikā</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, attractress, <s>Caṇḍī</s>, speech, enjoyment, sight, eternal one, and so on. May he remain in the hearts of meditators in each of those forms.

children.text: sā ca samagraśaktitādarśanena pūrṇatāsaṃvit prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: And that consciousness of fullness is made manifest through the vision that it possesses the totality of powers.

children.text: śaktayaś ca asya asaṃkhyeyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And his powers are innumerable.

children.text: kiṃ bahunā yat viśvaṃ tā asya śaktayaḥ tāḥ katham upadeṣṭuṃ śakyāḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: In short: whatever the universe is, those are his powers. How, then, could they be taught one by one?

children.text: tisṛṣu tāvat viśvaṃ samāpyate yayā idaṃ śivādidharaṇyantam avikalpyasaṃvinmātrarūpatayā bibharti ca paśyati ca bhāsayati ca parameśvaraḥ sā asya śrīparaśaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among the three, first, that by which the Lord completes the universe, by which he bears this whole reality from <s>Śiva</s> down to the earth as nothing but non-conceptual consciousness, and by which he sees and illumines it: that is his venerable supreme power, <s>Parāśakti</s>.

children.text: yayā ca darpaṇahastyādivat bhedābhedābhyāṃ sā asya śrīparāparaśaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that by which, as in the case of a mirror and a hand and the like, it is through both difference and non-difference: that is his venerable supreme-and-non-supreme power, <s>Parāparaśakti</s>.

children.text: yayā parasparaviviktātmanā bhedenaiva sā asya śrīmadaparaśaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That by which, through difference alone, things have mutually distinct natures: that is his venerable non-supreme power, <s>Aparaśakti</s>.

children.text: etat trividhaṃ yayā dhāraṇam ātmany eva kroḍīkāreṇa anusaṃdhānātmanā grasate sā asya bhagavatī śrīparaiva śrīmanmātṛsadbhāvakālakarṣiṇyādiśabdāntaraniruktā ||
children.translated_text: That by which he devours this threefold sustaining, by enclosing it in himself and by an act of reflective apprehension: she is his blessed venerable supreme power itself, explained also by other names such as venerable <s>Mātṛsadbhāva</s>, <s>Kālakarṣiṇī</s>, and so on.

children.text: tā etāḥ catasraḥ śaktayaḥ svātantryāt pratyekaṃ tridhaiva vartante ||
children.translated_text: These four powers, by their freedom, each operate in precisely three ways.

children.text: sṛṣṭau sthitau saṃhāre ca iti dvādaśa bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: They are therefore twelve: in creation, maintenance, and dissolution.

children.text: tathā hi saṃvit pūrvam antar eva bhāvaṃ kalayati tato bahir api sphuṭatayā kalayati tatraiva raktimayatāṃ gṛhītvā tataḥ tam eva bhāvam antar upasaṃjihīrṣayā kalayati tataś ca tadupasaṃhāravighnabhūtāṃ śaṅkāṃ nirmiṇoti ca grasate ca grastaśaṅkāṃśaṃ bhāvabhāgam ātmani upasaṃhāreṇa kalayati tata upasaṃhartṛtvaṃ mamedaṃ rūpam ity api svabhāvam eva kalayati tata upasaṃhartṛsvabhāvakalane kasyacid bhāvasya vāsanātmanā avasthitiṃ kasyacit tu saṃvinmātrāvaśeṣatāṃ kalayati tataḥ svarūpakalanānāntarīyakatvenaiva karaṇacakraṃ kalayati tataḥ karaṇeśvaram api kalayati tataḥ kalpitaṃ māyīyaṃ pramātṛrūpam api kalayati saṅkocatyāgonmukhavikāsagrahaṇarasikam api pramātāraṃ kalayati ato vikasitam api rūpaṃ kalayati iti etā dvādaśa bhagavatyaḥ saṃvidaḥ pramātṝn ekaṃ vāpi uddiśya yugapat krameṇa dviśaḥ triśa ityādisthityāpi udayabhāginyaḥ cakravad āvartamānā bahir api māsakalārāśyādikrameṇa antato vā ghaṭapaṭādikrameṇāpi bhāsamānāḥ cakreśvarasya svātantryaṃ puṣṇatyaḥ śrīkālīśabdavācyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For thus consciousness first forms an entity inwardly; then it forms it outwardly as well, in a manifest way; taking on redness in that very entity, it then forms that same entity with the wish to withdraw it inwardly; then it produces and also devours the doubt that obstructs that withdrawal; it forms the portion of the entity whose element of doubt has been devoured by withdrawing it into itself; then it also forms its own nature as, 'this power of withdrawal is my own form'; then, while forming the nature of the withdrawer, it forms the abiding of some entity as a latent impression and the remaining of another as mere consciousness; then, as immediately consequent upon the formation of its own form, it forms the circle of instruments; then it forms the lord of the instruments as well; then it forms even the constructed, māyic form of the knower; and it forms the knower too, who delights in receiving the expansion that is turned toward abandoning contraction; and from this it forms even the expanded form. Thus these twelve blessed powers of consciousness, whether with reference to many knowers or even one, arising simultaneously, successively, in pairs, in triads, and in other such arrangements, revolving like a wheel, and appearing outwardly too according to the sequence of months, kalās, zodiacal groups, and so on, or finally even according to the sequence of pots, cloths, and the like, are called by the word '<s>Kālī</s>', since they nourish the freedom of the Lord of the wheel.

children.text: kalanaṃ ca gatiḥ kṣepo jñānaṃ gaṇanaṃ bhogīkaraṇaṃ śabdanaṃ svātmalayīkaraṇaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And kalana means motion, projection, cognition, enumeration, making into an object of enjoyment, verbal expression, and making something dissolve into one's own self.

children.text: yad āhuḥ śrībhūtirājaguravaḥ kṣepāj jñānāc ca kālī kalanavaśatayātha iti ||
children.translated_text: As the venerable teacher <s>Bhūtirāja</s> said: 'She is <s>Kālī</s> because of projection and cognition, and then because of the power of kalana.'

children.text: eṣa ca arthaḥ tatra tatra madviracite vivaraṇe prakaraṇastotrādau vitatya vīkṣyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This meaning should be examined in detail here and there in the explanation, chapter, hymns, and other works composed by me.

children.text: na atirahasyam ekatra khyāpyaṃ na ca sarvathā gopyam iti hi asmadguravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For our teachers say: what is extremely secret should not be proclaimed in one place, nor should it be wholly concealed.

children.text: tad evam yad uktaṃ yāgahomādi tat evaṃvidhe maheśvara eva mantavyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, what was mentioned as sacrifice, oblation, and the like must be understood as occurring in <s>Maheśvara</s> of this kind.

children.text: sarve hi heyam eva upādeyabhūmirūpaṃ viṣṇutaḥ prabhṛti śivāntaṃ paramaśivatayā paśyanti tac ca mithyādarśanam avaśyatyājyam anuttarayogibhir iti tadartham eva vidyādhipateḥ anubhavastotre mahān saṃrambhaḥ evaṃvidhe yāgādau yogānte ca pañcake pratyekaṃ bahuprakāraṃ nirūḍhiḥ yathā yathā bhavati tathaiva ācaret na tu bhakṣyābhakṣyaśuddhyaśuddhyādivivecanayā vastudharmojjhitayā kalpanāmātrasārayā svātmā khedanīya iti uktaṃ śrīpūrvādau na hi śuddhiḥ vastuno rūpaṃ nīlatvavat anyatra tasyaiva aśuddhicodanāt dānasyeva dīkṣitatve codanātaḥ tasya tat tatra aśuddham iti cet codanāntare 'pi tulyaṃ codanāntaram asat tadbādhitatvāt iti cet na śivacodanāyā eva bādhakatvaṃ yuktisiddhaṃ sarvajñānottarādyanantāgamasiddhaṃ ca iti vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For everyone, from <s>Viṣṇu</s> onward up to <s>Śiva</s>, sees as the supreme <s>Śiva</s> only what is really to be rejected, though it has the form of a level of what is to be accepted; and that false vision must necessarily be abandoned by the unsurpassed yogins. For that very purpose there is great insistence in the experiential hymn of the Lord of Vidyā. In sacrifice and the like of this sort, at the end of yoga, and in each of the five, in whatever many-sided way established practice has arisen, one should act in just that way; but one should not torment one's own self by discriminating what may or may not be eaten, what is pure or impure, and so on, a discrimination devoid of the real nature of things and consisting only in imagination. This is stated in the venerable <s>Pūrva</s> and other scriptures: purity is not the form of a thing, as blueness is, because impurity is enjoined elsewhere for that very same thing, just as giving is enjoined in the case of one who has been initiated. If it is said, 'Because of an injunction, that thing is impure there,' the same applies even to another injunction. If it is said, 'The other injunction is invalid because it is overridden by that one,' no; for we shall say that it is precisely the injunction of <s>Śiva</s> that has overriding force, as established by reasoning and by innumerable scriptures such as the <s>Sarvajñānottara</s>.

children.text: tasmāt vaidikāt prabhṛti pārameśvarasiddhāntatantrakulocchuṣmādiśāstrokto 'pi yo niyamo vidhiḥ vā niṣedho vā so 'tra yāvad akiṃcitkara eva iti siddham ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it is established that any rule, prescription, or prohibition taught here, beginning with the Vedic and extending to the <s>Pārameśvara</s>, <s>Siddhānta</s>, <s>Tantra</s>, <s>Kula</s>, <s>Ucchuṣma</s>, and other scriptures, is here, to that extent, entirely ineffectual.

children.text: tathaiva ca uktaṃ śrīpūrvādau vitatya tantrālokāt anveṣyam ||
children.translated_text: And this very point is stated at length in the venerable <s>Pūrva</s> and other scriptures; it should be sought out from the <s>Tantrāloka</s>.

children.text: Chapter 5

tatra yadā vikalpaḥ svayam eva saṃskāram ātmani upāyāntaranirapekṣatayaiva kartuṃ prabhavati tadā asau pāśavavyāpārāt pracyutaḥ śuddhavidyānugraheṇa parameśaśaktirūpatām āpanna upāyatayā avalambyamānaḥ śāktaṃ jñānam āvirbhāvayati ||
children.translated_text: There, when conceptual thought is by itself capable of producing a refinement in the self without dependence on any other means, then, having fallen away from the activity of the bound soul and having attained, through the grace of pure knowledge, the condition of being the power of <s>Parameśa</s>, that conceptual thought, when relied on as a means, brings forth <s>Śākta</s> knowledge.

children.text: tad etac ca nirṇītam anantara eva āhnike ||
children.translated_text: And this has been determined in the immediately preceding <s>āhnika</s>.

children.text: yadā tu upāyāntaram asau svasaṃskārārthaṃ vikalpo 'pekṣate tadā buddhiprāṇadehaghaṭādikān parimitarūpān upāyatvena gṛhṇan aṇutvaṃ prāpta āṇavaṃ jñānam āvirbhāvayati tatra buddhiḥ dhyānātmikā prāṇaḥ sthūlaḥ sūkṣmaś ca ādya uccāraṇātmā uccāraṇaṃ ca nāma pañca prāṇādyā vṛttayaḥ sūkṣmas tu varṇaśabdavācyo vakṣyate dehaḥ saṃniveśaviśeṣātmā karaṇaśabdavācyaḥ ghaṭādayo bāhyāḥ kumbhasthaṇḍilaliṅgapūjādyupāyatayā kīrtayiṣyamāṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when that conceptual construction, for the sake of refining itself, requires another means, then, taking the intellect, breath, body, pot, and the like, which are limited forms, as means, it attains atomicity and manifests āṇava knowledge. There the intellect is of the nature of meditation; breath is both gross and subtle. The first has the nature of <s>uccāraṇa</s> (recitation or upward utterance), and what is called <s>uccāraṇa</s> is the activity beginning with the five breaths. The subtle breath, however, is what is denoted by the word 'phoneme'; it will be explained later. The body, whose nature is a specific arrangement, is denoted by the word 'instrument'. Pots and the like are external things, to be described as means such as a pot, altar-ground, liṅga-worship, and so on.

children.text: tatra dhyānaṃ tāvat iha ucitam upadekṣyāmaḥ yat etat svaprakāśaṃ sarvatattvāntarbhūtaṃ paraṃ tattvam uktaṃ tad eva nijahṛdayabodhe dhyātvā tatra pramātṛpramāṇaprameyarūpasya vahnyarkasomatritayasya saṃghaṭṭaṃ dhyāyet yāvat asau mahābhairavāgniḥ dhyānavātasamiddhākāraḥ sampadyate tasya prāktanaśaktijvālādvādaśakaparivṛtasya cakrātmanaḥ cakṣurādīnām anyatamasuṣiradvāreṇa niḥsṛtasya bāhye grāhyātmani viśrāntaṃ cintayet tena ca viśrāntena prathamaṃ tadbāhyaṃ somarūpatayā sṛṣṭikrameṇa prapūritaṃ tataḥ arkarūpatayā sthityā avabhāsitaṃ tato 'pi saṃhāravahnirūpatayā vilāpitaṃ tataḥ anuttarātmatām āpāditaṃ dhyāyet ||
children.translated_text: There, first, we shall teach here the meditation that is appropriate. Having meditated in the awareness of one's own heart on that very supreme reality which has been described as self-luminous and containing all the tattvas within itself, one should meditate there on the collision of the triad of fire, sun, and moon, whose form is knower, means of knowledge, and known, until that great <s>Bhairava</s>-fire comes to have the form of being kindled by the wind of meditation. One should think of it as a wheel, surrounded by the twelve flames of its prior powers, issuing out through one or another aperture such as the eye, and coming to rest outside in the object to be grasped. And with that fire thus at rest, one should meditate that first that external object is filled, in the order of creation, as moon-formed; then illuminated in stability as sun-formed; then dissolved as the fire of withdrawal; and after that brought into the state of the unsurpassed.

children.text: evaṃ tac cakraṃ samastabāhyavastvabhedaparipūrṇaṃ sampadyate ||
children.translated_text: In this way that wheel becomes full with the non-difference of all external objects.

children.text: tato vāsanāśeṣān api bhāvān tena cakreṇa itthaṃ kṛtān dhyāyet ||
children.translated_text: Then one should meditate that even the entities remaining as latent dispositions have been made so by that wheel.

children.text: evam asya anavarataṃ dhyāyinaḥ svasaṃvinmātraparamārthān sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhāraprabandhān sṛṣṭyādisvātantryaparamārthatvaṃ ca svasaṃvido niścinvataḥ sadya eva bhairavībhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who meditates on this continually, as he ascertains that the streams of creation, maintenance, and withdrawal have the mere fact of his own consciousness as their ultimate reality, and that the freedom beginning with creation is the ultimate reality of his own consciousness, the state of <s>Bhairavī</s> arises immediately.

children.text: abhyāsāt tu sarvepsitasiddhyādayo 'pi ||
children.translated_text: And through practice there also arise all desired accomplishments and the like.

children.text: svaprakāśaṃ samastātmatattvaṃ mātrādikaṃ trayam
children.translated_text: One should meditate on the self-luminous reality of the self of all,

children.text: antaḥkṛtya sthitaṃ dhyāyeddhṛdayānandadhāmani ||
children.translated_text: standing within after internalizing the triad beginning with the measurer, in the abode of the bliss of the heart.

children.text: taddvādaśamahāśaktiraśmicakreśvaraṃ vibhum
children.translated_text: One should meditate on the mighty lord of the wheel of rays,

children.text: vyomabhir niḥsarad bāhye dhyāyet sṛṣṭyādibhāvakam ||
children.translated_text: that is, the twelve great powers, as issuing outward through the spaces and as bringing about creation and the rest.

children.text: tadgrastasarvabāhyāntarbhāvamaṇḍalam ātmani
children.translated_text: The yogin, coming to rest in himself, should contemplate the circle of inner and outer entities

children.text: viśrāmyan bhāvayed yogī syād evam ātmanaḥ prathā ||
children.translated_text: all swallowed up by that; in this way there comes to be the manifestation of the self.

children.text: iti saṃgrahaślokāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the summary verses.

children.text: iti dhyānam ||
children.translated_text: Thus meditation.

children.text: tatra prāṇam uccicārayiṣuḥ pūrvaṃ hṛdaya eva śūnye viśrāmyati tato bāhye prāṇodayāt tato 'pi bāhyaṃ prati apānacandrāpūraṇena sarvātmatāṃ paśyati tataḥ anyanirākāṅkṣo bhavati tataḥ samānodayāt saṃghaṭṭaviśrāntim anubhavati tata udānavahnyudaye mātṛmeyādikalanāṃ grasate ||
children.translated_text: There, one who wishes to perform <s>uccāraṇa</s> of the breath first rests in emptiness in the heart itself. Then, because of the arising of breath outwardly, and then by the filling of what is still further external through the moon of <s>apāna</s>, he sees all-selfhood. Then he becomes free of expectation of anything else. Then, from the arising of <s>samāna</s>, he experiences repose in the collision. Then, when the fire of <s>udāna</s> arises, he swallows up the construction of the knower and known and so forth.

children.text: tadgrāsakavahnipraśame vyānodaye sarvāvacchedavandhyaḥ sphurati ||
children.translated_text: When the fire that swallows that has subsided, with the arising of <s>vyāna</s>, he flashes forth, barren of every delimitation.

children.text: evaṃ śūnyāt prabhṛti vyānāntaṃ yā etā viśrāntayaḥ tā eva nijānando nirānandaḥ parānando brahmānando mahānandaḥ cidānanda iti ṣaṭ ānandabhūmaya upadiṣṭāḥ yāsām ekaḥ anusaṃdhātā udayāstamayavihīnaḥ antarviśrāntiparamārtharūpo jagadānandaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus these rests, beginning with emptiness and ending with <s>vyāna</s>, are taught as the six levels of bliss: one's own bliss, blissless bliss, supreme bliss, brahman-bliss, great bliss, and consciousness-bliss. Their single connector, free from rise and setting and whose ultimate form is inward repose, is world-bliss.

children.text: tat etāsu uccārabhūmiṣu pratyekaṃ dvyādiśaḥ sarvaśo vā viśrāmya anyat taddehaprāṇādivyatiriktaṃ viśrāntitattvam āsādayati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, having rested in each of these grounds of <s>uccāra</s>, by twos and so on or in every way, one attains another reality of repose, distinct from that body, breath, and so forth.

children.text: tad eva sṛṣṭisaṃhārabījoccāraṇarahasyam anusaṃdadhat vikalpaṃ saṃskuryāt āsu ca viśrāntiṣu pratyekaṃ pañca avasthā bhavanti praveśatāratamyāt ||
children.translated_text: Meditating on that very secret of the <s>uccāraṇa</s> of the seeds of creation and withdrawal, one should refine conceptual construction. And in each of these rests there are five states, according to gradations of entry.

children.text: tatra prāg ānandaḥ pūrṇatāṃśasparśāt tata udbhavaḥ kṣaṇaṃ niḥśarīratāyāṃ rūḍheḥ tataḥ kampaḥ svabalākrāntau dehatādātmyaśaithilyāt tato nidrā bahirmukhatvavilayāt ||
children.translated_text: There first is bliss, because of contact with the portion of fullness. Then there is arising, because of being established for a moment in bodilessness. Then there is trembling, because, when one is overpowered by one's own strength, identification with the body slackens. Then there is sleep, because outward-turnedness dissolves.

children.text: ittham anātmani ātmabhāve līne svātmanaḥ sarvamayatvāt ātmani anātmabhāvo vilīyate iti ato ghūrṇiḥ mahāvyāptyudayāt ||
children.translated_text: In this way, when the sense of self in what is not self has dissolved, the sense of non-self in the self dissolves because one's own self is all-formed. Therefore there is <s>ghūrṇi</s> (reeling or divine whirling), because the great pervasion has arisen.

children.text: tā etā jāgradādibhūmayaḥ turyātītāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These are the grounds beginning with waking and ending in what is beyond the fourth.

children.text: etāś ca bhūmayaḥ trikoṇakandahṛttālūrdhvakuṇḍalinīcakrapraveśe bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: And these grounds occur on entry into the triangle, the bulb, the heart, the palate, the upper <s>kuṇḍalinī</s>, and the wheel.

children.text: evam uccāraviśrāntau yat paraṃ spandanaṃ galitāśeṣavedyaṃ yac ca unmiṣad vedyaṃ yac ca unmiṣitavedyaṃ tad eva liṅgatrayam iti vakṣyāmaḥ svāvasare ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the repose of <s>uccāra</s>, that supreme vibration in which all knowable object has melted away, that in which the knowable is just opening, and that in which the knowable has opened: these are precisely the three liṅgas, as we shall explain in their own proper place.

children.text: paraṃ cātra liṅgaṃ yoginīhṛdayam ||
children.translated_text: And the supreme liṅga here is the heart of the yoginī.

children.text: tatra mukhyā spandanarūpatā saṃkocavikāsātmatayā yāmalarūpatodayena visargakalāviśrāntilābhāt ity alam ||
children.translated_text: There the principal state consists in vibration, because repose in the emission-power is obtained through contraction and expansion, with the arising of the form of the couple. Enough on this.

children.text: aprakāśaḥ atra anupraveśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, non-manifestation is entry.

children.text: pūrvaṃ svabodhe tadanu prameye viśramya meyaṃ paripūrayeta
children.translated_text: First, having rested in one's own awareness, and then in the object of knowledge, one should fill the known object.

children.text: pūrṇe 'tra viśrāmyati mātṛmeyavibhāgam āśv eva sa saṃhareta ||
children.translated_text: When it has become full, he rests there and at once withdraws the division between knower and known.

children.text: vyāptyātha viśrāmyati tā imāḥ syuḥ śūnyena sākaṃ ṣaḍupāyabhūmyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then he rests in pervasion. These, together with emptiness, are the six grounds of the means.

children.text: prāṇādayo vyānanapaścimās tallīnaś ca jāgratprabhṛtiprapañcaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The breaths beginning with <s>prāṇa</s> and ending with <s>vyāna</s>, and the manifold display beginning with waking, are dissolved in that.

children.text: abhyāsaniṣṭho 'tra tu sṛṣṭisaṃhṛdvimarśadhāmany acireṇa rohet ||
children.translated_text: But one who is firmly established in practice here quickly rises in the abode of reflective awareness that creates and withdraws.

children.text: iti āntaraślokāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the internal verses.

children.text: iti uccāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Thus the section on utterance.

children.text: asmin eva uccāre sphuran avyaktānukṛtiprāyo dhvaniḥ varṇaḥ tasya sṛṣṭisaṃhārabīje mukhyaṃ rūpaṃ tadabhyāsāt parasaṃvittilābhaḥ tathāhi kādau mānte sācke anacke vā antaruccārite smṛte vā samaviśiṣṭaḥ saṃvitspandasparśaḥ samayānapekṣitvāt paripūrṇaḥ samayāpekṣiṇo 'pi śabdāḥ tadarthabhāvakā manorājyādivat anuttarasaṃvitsparśāt ekīkṛtahṛtkaṇṭhoṣṭho dvādaśāntadvayaṃ hṛdayaṃ ca ekīkuryāt iti varṇarahasyam ||
children.translated_text: In this very utterance, the sound that flashes forth, generally resembling what is still unmanifest, is the phoneme. Its principal form is in the seed of creation and withdrawal; through practice of that, one attains supreme awareness. For thus, when the series from ka to ma, whether with vowels or without vowels, is inwardly uttered or remembered, there is the same contact with the pulse of awareness, complete because it does not depend on convention. Even words that do depend on convention produce the cognition of their meanings, as in a realm imagined by the mind. From contact with unsurpassed awareness one should make the heart, throat, and lips one, and also make one the two <s>dvādaśāntas</s> and the heart. This is the secret of the phonemes.

children.text: antaḥsphuradvimarśānantarasamudbhūtaṃ sitapītādyāntaraṃ varṇam udbhāvyamānaṃ saṃvidam anubhāvayati iti kecit ||
children.translated_text: Some say that an inner phoneme such as white, yellow, and so on, arising immediately after reflective awareness flashing within, when brought forth, makes awareness directly experienced.

children.text: vācyaviraheṇa saṃvitspandād indvarkagatinirodhābhyām
children.translated_text: Through the absence of the expressed object, from the pulse of awareness, by stopping the movement of moon and sun,

children.text: yasya tu samasaṃpraveśāt pūrṇā cidbījapiṇḍavarṇavidhau ||
children.translated_text: for the one whose consciousness is full through equal entry in the procedure of the mass of the seed-phonemes of consciousness,

children.text: iti āntaraślokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thus the internal verse.

children.text: iti varṇavidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the procedure of the phonemes.

children.text: karaṇaṃ tu mudrāprakāśane vakṣyāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As for the instrument, we shall explain it in the exposition of <s>mudrā</s>.

children.text: Chapter 6

sa eva sthānaprakalpanaśabdena uktaḥ tatra tridhā sthānaṃ prāṇavāyuḥ śarīraṃ bāhyaṃ ca tatra prāṇe tāvat vidhiḥ sarvaḥ asau vakṣyamāṇaḥ adhvā prāṇasthaḥ kalyate tasya kramākramakalanaiva kālaḥ sa ca parameśvara eva antarbhāti tadbhāsanaṃ ca devasya kālī nāma śaktiḥ bhedena tu tadābhāsanaṃ kramākramayoḥ prāṇavṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That same thing has been stated by the term 'configuration of place.' There, place is threefold: the vital breath, the body, and the external. Of these, first, the procedure in the breath is as follows. The whole course to be explained, the <s>adhvan</s>, is conceived as residing in the breath. Its conception in sequence and non-sequence is time, and that time shines within <s>Parameśvara</s> himself. The shining forth of that is the power of the Lord called <s>Kālī</s>; but when it shines as differentiated, it is the movement of breath in sequence and non-sequence.

children.text: saṃvid eva hi prameyebhyo vibhaktaṃ rūpaṃ gṛhṇāti ata eva ca avacchedayogāt vedyatāṃ yāntī nabhaḥ tataḥ svātantryāt meye svīkārautsukyena nipatantī kriyāśaktipradhānā prāṇanārūpā jīvasvabhāvā pañcabhī rūpaiḥ dehaṃ yataḥ pūrayati tato 'sau cetana iva bhāti ||
children.translated_text: For awareness itself assumes a form divided off from knowable objects. And precisely because, through connection with limitation, it comes to be knowable, then from the sky, by its freedom, falling upon the object to be measured in eagerness to appropriate it, being dominated by the power of action, having the form called breath, and having the nature of the living being, it fills the body with the five forms; therefore it appears as if conscious.

children.text: tatra kriyāśaktau kālādhvā prācyabhāge uttare tu mūrtivaicitryarūpo deśādhvā tatra varṇamantrapadādhvanaḥ kālādhvani sthitiḥ parasūkṣmasthūlarūpatvāt ||
children.translated_text: There, in the power of action, the temporal <s>adhvan</s> is in the eastern part, while in the northern part is the spatial <s>adhvan</s>, whose form is the variety of embodiment. There the <s>adhvans</s> of phoneme, mantra, and word abide in the temporal <s>adhvan</s>, because they have supreme, subtle, and gross forms.

children.text: deśādhvasthitis tu tattvapurakalātmanā iti bhaviṣyati svāvasare ||
children.translated_text: But the abiding of the spatial <s>adhvan</s>, consisting of principle, world, and kalā, will be explained in its own place.

children.text: tatra yady api dehe sabāhyābhyantaram otaprotarūpaḥ prāṇaḥ tathāpi prasphuṭasaṃvedyaprayatnaḥ asau hṛdayāt prabhṛti iti tata eva ayaṃ nirūpaṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, although in the body the breath is woven through both the external and the internal, nevertheless it is perceptible with manifest effort beginning from the heart; therefore it is to be explained from there alone.

children.text: tatra prabhuśaktiḥ ātmaśaktiḥ yatna iti tritayaṃ prāṇeraṇe hetuḥ guṇamukhyabhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: There the triad consisting of the Lord's power, the self's power, and effort is the cause in the impelling of the breath, according to whether each is subsidiary or primary.

children.text: tatra hṛdayāt dvādaśāntāntaṃ svāṅgulaiḥ sarvasya ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulaḥ prāṇacāraḥ nirgame praveśe ca svocitabalayatnadehatvāt sarvasya ||
children.translated_text: There, from the heart up to the end of the <s>dvādaśānta</s>, the movement of the breath for everyone is thirty-six finger-breadths by one's own fingers, both in exhalation and inhalation, because for everyone it has its own proper strength, effort, and bodily measure.

children.text: tatra ghaṭikā tithiḥ māso varṣaṃ ca varṣasamūhātmā iti samastaḥ kālaḥ parisamāpyate ||
children.translated_text: There the entire range of time is completed as ghaṭikā, tithi, month, year, and what consists of a group of years.

children.text: tatra sapañcāṃśe aṅgule caṣaka iti sthityā ghaṭikodayaḥ ghaṭikā hi ṣaṣṭyā caṣakaiḥ tasmāt dvāsaptatyaṅgulā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: There, when a caṣaka is established at one finger-breadth plus a fifth part, the arising of a ghaṭikā occurs; for a ghaṭikā consists of sixty caṣakas, and therefore it amounts to seventy-two finger-breadths.

children.text: atha tithyudayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now the arising of a tithi.

children.text: sapādam aṅguladvayaṃ tuṭiḥ ucyate tāsu catasṛṣu praharaḥ tuṭyardhaṃ tuṭyardhaṃ tatra saṃdhyā evaṃ nirgame dinaṃ praveśe rātriḥ iti tithyudayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Two and a quarter finger-breadths are called a tuṭi. Among these, four make a prahara; half a tuṭi and half a tuṭi there are the twilights. Thus in exhalation there is day, and in inhalation night. This is the arising of a tithi.

children.text: atha māsodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now the arising of a month.

children.text: tatra dinaṃ kṛṣṇapakṣaḥ rātriḥ śuklaḥ tatra pūrvaṃ tuṭyardham antyaṃ ca tuṭyardhaṃ viśrāntiḥ akālakalitāḥ madhyās tu pañcadaśa tuṭaya eva tithayaḥ tatra prakāśo viśrāntiś ca iti ete eva dinaniśe ||
children.translated_text: There, day is the dark fortnight and night is the bright one. In that, the first half-tuṭi and the last half-tuṭi are repose, unmeasured by time, while the middle fifteen tuṭis are the tithis. There, luminosity and repose are just these two, day and night.

children.text: tatra vedyamayatāprakāśo dinaṃ vedyasya vicārayitari layo rātriḥ te ca prakāśaviśrāntī cirāciravaicitryāt anantabhede tatsāmye tu viṣuvat ||
children.translated_text: There, the manifestation consisting of knowable objects is day, and the dissolution of the knowable into the one who examines it is night. And these, manifestation and repose, have infinite divisions because of their variety in length and brevity; but when they are equal, there is equinox.

children.text: tatra kṛṣṇapakṣe prāṇārke apānacandra āpyāyikām ekām ekāṃ kalām arpayati yāvat pañcadaśyāṃ tuṭau dvādaśāntasamīpe kṣīṇapṛthagbhūtakalāprasaraḥ candramāḥ prāṇārka eva līyate ||
children.translated_text: There, in the dark fortnight, the apāna-moon offers one nourishing digit after another to the prāṇa-sun, until, on the fifteenth tuṭi, near the <s>dvādaśānta</s>, the moon, whose extension of separate digits has waned, dissolves into the prāṇa-sun itself.

children.text: tadanantaraṃ yat tuṭyardhaṃ sa pakṣasaṃdhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The half-tuṭi immediately after that is the juncture of the fortnights.

children.text: tasya ca tuṭyardhasya prācyam ardham āmāvasyaṃ dvitīyaṃ prātipadam ||
children.translated_text: And of that half-tuṭi, the first half is the new moon, and the second is the first lunar day.

children.text: tatra prātipade tasmin bhāge sa āmāvasyo bhāgo yadā kāsaprayatnāvadhānādikṛtāt tithicchedāt viśati tadā tatra grahaṇam tatra ca vedyarūpasomasahabhūto māyāpramātṛrāhuḥ svabhāvatayā vilāpanāśaktaḥ kevalam ācchādanamātrasamarthaḥ sūryagataṃ cāndram amṛtaṃ pibati iti ||
children.translated_text: There, on that first lunar day, when the new-moon portion enters that part because of a cutting of the tithi produced by attention to the effort of coughing and the like, then an eclipse occurs there. And there <s>Rāhu</s>, the knowing subject formed of <s>māyā</s>, who exists together with the soma whose form is the knowable, is by nature incapable of dissolving it and able only to cover it; he drinks the lunar nectar that has gone into the sun.

children.text: pramātṛpramāṇaprameyatritayāvibhāgakāritvāt sa puṇyaḥ kālaḥ pāralaukikaphalapradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because it produces the non-differentiation of the triad of knower, means of knowledge, and object known, that time is meritorious and bestows a result pertaining to the next world.

children.text: tataḥ praviśati prāṇe cidarka ekaikayā kalayā apānacandram āpūrayati yāvat pañcadaśī tuṭiḥ pūrṇimā tadanantaraṃ pakṣasaṃdhiḥ grahaṇaṃ ca iti prāgvat etat tu aihikaphalapradam iti māsodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the prana enters, the sun of consciousness, by each single <s>kala</s> (digit), fills the moon of apana up to the fifteenth <s>tuti</s>; this is the full moon. Immediately after that come the junction of the fortnight and the eclipse, as before. This, however, bestows results in this world. Thus is the arising of the month.

children.text: atha varṣodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, the arising of the year.

children.text: tatra kṛṣṇapakṣa eva uttarāyaṇaṃ ṣaṭsu ṣaṭsu aṅguleṣu saṃkrāntiḥ makarāt mithunāntam ||
children.translated_text: In that case, the dark fortnight itself is the northern course; at every six aṅgulas there is a transition, from <s>Makara</s> through the end of <s>Mithuna</s>.

children.text: tatra pratyaṅgulaṃ pañca tithayaḥ tatrāpi dinarātrivibhāgaḥ evaṃ praveśe dakṣiṇāyanaṃ garbhatvam udbhavecchā udbubhūṣutā udbhaviṣyatvam udbhavārambhaḥ udbhavattā janmādivikāraṣaṭkaṃ ca iti kramāt makarādiṣu iti ||
children.translated_text: There, for each aṅgula there are five lunar days, and within that there is the division of day and night. In the same way, at entry there is the southern course: becoming an embryo, the desire to arise, the wish to come forth, the state of being about to arise, the beginning of arising, the condition of arising, and the six modifications beginning with birth, in due order among <s>Makara</s> and the following signs.

children.text: tathaiva upāsā atra phalaṃ samucitaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: Worship in just this way here produces the appropriate fruit.

children.text: atra ca dakṣādyāḥ pitāmahāntā rudrāḥ śaktayaś ca dvādaśādhipataya iti varṣodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And here the <s>Rudras</s>, beginning with <s>Dakṣa</s> and ending with the grandfather, together with the powers, are the twelve presiding deities. Thus is the arising of the year.

children.text: pratyaṅgulaṃ ṣaṣṭiḥ tithaya iti krameṇa saṃkrāntau varṣam ity anena krameṇa praveśanirgamayoḥ dvādaśābdodayaḥ pratyaṅgulaṃ tithīnāṃ śatatrayaṃ sapañcāṃśe 'ṅgule varṣaṃ yatra prāk caṣakam uktam iti gaṇanayā saṃkrāntau pañca varṣāṇi iti anayā paripāṭyā ekasmin prāṇanirgamapraveśakāle ṣaṣṭyabdodayaḥ atra ekaviṃśatisahasrāṇi ṣaṭ śatāni iti tithīnāṃ saṃkhyā ||
children.translated_text: There are sixty lunar days for each aṅgula. Thus, by this sequence, at a transition there is a year; and by this order, in the entry and exit of the breath, there is the arising of twelve years. There are three hundred lunar days for each aṅgula, and in an aṅgula together with a fifth there is a year, according to the calculation in which the small measure was stated earlier; thus at a transition there are five years. By this procedure, within a single time of the breath's exit and entry, there is the arising of sixty years. Here the number of lunar days is twenty-one thousand six hundred.

children.text: tāvatī eva ahorātre prāṇasaṃkhyā iti na ṣaṣṭyabdodayāt adhikaṃ parīkṣyate ānantyāt ||
children.translated_text: Just that many is the number of breaths in a day and night; therefore one does not examine beyond the arising of sixty years, because it would be endless.

children.text: tatra mānuṣaṃ varṣaṃ devānāṃ tithiḥ anena krameṇa divyāni dvādaśavarṣasahasrāṇi caturyugam ||
children.translated_text: There, a human year is a lunar day of the gods. By this sequence, twelve thousand divine years are a four-yuga cycle.

children.text: catvāri trīṇi dve ekam iti kṛtāt prabhṛti tāvadbhiḥ śataiḥ aṣṭau saṃdhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Four, three, two, and one: beginning with the <s>Kṛta</s> age, by so many hundreds there are the eight twilights.

children.text: caturyugānām ekasaptatyā manvantaram manvantaraiḥ caturdaśabhiḥ brāhmaṃ dinaṃ brahmadinānte kālāgnidagdhe lokatraye anyatra ca lokatraye dhūmaprasvāpite sarve janā vegavad agnipreritā janaloke pralayākalībhūya tiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: A <s>manvantara</s> consists of seventy-one four-yuga cycles. Fourteen <s>manvantaras</s> make a day of <s>Brahmā</s>. At the end of <s>Brahmā</s>'s day, when the three worlds have been burned by the fire of time and the other three worlds have been enveloped by smoke, all beings, driven by the forceful fire, become as if seized by dissolution and remain in the world of beings.

children.text: prabuddhās tu kūṣmāṇḍahāṭakeśādyā maholoke krīḍanti ||
children.translated_text: But those who are awakened, such as the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍas</s> and <s>Hāṭakeśas</s>, sport in the great world.

children.text: tato niśāsamāptau brāhmī sṛṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, at the end of the night, there is the creation belonging to <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: anena mānena varṣaśataṃ brahmāyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this measure, one hundred years is the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: tat viṣṇoḥ dinaṃ tāvatī ca rātriḥ tasyāpi śatam āyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is a day of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and his night is of the same length; his lifespan too is one hundred such years.

children.text: tat dinaṃ tadūrdhve rudralokaprabho rudrasya tāvatī rātriḥ prāgvat varṣaṃ tacchatam api ca avadhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is the day of <s>Rudra</s>, the lord of the <s>Rudra</s>-world above that, and his night is of the same length; as before, his year and a hundred of those years are also the limit.

children.text: tatra rudrasya tadavasitau śivatvagatiḥ rudrasya uktādhikārāvadhiḥ brahmāṇḍadhārakāṇāṃ tat dinaṃ śatarudrāṇāṃ niśā tāvatī teṣām api ca śatam āyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, when that comes to an end for <s>Rudra</s>, the attainment of <s>Śiva</s>-hood is taught for him. The limit of <s>Rudra</s>'s stated office is the day of the bearers of the cosmic egg, and the night of the hundred <s>Rudras</s> is of the same length; their lifespan too is one hundred such years.

children.text: śatarudrakṣaye brahmāṇḍavināśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the hundred <s>Rudras</s> perish, the cosmic egg is destroyed.

children.text: evaṃ jalatattvāt avyaktāntam etad eva krameṇa rudrāṇām āyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, from the water-tattva up to the unmanifest, this very sequence is the lifespan of the <s>Rudras</s>.

children.text: pūrvasyāyur uttarasya dinam iti ||
children.translated_text: The lifespan of the preceding one is the day of the following one.

children.text: tataś ca brahmā rudrāś ca abādyadhikāriṇaḥ avyakte tiṣṭhanti iti ||
children.translated_text: And so <s>Brahmā</s> and the <s>Rudras</s>, whose offices have not been obstructed, remain in the unmanifest.

children.text: śrīkaṇṭhanāthaś ca tadā saṃhartā ||
children.translated_text: And then <s>Śrīkaṇṭhanātha</s> is the agent of dissolution.

children.text: eṣo 'vāntarapralayaḥ tatkṣaye sṛṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is an intermediate dissolution; when it ends, there is creation.

children.text: tatra śāstrāntaramuktā api sṛjyante ||
children.translated_text: There, even those mentioned in other scriptures are created.

children.text: yat tu śrīkaṇṭhanāthasya svam āyuḥ tat kañcukavāsināṃ rudrāṇāṃ dinaṃ tāvatī rajanī teṣāṃ yad āyuḥ tat gahaneśadinaṃ tāvatī eva kṣapā tasyāṃ ca samastam eva māyāyāṃ vilīyate ||
children.translated_text: But the own lifespan of <s>Śrīkaṇṭhanātha</s> is the day of the <s>Rudras</s> who dwell in the sheaths, and their night is of the same length. Their lifespan is the day of <s>Gahaneśa</s>, and his night is exactly the same length; during that night everything whatsoever is dissolved into <s>Māyā</s>.

children.text: punaḥ gahaneśaḥ sṛjati ||
children.translated_text: Again <s>Gahaneśa</s> creates.

children.text: evaṃ yaḥ avyaktakālaḥ taṃ daśabhiḥ parārdhaiḥ guṇayitvā māyādinaṃ kathayet tāvatī rātriḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, one should multiply the time of the unmanifest by ten <s>parārdhas</s> and call that the day of <s>Māyā</s>; the night is of the same length.

children.text: sa eva pralayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That itself is dissolution.
