children.text: māyākālaḥ parārdhaśatena guṇita aiśvaratattve dinam ||
children.translated_text: The time of <s>Māyā</s>, multiplied by one hundred <s>parārdhas</s>, is a day in the <s>Īśvara</s>-tattva.

children.text: atra prāṇo jagat sṛjati tāvatī rātriḥ yatra prāṇapraśamaḥ prāṇe ca brahmabiladhāmni śānte 'pi yā saṃvit tatrāpy asti kramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the breath creates the universe, and the night is of the same length, when the breath comes to rest. And even when the breath has become still in the abode of the aperture of <s>Brahman</s>, there is still sequence in the consciousness that remains there too.

children.text: aiśvare kāle parārdhaśataguṇite yā saṃkhyā tat sādāśivaṃ dinaṃ tāvatī niśā sa eva mahāpralayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The number that results when the time of <s>Īśvara</s> is multiplied by one hundred <s>parārdhas</s> is the day of <s>Sadāśiva</s>; the night is of the same length. That itself is the great dissolution.

children.text: sadāśivaḥ svakālaparikṣaye bindvardhacandranirodhikā ākramya nāde līyate nādaḥ śaktitattve tat vyāpinyāṃ sā ca anāśrite ||
children.translated_text: When his own time has run out, <s>Sadāśiva</s> passes beyond <s>Bindu</s>, <s>Ardhacandra</s>, and <s>Nirodhikā</s> and dissolves into <s>Nāda</s>; <s>Nāda</s> dissolves into the <s>Śakti</s>-tattva, that into <s>Vyāpinī</s>, and she into <s>Anāśritā</s>.

children.text: śaktikālena parārdhakoṭiguṇitena anāśritadinam ||
children.translated_text: The time of <s>Śakti</s>, multiplied by a crore of <s>parārdhas</s>, is the day of <s>Anāśrita</s>.

children.text: anāśritaḥ sāmanase pade yat tat sāmanasyaṃ sāmyaṃ tat brahma ||
children.translated_text: What belongs to <s>Anāśrita</s> in the state of <s>Sāmanasa</s> is that sameness of mind, that equality; that is <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: asmāt sāmanasyāt akalyāt kālāt nimeṣonmeṣamātratayā proktāśeṣakālaprasarapravilayacakrabhramodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From this equality of mind, from time without kalā, there arises the whirling wheel of expansion and dissolution of all the time previously described, in the mere measure of closing and opening the eyes.

children.text: ekaṃ daśa śataṃ sahasram ayutaṃ lakṣaṃ niyutaṃ koṭiḥ arbudaṃ vṛndaṃ kharvaṃ nikharvaṃ padmaṃ śaṅkuḥ samudram antyaṃ madhyam parārdham iti krameṇa daśaguṇitāni aṣṭādaśa iti gaṇitavidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: One, ten, hundred, thousand, ten thousand, lakh, million, crore, arbuda, vṛnda, kharva, nikharva, padma, śaṅku, samudra, antya, madhya, and parārdha: these eighteen, each multiplied by ten in sequence, are the method of calculation.

children.text: evam asaṃkhyāḥ sṛṣṭipralayāḥ ekasmin mahāsṛṣṭirūpe prāṇe so 'pi saṃvidi sā upādhau sa cinmātre cinmātrasyaiva ayaṃ spando yad ayaṃ kālodayo nāma ||
children.translated_text: Thus there are innumerable creations and dissolutions within a single breath whose form is the great creation; that too is within consciousness, and that consciousness is within a limiting adjunct. It is pure consciousness; and this temporal arising is precisely the vibration of pure consciousness itself.

children.text: tata eva svapnasaṃkalpādau vaicitryam asya na virodhāvaham ||
children.translated_text: Therefore even the diversity in dream, imagination, and so on involves no contradiction for him.

children.text: evaṃ yathā prāṇe kālodayaḥ tathā apāne 'pi hṛdayāt mūlapīṭhaparyantam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, just as the arising of time occurs in <s>prāṇa</s>, so too it occurs in <s>apāna</s>, from the heart down to the root-seat.

children.text: yathā ca hṛtkaṇṭhatālulalāṭarandhradvādaśānteṣu brahmaviṣṇurudreśasadāśivānāśritākhyaṃ kāraṇaṣaṭkam tathaiva apāne 'pi hṛtkandānandasaṃkocavikāsadvādaśānteṣu bālyayauvanavārddhakanidhanapunarbhavamuktyadhipataya ete ||
children.translated_text: And just as, in the heart, throat, palate, forehead-aperture, and twelve-finger limit, there is the sixfold causal series called <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, and <s>Anāśrita</s>, so too in <s>apāna</s>, in the heart, bulb, bliss, contraction, expansion, and twelve-finger limit, these are the presiding lords of childhood, youth, old age, death, rebirth, and liberation.

children.text: atha samāne kālodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, the arising of time in <s>samāna</s>.

children.text: samāno hārdīṣu daśasu nāḍīṣu saṃcaran samaste dehe sāmyena rasādīn vāhayati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Samāna</s>, moving in the ten nāḍīs of the heart, carries rasa and the other constituents evenly through the whole body.

children.text: tatra digaṣṭake saṃcaran taddikpaticeṣṭām iva pramātuḥ anukārayati ||
children.translated_text: There, moving through the eight directions, it makes the knower imitate, as it were, the activity of the lord of that direction.

children.text: ūrdhvādhas tu saṃcaran tisṛṣu nāḍīṣu gatāgataṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: But moving upward and downward, it brings about coming and going in the three nāḍīs.

children.text: tatra viṣuvaddine bāhye prabhātakāle sapādāṃ ghaṭikāṃ madhyamārge vahati ||
children.translated_text: There, on the equinoctial day, at the external time of dawn, it flows for one and a quarter ghaṭikās along the middle path.

children.text: tato navaśatāni prāṇavikṣepāṇām iti gaṇanayā bahiḥ sārdhaghaṭikādvayaṃ vāme dakṣiṇe vāme dakṣiṇe vāme iti pañca saṃkrāntayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, by the calculation that there are nine hundred projections of <s>prāṇa</s>, there are externally two and a half ghaṭikās and five transitions: left, right, left, right, left.

children.text: tataḥ saṃkrāntipañcake vṛtte pādonāsu caturdaśasu ghaṭikāsu atikrāntāsu dakṣiṇaṃ śāradaṃ viṣuvanmadhyāhne nava prāṇaśatāni ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the set of five transitions has occurred, and thirteen and three-quarter ghaṭikās have passed, at midday on the autumnal equinox there are nine hundreds of breaths on the right.

children.text: tato 'pi dakṣiṇe vāme dakṣiṇe vāme dakṣiṇe iti saṃkrāntipañcakaṃ pratyekaṃ navaśatāni ity evaṃ rātrāv api iti ||
children.translated_text: After that too there is a set of five transitions: right, left, right, left, right, each consisting of nine hundreds; and the same holds at night.

children.text: evaṃ viṣuvaddivase tadrātrau ca dvādaśa dvādaśa saṃkrāntayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus on the equinoctial day and on its night there are twelve transitions each.

children.text: tato dinavṛddhikṣayeṣu saṃkrāntivṛddhikṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, with the increase and decrease of the day, there is an increase and decrease of the transitions.

children.text: evam ekasmin samānamaruti varṣadvayaṃ śvāsapraśvāsayogābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: In this way, in a single <s>samāna</s> wind, there are two years, because there is no combination of inhalation and exhalation.

children.text: atrāpi dvādaśābdodayādi pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: Here too the arising of twelve years and the rest is as before.

children.text: udāne tu dvādaśāntāvadhiś cāraḥ spandamātrātmanaḥ kālasya ||
children.translated_text: But in <s>udāna</s>, the movement of time, whose nature is mere vibration, extends up to the twelve-finger limit.

children.text: atrāpi pūrvavat vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here too the rule is as before.

children.text: vyāne tu vyāpakatvāt akrame 'pi sūkṣmocchalattāyogena kālodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But in <s>vyāna</s>, because of its pervasiveness, the arising of time occurs even without sequence, by virtue of a subtle upsurging.

children.text: atha varṇodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, the arising of phonemes.

children.text: tatra ardhaprahare ardhaprahare vargodayo viṣuvati samaḥ varṇasya varṇasya dve śate ṣoḍaśādhike prāṇānām bahiḥ ṣaṭtriṃśat caṣakāṇi iti udayaḥ ayam ayatnajo varṇodayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, at each half-prahara, the arising of a class of phonemes is equal at the equinox; for each phoneme the arising consists of two hundred and sixteen breaths, externally thirty-six caṣakas. This is the effortless arising of phonemes.

children.text: yatnajas tu mantrodayaḥ araghaṭṭaghaṭīyantravāhanavat ekānusaṃdhibalāt citraṃ mantrodayaṃ divāniśam anusaṃdadhat mantradevatayā saha tādātmyam eti ||
children.translated_text: But the effort-produced arising is the arising of mantra. Like the driving of a waterwheel or pot-machine, through the force of a single continuity of attention, one who contemplates the wondrous arising of mantra by day and night reaches identity with the mantra-deity.

children.text: tatra sadodite prāṇacārasaṃkhyayaiva udayasaṃkhyā vyākhyātā taddviguṇite tadardham ityādikrameṇa aṣṭottaraśate cakre dviśata udayaḥ iti krameṇa sthūlasūkṣme cārasvarūpe viśrāntasya prāṇacāre kṣīṇe kālagrāse vṛtte sampūrṇam ekam evedaṃ saṃvedanaṃ citraśaktinirbharaṃ bhāsate ||
children.translated_text: There, in the ever-arisen state, the number of arisings has been explained precisely by the number of movements of <s>prāṇa</s>; when that is doubled, the half of that, and so on, in the sequence of the wheel of one hundred and eight and of two hundred arisings. Thus, when one has come to rest in the gross and subtle forms of movement, when the movement of <s>prāṇa</s> has been exhausted and the devouring of time has occurred, this whole thing shines forth as one complete awareness, filled with manifold power.

children.text: kālabheda eva saṃvedanabhedakaḥ na vedyabhedaḥ śikharasthajñānavat jñānasya yāvān avasthitikālaḥ sa eva kṣaṇaḥ prāṇodaye ca ekasmin ekam eva jñānam avaśyaṃ caitat anyathā vikalpajñānam ekaṃ na kiṃcit syāt kramikaśabdārūṣitatvāt mātrāyā api kramikatvāt ||
children.translated_text: It is the distinction of time alone that differentiates awareness, not a distinction in the object known, as in knowledge situated at a summit. However long knowledge remains, that itself is the moment. And in a single arising of <s>prāṇa</s> there is necessarily only one cognition; this must be so, for otherwise there would be no such thing as a single conceptual cognition, since it would be tinted by sequential words and since even a mora is sequential.

children.text: yad āha tasyādita udāttam ardhahrasvam iti ||
children.translated_text: As has been said: 'From its beginning, the acute accent is half-short.'

children.text: tasmāt spandāntaraṃ yāvat na uditaṃ tāvat ekam eva jñānam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, until another vibration has arisen, there is only one cognition.

children.text: ata eva ekāśītipadasmaraṇasamaye vividhadharmānupraveśamukhena eka eva asau parameśvaraviṣayo vikalpaḥ kālagrāse na avikalpātmā eva sampadyate iti ||
children.translated_text: For this very reason, at the time of remembering eighty-one words, through the mode of the entrance of various properties, that single conceptual cognition whose object is <s>Parameśvara</s>, when time is devoured, does not become anything other than non-conceptual in nature.

children.text: evam akhilaṃ kālādhvānaṃ prāṇodaya eva paśyan sṛṣṭisaṃhārāṃś ca vicitrān niḥsaṃkhyān tatraiva ākalayan ātmana eva pāramaiśvaryaṃ pratyabhijānan mukta eva bhavati iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, seeing the whole path of time in the very arising of <s>prāṇa</s>, and reckoning there creations and dissolutions that are varied and innumerable, one recognizes the supreme lordship of one's own self and is already liberated.

children.text: saṃvidrūpasyātmanaḥ prāṇaśaktiṃ paśyan rūpaṃ tatragaṃ cātikālam
children.translated_text: Seeing the power of <s>prāṇa</s> belonging to the self whose form is consciousness, and the form situated there beyond time,

children.text: sākaṃ sṛṣṭisthemasaṃhāracakrair nityodyukto bhairavībhāvam eti ||
children.translated_text: together with the cycles of creation, maintenance, and dissolution, always intent, one attains the state of <s>Bhairavī</s>.

children.text: Chapter 7

tatra samasta eva ayaṃ mūrtivaicitryābhāsanaśaktijo deśādhvā saṃvidi viśrāntaḥ taddvāreṇa śūnye buddhau prāṇe nāḍīcakrānucakreṣu bahiḥ śarīre yāvalliṅgasthaṇḍilapratimādau samasto 'dhvā pariniṣṭhitaḥ taṃ samastam adhvānaṃ dehe vilāpya dehaṃ ca prāṇe taṃ dhiyi tāṃ śūnye tatsaṃvedane nirbharaparipūrṇasaṃvit sampadyate ṣaṭtriṃśattattvasvarūpajñaḥ taduttīrṇāṃ saṃvidaṃ paramaśivarūpāṃ paśyan viśvamayīm api saṃvedayeta aparathā vedyabhāgam eva kaṃcit paratvena gṛhṇīyān māyāgarbhādhikāriṇaṃ viṣṇubrahmādikaṃ vā tasmād avaśyaṃ prakriyājñānapareṇa bhavitavyam ||
children.translated_text: There, this entire spatial adhvan, born from the power that makes the diversity of forms appear, rests in consciousness. Through that, in emptiness, in the intellect, in <s>prāṇa</s>, in the wheels and sub-wheels of the nāḍīs, and externally in the body as far as the liṅga, altar-ground, image, and so on, the whole adhvan is fully established. Having dissolved that entire adhvan into the body, the body into <s>prāṇa</s>, that into the intellect, that into emptiness, and that into its awareness, one becomes consciousness, densely and completely full. Knowing the nature of the thirty-six tattvas and seeing the consciousness beyond them, whose form is <s>Paramaśiva</s>, one should experience it also as all-formed. Otherwise one would apprehend as supreme only some portion of the knowable, or some authority within <s>māyā</s>, such as <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the like. Therefore one must necessarily be devoted to knowledge of the process.

children.text: tad uktaṃ na prakriyāparaṃ jñānam iti ||
children.translated_text: That is why it has been said: 'Knowledge is not concerned with the process.'

children.text: tatra pṛthivītattvaṃ śatakoṭipravistīrṇaṃ brahmāṇḍagolakarūpam ||
children.translated_text: There, the earth-tattva has the form of the sphere of the brahmāṇḍa, extending over a hundred crores.

children.text: tasya antaḥ kālāgnir narakāḥ pātālāni pṛthivī svargo yāvad brahmaloka iti ||
children.translated_text: Within it are the fire of time, the hells, the nether worlds, the earth, heaven, up to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: brahmāṇḍabāhye rudrāṇāṃ śatam ||
children.translated_text: Outside the cosmic egg there are a hundred <s>Rudras</s>.

children.text: na ca brahmāṇḍānāṃ saṃkhyā vidyate ||
children.translated_text: And there is no number of the cosmic eggs.

children.text: tato dharātattvād daśaguṇaṃ jalatattvam ||
children.translated_text: Beyond that earth-tattva, the water-tattva is ten times greater.

children.text: tata uttarottaraṃ daśaguṇam ahaṃkārāntam ||
children.translated_text: Then each successive one, up to <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), is ten times greater.

children.text: tad yathā jalaṃ tejo vāyur nabhaḥ tanmātrapañcakākṣaikādaśagarbho 'haṃkāraś ceti ||
children.translated_text: That is: water, fire, wind, ether, and <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, containing the five subtle elements and the eleven faculties.

children.text: ahaṃkārāt śataguṇaṃ buddhitattvam ||
children.translated_text: The intellect-tattva is a hundred times greater than <s>ahaṃkāra</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sahasradhā prakṛtitattvam etāvat prakṛtyaṇḍam ||
children.translated_text: After that, the prakṛti-tattva is a thousandfold; this much is the prakṛti-egg.

children.text: tac ca brahmāṇḍavad asaṃkhyam ||
children.translated_text: And that too is innumerable, like the brahmāṇḍa.

children.text: prakṛtitattvāt puruṣatattvaṃ ca daśasahasradhā ||
children.translated_text: The puruṣa-tattva is ten thousand times greater than the prakṛti-tattva.

children.text: puruṣān niyatiḥ lakṣadhā ||
children.translated_text: Niyati is a hundred thousand times greater than <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: niyater uttarottaraṃ daśalakṣadhā kalātattvāntam ||
children.translated_text: From niyati onward, each successive one up to the kalā-tattva is ten lakhs greater.

children.text: tad yathā niyatiḥ rāgo 'śuddhavidyā kālaḥ kalā ceti ||
children.translated_text: That is: niyati, rāga, impure knowledge, time, and kalā.

children.text: kalātattvāt koṭidhā māyā etāvat māyāṇḍam ||
children.translated_text: The māyā-tattva is a crore times greater than the kalā-tattva; this much is the māyā-egg.

children.text: māyātattvāt śuddhavidyā daśakoṭiguṇitā ||
children.translated_text: Pure knowledge is ten crore times greater than the māyā-tattva.

children.text: vidyātattvād īśvaratattvaṃ śatakoṭidhā ||
children.translated_text: The īśvara-tattva is a hundred crore times greater than the vidyā-tattva.

children.text: īśvaratattvāt sādākhyaṃ sahasrakoṭidhā ||
children.translated_text: The sādākhya-tattva is a thousand crore times greater than the īśvara-tattva.

children.text: sādākhyāt vṛndaguṇitaṃ śaktitattvam iti śaktyaṇḍam ||
children.translated_text: The śakti-tattva is multiplied by a vṛnda from <s>Sādākhya</s>; this is the śakti-egg.

children.text: sā śaktir vyāpya yato viśvam adhvānam antarbahir āste tasmād vyāpinī ||
children.translated_text: Since that <s>Śakti</s> pervades the whole cosmic path, both within and without, and abides there, she is called <s>Vyāpinī</s> (the Pervasive One).

children.text: evam etāni uttarottaram āvaraṇatayā vartamānāni tattvāny uttaraṃ vyāpakaṃ pūrvaṃ vyāpyam iti sthityā vartante ||
children.translated_text: Thus these tattvas, existing successively as coverings one beyond another, stand in the relation that the later is the pervader and the earlier is the pervaded.

children.text: yāvad aśeṣaśaktitattvānto 'dhvā śivatattvena vyāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The whole adhvan, ending with the entire śakti-tattva, is pervaded by the śiva-tattva.

children.text: śivatattvaṃ punar aparimeyaṃ sarvādhvottīrṇaṃ sarvādhvavyāpakaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: But the śiva-tattva is immeasurable, beyond all adhvans and also pervasive of all adhvans.

children.text: etattattvāntarālavartīni yāni bhuvanāni tatpataya eva atra pṛthivyāṃ sthitā iti ||
children.translated_text: The worlds that exist in the intervals between these tattvas, and their lords, are situated here on earth.

children.text: teṣv āyataneṣu ye mriyante teṣāṃ tatra tatra gatiṃ te vitaranti ||
children.translated_text: Those lords bestow, in each of those abodes, the corresponding destination on those who die there.

children.text: kramācca ūrdhvordhvaṃ prerayanti dīkṣākrameṇa ||
children.translated_text: And, in sequence, they impel them higher and higher through the order of initiation.

children.text: Chapter 8
yad idaṃ vibhavātmakaṃ bhuvanajātam uktaṃ garbhīkṛtānantavicitrabhoktṛbhogyaṃ tatra yad anugataṃ mahāprakāśarūpaṃ tat mahāsāmānyakalpaṃ paramaśivarūpam ||
children.translated_text: Within the manifold class of worlds just described as constituted by manifestation, enclosing endlessly varied enjoyers and objects of enjoyment, that which runs through it as the form of great illumination, resembling a great universal, is the form of <s>Paramaśiva</s>.

children.text: yat tu katipayakatipayabhedānugataṃ rūpaṃ tat tattvaṃ yathā pṛthivī nāma dyutikāṭhinyasthaulyādirūpā kālāgniprabhṛtivīrabhadrāntabhuvaneśādhiṣṭhitasamastabrahmāṇḍānugatā ||
children.translated_text: But the form that runs through only certain particular differentiations is a tattva; for example, what is called earth, whose form is brightness, hardness, grossness, and the like, runs through all the cosmic eggs presided over by the lords of worlds from <s>Kālāgni</s> up to <s>Vīrabhadra</s>.

children.text: tatra eṣāṃ tattvānāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvo darśyate sa ca dvividhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the relation of effect and cause among these tattvas is shown, and it is twofold.

children.text: pāramārthikaḥ sṛṣṭeś ca ||
children.translated_text: It is ultimate, and it belongs to creation.

children.text: tatra pāramārthika etāvān kāryakāraṇabhāvo yad uta kartṛsvabhāvasya svatantrasya bhagavata evaṃvidhena śivādidharāntena vapuṣā svarūpabhinnena svarūpaviśrāntena ca prathanam ||
children.translated_text: There, the ultimate relation of effect and cause is only this: the manifestation of the independent Lord, whose nature is agency, in such a body extending from <s>Śiva</s> down to earth, a body both non-different from his own nature and resting in his own nature.

children.text: kalpitas tu kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ parameśecchayā niyatiprāṇayā nirmitaḥ sa ca yāvati yadā niyatapaurvāparyāvabhāsanaṃ saty api adhike svarūpānugatam etāvaty eva tena yogīcchāto 'pi aṅkuro bījād api svapnādau ghaṭāder apīti ||
children.translated_text: But the constructed relation of effect and cause is fashioned by the will of <s>Parameśvara</s>, whose life-breath is niyati. It is this: although there may be more that follows its own nature, whenever a fixed prior-and-posterior appearance occurs to a certain extent, it is just that much; therefore, even from a yogin's will there may be a sprout, and also from a seed, and in dream and the like there may be a pot and so on.

children.text: tatrāpi ca parameśvarasya kartṛtvānapāya iti akalpito 'pi asau pāramārthikaḥ sthita eva ||
children.translated_text: Yet even there <s>Parameśvara</s>'s agency does not lapse; so that agency, though not constructed, remains established as ultimate.

children.text: pāramārthike hi bhittisthānīye sthite rūpe sarvam idam ullikhyamānaṃ ghaṭate na anyathā ata eva sāmagryā eva kāraṇatvaṃ yuktam ||
children.translated_text: For when the ultimate form, which is like the surface of a wall, stands firm, all this that is being drawn upon it can occur, and not otherwise; hence it is reasonable that the total complex alone has causal status.

children.text: sā hi samastabhāvasaṃdarbhamayī svatantrasaṃvedanamahimnā tathā niyatanijanijadeśakālabhāvarāśisvabhāvā pratyekaṃ vastusvarūpaniṣpattisamaye tathābhūtā tathābhūtāyā hi anyathābhāvo yathā yathā adhikībhavati tathā tathā kāryasyāpi vijātīyatvaṃ tāratamyena puṣyati ||
children.translated_text: For that complex consists in the whole arrangement of entities. Through the greatness of autonomous consciousness, its nature is the fixed mass of each entity's own place, time, and condition; at the moment when each thing's own nature is produced, it is such and such. As difference from such a state increases in whatever way, so too the heterogeneity of the effect grows by degrees.

children.text: ity evaṃ saṃvedanasvātantryasvabhāvaḥ parameśvara eva viśvabhāvaśarīro ghaṭāder nirmātā kumbhakārasaṃvidas tato 'nadhikatvāt kumbhakāraśarīrasya ca bhāvarāśimadhye nikṣepāt kathaṃ kumbhakāraśarīrasya kartṛtvābhimānaḥ iti cet parameśvarakṛta evāsau ghaṭādivat bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Parameśvara</s> alone, whose nature is the autonomy of consciousness and whose body is the whole universe, is the maker of a pot and the like. If one asks, 'Since the potter's consciousness is no more than that, and since the potter's body is included within the mass of entities, how can there be an assumption that the potter's body is the agent?', that assumption too will be made by <s>Parameśvara</s>, just like the pot and so on.

children.text: tasmāt sāmagrīvādo 'pi viśvaśarīrasya saṃvedanasyaiva kartṛtāyām upodbalakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore even the doctrine of the total complex supports the agency of consciousness itself, whose body is the universe.

children.text: merau hi tatrasthe na bhavet tathāvidho ghaṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For if <s>Meru</s> were present there, such a pot would not come into being.

children.text: evaṃ kalpite 'smin kāryatve śāstreṣu tattvānāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvaṃ prati yat bahuprakāratvaṃ tad api saṃgataṃ gomayāt kīṭāt yogīcchāto mantrād auṣadhāt vṛścikodayavat ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when this effectedness is constructed, the many forms taught in the scriptures regarding the causal relation of the tattvas are also coherent, just as the arising of scorpions from cow dung, from insects, from a yogin's will, from mantra, or from medicine is coherent.

children.text: tatra nijatantradṛśā taṃ kalpitaṃ darśayāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, from the viewpoint of our own tantra, we shall show that constructed relation.

children.text: tatra parameśvaraḥ pañcabhiḥ śaktibhiḥ nirbhara ity uktam sa svātantryāt śaktiṃ tāṃ tāṃ mukhyatayā prakaṭayan pañcadhā tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: There <s>Parameśvara</s> has been said to be full of five powers. By his autonomy, making each particular power manifest as primary, he abides in five ways.

children.text: citprādhānye śivatattvam ānandaprādhānye śaktitattvam icchāprādhānye sadāśivatattvam icchāyā hi jñānakriyayoḥ sāmyarūpābhyupagamātmakatvāt jñānaśaktiprādhānye īśvaratattvam kriyāśaktiprādhānye vidyātattvam iti ||
children.translated_text: When consciousness is predominant, there is the <s>Śiva</s>-tattva; when bliss is predominant, the <s>Śakti</s>-tattva; when will is predominant, the <s>Sadāśiva</s>-tattva, because will has the nature of accepting knowledge and action in equality. When the power of knowledge is predominant, there is the <s>Īśvara</s>-tattva; when the power of action is predominant, the <s>Vidyā</s>-tattva.

children.text: atra ca tattveśvarāḥ śivaśaktisadāśiveśvarānantāḥ brahmeva nivṛttau eṣāṃ sāmānyarūpāṇāṃ viśeṣā anugativiṣayāḥ pañca tadyathā śāmbhavāḥ śāktāḥ mantramaheśvarāḥ mantreśvarāḥ mantrā iti śuddhādhvā ||
children.translated_text: And here the lords of the tattvas are <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and <s>Ananta</s>. Just as <s>Brahmā</s> presides over <s>Nivṛtti</s>, the particular forms of these general forms, as objects of progressive inclusion, are five: the <s>Śāmbhavas</s>, the <s>Śāktas</s>, the <s>Mantramaheśvaras</s>, the <s>Mantreśvaras</s>, and the <s>Mantras</s>. This is the pure adhvan.

children.text: iyati sākṣāt śivaḥ kartā aśuddhaṃ punar adhvānam anantāparanāmāghoreśaḥ sṛjati īśvarecchāvaśena prakṣubdhabhogalolikānām aṇūnāṃ bhogasiddhyartham ||
children.translated_text: In this extent, <s>Śiva</s> is directly the agent. But the impure adhvan is created by <s>Aghoreśa</s>, also called <s>Ananta</s>, under the force of <s>Īśvara</s>'s will, for the accomplishment of experience for the aṇus who are stirred and eager for enjoyment.

children.text: tatra loliko 'pūrṇaṃmanyatārūpaḥ parispandaḥ akarmakam abhilāṣamātram eva bhaviṣyadavacchedayogyateti na malaḥ puṃsas tattvāntaram ||
children.translated_text: There, eagerness is a vibration whose form is the sense of being incomplete; it is not mala, nor another tattva of the self, but only desire without an object, the capacity for future limitation.

children.text: rāgatattvaṃ tu karmāvacchinno 'bhilāṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The rāga-tattva, however, is desire limited by karma.

children.text: karma tu tatra karmamātraṃ buddhidharmas tu rāgaḥ karmabhedacitra iti vibhāgo vakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: There karma is simply karma, while rāga is a property of the intellect, variegated by the differences of karma. This distinction will be explained.

children.text: so 'yaṃ malaḥ parameśvarasya svātmapracchādanecchātaḥ nānyat kiṃcit vastv api ca tatparameśvarecchātmanaiva dharāder api vastutvāt ||
children.translated_text: This mala arises from <s>Parameśvara</s>'s will to conceal his own self; it is not anything else. Moreover, even earth and the rest have reality only through having the nature of that will of <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: sa ca malo vijñānakevale vidyamāno dhvaṃsonmukha iti na svakāryaṃ karma āpyāyati ||
children.translated_text: And when that mala is present in the <s>vijñānakevala</s>, it is on the verge of destruction, and therefore it does not nourish karma, its own effect.

children.text: pralayakevalasya tu jṛmbhamāṇa eva āsta iti malopodbalitaṃ karma saṃsāravaicitryabhoge nimittam iti tadbhogavāsanānuviddhānām aṇūnāṃ bhogasiddhaye śrīmān aghoreśaḥ sṛjati iti yuktam uktaṃ malasya ca prakṣobha īśvarecchābalād eva jaḍasya svataḥ kutracid api asāmarthyāt ||
children.translated_text: But in the <s>pralayakevala</s> it remains in an expanding state; therefore karma, strengthened by mala, is the cause of the varied experiences of saṃsāra. Thus it has rightly been said that blessed <s>Aghoreśa</s> creates for the accomplishment of experience for the aṇus permeated by the residual impressions of that experience. And the stirring of mala too occurs only through the force of <s>Īśvara</s>'s will, since what is inert has no capacity anywhere by itself.

children.text: aṇur nāma kila cidacidrūpāvabhāsa eva tasya cidrūpam aiśvaryam eva acidrūpataiva malaḥ tasya ca sṛjataḥ parameśvarecchāmayaṃ tata eva ca nityaṃ srakṣyamāṇavastugatasya rūpasya jaḍatayābhāsayiṣyamāṇatvāt jaḍaṃ sakalakāryavyāpanādirūpatvācca vyāpakaṃ māyākhyaṃ tattvam upādānakāraṇaṃ tadavabhāsakāriṇī ca parameśvarasya māyā nāma śaktis tato 'nyaiva ||
children.translated_text: The aṇu, indeed, is an appearance whose form is both conscious and non-conscious. Its conscious form is lordship itself; its non-conscious form alone is mala. And when he creates, the material cause is the tattva called <s>Māyā</s>, made of <s>Parameśvara</s>'s will, and for that very reason eternal, inert because the form belonging to the object about to be created will appear as inert, and pervasive because it has the nature of pervading all effects and so on. The power of <s>Parameśvara</s> that causes that to appear is called <s>Māyā</s>, and is distinct from it.

children.text: evaṃ kalāditattvānāṃ dharāntānām api dvairūpyaṃ nirūpyam ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, the twofold form of the tattvas beginning with <s>Kalā</s> and ending with earth is also to be explained.

children.text: atra ca dvairūpye pramāṇam api āhur abhinavaguptaguravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And regarding this twofold form, the teachers of <s>Abhinavagupta</s> also state a proof.

children.text: yat saṃkalpe bhāti tat pṛthagbhūtaṃ bahir api asti sphuṭena vapuṣā ghaṭa iva ||
children.translated_text: Whatever shines forth in conceptual intention exists outside as a separate thing too, with a clear body, like a pot.

children.text: tathā ca māyākalādikhapuṣpāder api eṣaiva vartanī iti kevalānvayī hetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: And thus this same path applies even to <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Kalā</s>, and the like, as also to a sky-flower and so on; this is a reason with purely positive concomitance.

children.text: anena ca māyākalāprakṛtibuddhyādiviṣayaṃ sākṣātkārarūpaṃ jñānaṃ ye bhajante te 'pi siddhāḥ siddhā eva ||
children.translated_text: By this, even those who partake of knowledge in the form of direct realization whose objects are <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Kalā</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Buddhi</s>, and the like are indeed siddhas.

children.text: evaṃ sthite māyātattvāt viśvaprasavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When this is established, the production of the universe comes from the <s>Māyā</s>-tattva.

children.text: sa ca yady api akramam eva tathāpi uktadṛśā kramo 'vabhāsate iti ||
children.translated_text: And although that production is in fact without sequence, nevertheless, from the point of view just stated, sequence appears.

children.text: so 'pi ucyate tatra pratyātma kalādivargo bhinnaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That too is now stated: there, the group beginning with <s>Kalā</s> is different for each individual self.

children.text: tatkāryasya kartṛtvopodbalanādeḥ pratyātmabhedena upalambhāt sa tu vargaḥ kadācit ekībhavet api īśvarecchayā sāmājikātmanām iva tatra sarvo 'yaṃ kalādivargaḥ śuddhaḥ yaḥ parameśvaraviṣayatayā tatsvarūpalābhānuguṇanijakāryakārī saṃsārapratidvaṃdvitvāt ||
children.translated_text: For the strengthening of agency and other effects belonging to that group are observed as differing for each self. Yet that group may at times become unified by <s>Īśvara</s>'s will, as in the case of social persons. There, this entire group beginning with <s>Kalā</s> is pure when, because it has <s>Parameśvara</s> as its object, it performs its own function in a way favorable to attaining his nature, since it is opposed to saṃsāra.

children.text: sa ca parameśvaraśaktipātavaśāt tathā bhavati iti vakṣyāmas tatprakāśane ||
children.translated_text: And it becomes so through the descent of <s>Parameśvara</s>'s power, as we shall explain when that is set forth.

children.text: aśuddhas tu tadviparītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the impure is the opposite of that.

children.text: tatra māyātaḥ kalā jātā yā suptasthānīyam aṇuṃ kiṃcitkartṛtvena yunakti sā ca ucchūnateva saṃsārabījasya māyāṇvor ubhayoḥ saṃyogāt utpannāpi māyāṃ vikaroti na avikāryam aṇum iti māyākāryatvam asyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, from <s>Māyā</s> arose <s>Kalā</s>, which joins the aṇu, comparable to one asleep, with limited agency. Although it is produced from the conjunction of both <s>Māyā</s> and the aṇu, as though by the swelling of the seed of saṃsāra, it modifies <s>Māyā</s>, not the unmodifiable aṇu; therefore it is an effect of <s>Māyā</s>.

children.text: evam anyonyaśleṣāt alakṣaṇīyāntaratvaṃ puṃskalayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, because of their mutual adhesion, the difference between the self and <s>Kalā</s> is not perceptible.

children.text: māyāgarbhādhikāriṇas tu kasyacid īśvarasya prasādāt sarvakarmakṣaye māyāpuruṣaviveko bhavati yena māyordhve vijñānākala āste na jātucit māyādhaḥ kalāpuṃviveko vā yena kalordhve tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: But for one who has authority within the womb of <s>Māyā</s>, through the grace of some <s>Īśvara</s> and when all karma has been exhausted, there arises discrimination between <s>Māyā</s> and the person; by that he remains as a <s>vijñānākala</s> above <s>Māyā</s>, never below <s>Māyā</s>. Or there is discrimination between <s>Kalā</s> and the self, by which he stands above <s>Kalā</s>.

children.text: prakṛtipuruṣaviveko vā yena pradhānādho na saṃsaret ||
children.translated_text: Or there is discrimination between <s>Prakṛti</s> and the person, by which he does not transmigrate below <s>Pradhāna</s>.

children.text: malapuruṣaviveke tu śivasamānatvam ||
children.translated_text: But when there is discrimination between mala and the person, there is equality with <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: puruṣapūrṇatādṛṣṭau tu śivatvam eveti ||
children.translated_text: And when the fullness of the person is seen, there is simply <s>Śiva</s>-hood.

children.text: evaṃ kalātattvam eva kiṃcitkartṛtvadāyi na ca ||
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Kalā</s>-tattva is indeed what grants limited agency, and nothing else.

children.text: kartṛtvam ajñasya iti ||
children.translated_text: For agency belongs to one who is ignorant.

children.text: kiṃcijjñatvadāyiny aśuddhavidyā kalāto jātā sā ca vidyā buddhiṃ paśyati tadgatāṃś ca sukhādīn vivekena gṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aśuddhavidyā</s>, which grants limited knowledge, arises from <s>Kalā</s>. That vidyā sees the intellect and, by discrimination, grasps pleasure and the other things present in it.

children.text: buddher guṇasaṃkīrṇākārāyā vivekena grahītum asāmarthyāt ||
children.translated_text: For the intellect, whose form is mixed with the guṇas, is incapable of grasping them by discrimination.

children.text: tasmāt buddhipratibimbito bhāvo vidyayā vivicyate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the state reflected in the intellect is discriminated by <s>Vidyā</s>.

children.text: kiṃcitkartṛtvaṃ kiṃcidbhāgasiddhaye kvacid eva kartṛtvam ity atra arthe paryavasyati kvacid eva ca ity atra bhāge rāgatattvasya vyāpāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning comes down to this: finite agency is agency only in some respect, for the accomplishment of some limited share. And in the expression "only in some respect," the operation of the <s>rāga</s>-tattva is present in the element of partiality.

children.text: na ca avairāgyakṛtaṃ tat avairāgyasyāpi araktidarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: And that is not produced by non-detachment, because even in non-detachment one sees an absence of attachment.

children.text: vairāgye dharmādāv api raktir dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Even when there is detachment, attachment toward <s>dharma</s> and so on is seen.

children.text: tṛptasya ca annādau avairāgyābhāve 'pi antaḥstharāgānapāyāt ||
children.translated_text: And in one who is satisfied with food and the like, even when there is no non-detachment, inward attachment has not disappeared.

children.text: tena vinā punar avairāgyānutpattiprasaṅgāt ||
children.translated_text: For without that, there would follow the unwanted consequence that non-detachment could not arise again.

children.text: kālaś ca kāryaṃ kalayaṃs tadavacchinnaṃ kartṛtvam api kalayati tulye kvacittve asminn eva kartṛtvam ity atrārthe niyater vyāpāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: And <s>kāla</s> (time), while measuring out the effect, also measures out agency delimited by that effect. Since this "in some respect" is the same, in the meaning "agency is only in this," there is the operation of <s>niyati</s> (necessitation).

children.text: kāryakāraṇabhāve 'pi asyā eva vyāpāraḥ tena kalāta eva etac catuṣkaṃ jātam idam eva kiṃcid adhunā jānan abhiṣvaktaḥ karomi ity evaṃrūpā saṃvid dehapuryaṣṭakādigatā paśur ity ucyate ||
children.translated_text: In the relation of cause and effect too, the operation belongs to this same <s>niyati</s>. Therefore, from <s>kalā</s> alone this group of four has arisen. The awareness whose form is, "Knowing just this, now, and being attached, I act," when situated in the body, the eightfold subtle body, and so on, is called the bound soul, the <s>paśu</s>.

children.text: tad idaṃ māyādiṣaṭkaṃ kañcukaṣaṭkam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: This sixfold group beginning with <s>māyā</s> is called the sixfold sheath, the <s>kañcuka</s>.

children.text: saṃvido māyayā apahastitatvena kalādīnām uparipātināṃ kañcukavat avasthānāt ||
children.translated_text: For consciousness has been thrust aside by <s>māyā</s>, and <s>kalā</s> and the others that descend upon it stand over it like a sheath.

children.text: evaṃ kiṃcitkartṛtvaṃ yat māyākāryaṃ tatra kiṃcit tv aviśiṣṭaṃ yat kartṛtvaṃ viśeṣyaṃ tatra vyāpriyamāṇā kalā vidyādiprasavahetuḥ iti nirūpitam ||
children.translated_text: Thus it has been explained that finite agency, which is the product of <s>māyā</s>, has <s>kalā</s> operating in it, in the agency that is the qualified subject, while the element "something" is not yet specified; and <s>kalā</s> is the cause for the production of <s>vidyā</s> and the rest.

children.text: idānīṃ viśeṣaṇabhāgo yaḥ kiṃcid ity ukto jñeyaḥ kāryaś ca taṃ yāvat sā kalā svātmanaḥ pṛthak kurute tāvat eṣa eva sukhaduḥkhamohātmakabhogyaviśeṣānusyūtasya sāmānyamātrasya tadguṇasāmyāparanāmnaḥ prakṛtitattvasya sargaḥ iti bhoktṛbhogyayugalasya samam eva kalātattvāyattā sṛṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, insofar as that <s>kalā</s> separates from itself the qualifying portion called "something," which is to be known and is an effect, to that same extent there is the creation of the <s>prakṛti</s>-tattva, whose other name is the equilibrium of those guṇas, and which is only the general form threaded through specific enjoyables consisting of pleasure, pain, and delusion. Thus the pair of experiencer and experienced is created simultaneously, dependent on the <s>kalā</s>-tattva.

children.text: atra caiṣāṃ vāstavena pathā kramavandhyaiva sṛṣṭir ity uktaṃ kramāvabhāso 'pi cāstīty api uktam eva ||
children.translated_text: And here it has been said that, by the real path, the creation of these is barren of sequence; and it has also indeed been said that there is an appearance of sequence.

children.text: kramaś ca vidyārāgādīnāṃ vicitro 'pi dṛṣṭaḥ kaścid rajyan vetti ko 'pi vidan rajyate ityādi ||
children.translated_text: And sequence, though varied, is also seen among <s>vidyā</s>, <s>rāga</s>, and the others: one person becomes attached and then knows; another, knowing, becomes attached, and so on.

children.text: tena bhinnakramanirūpaṇam api rauravādiṣu śāstreṣu aviruddhaṃ mantavyaṃ tad eva tu bhogyasāmānyaṃ prakṣobhagataṃ guṇatattvam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore different accounts of sequence in scriptures such as the <s>Raurava</s> should also be understood as not contradictory. But that same general object of experience, when agitated, is the <s>guṇa</s>-tattva.

children.text: yatra sukhaṃ bhogyarūpaprakāśaḥ sattvam duḥkhaṃ prakāśāprakāśāndolanātmakam ata eva kriyārūpaṃ rajaḥ mohaḥ prakāśābhāvarūpas tamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, pleasure, the manifestation of the object of experience, is <s>sattva</s>; pain, whose nature is an oscillation between manifestation and non-manifestation, and therefore whose form is activity, is <s>rajas</s>; delusion, whose form is the absence of manifestation, is <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: tritayam api etat bhogyarūpam ||
children.translated_text: All three of these have the form of the object of experience.

children.text: evaṃ kṣubdhāt pradhānāt kartavyāntarodayaḥ na akṣubdhād iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus a further effect to be made arises from agitated <s>pradhāna</s>, not from unagitated <s>pradhāna</s>.

children.text: kṣobhaḥ avaśyam eva antarāle abhyupagantavya iti siddhaṃ sāṃkhyāparidṛṣṭaṃ pṛthagbhūtaṃ guṇatattvam ||
children.translated_text: Since agitation must necessarily be admitted in between, a distinct <s>guṇa</s>-tattva, as envisaged by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, is established.

children.text: sa ca kṣobhaḥ prakṛtes tattveśādhiṣṭhānād eva anyathā niyataṃ puruṣaṃ prati iti na sidhyet ||
children.translated_text: And that agitation occurs only because <s>prakṛti</s> is presided over by the lord of the tattva; otherwise, it would not be established as directed toward a particular <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: tato guṇatattvāt buddhitattvaṃ yatra puṃprakāśo viṣayaś ca pratibimbam arpayataḥ ||
children.translated_text: From that <s>guṇa</s>-tattva comes the <s>buddhi</s>-tattva, in which the light of <s>puruṣa</s> and the object both cast a reflection.

children.text: buddhitattvāt ahaṃkāro yena buddhipratibimbite vedyasamparke kaluṣe puṃprakāśe anātmani ātmābhimānaḥ śuktau rajatābhimānavat ||
children.translated_text: From the <s>buddhi</s>-tattva comes <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, by which, when contact with the knowable reflected in the intellect makes the light of <s>puruṣa</s> turbid, the notion of self arises in what is not the self, just like the notion of silver in mother-of-pearl.

children.text: ata eva kāra ity anena kṛtakatvam asya uktaṃ sāṃkhyasya tu tat na yujyate sa hi na ātmano 'haṃvimarśamayatām icchati vayaṃ tu kartṛtvam api tasya icchāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Precisely by the word <s>kāra</s> in <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, its made or fabricated character is stated. For the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> view, however, this is not appropriate, since it does not accept that the self has the nature of reflective "I"-awareness. We, on the other hand, also accept agency for it.

children.text: tac ca śuddhaṃ vimarśa eva apratiyogi svātmacamatkārarūpo 'ham iti ||
children.translated_text: And that agency, in its purity, is nothing but reflective awareness, without an opposed counterpart, whose form is the savoring wonder of the self: "I."

children.text: eṣo 'sya ahaṃkārasya karaṇaskandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the instrumental aggregate of this <s>ahaṃkāra</s>.

children.text: prakṛtiskandhas tu tasyaiva trividhaḥ sattvādibhedāt ||
children.translated_text: Its aggregate of prakṛti, however, is threefold, according to the division into <s>sattva</s> and the others.

children.text: tatra sāttviko yasmāt manaś ca buddhīndriyapañcakaṃ ca tatra manasi janye sarvatanmātrajananasāmarthyayuktaḥ sa janakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, from the sāttvika form arise the mind and the five cognitive senses. In the case of mind, when it is produced, that producer is endowed with the capacity to generate all the subtle elements.

children.text: śrotre tu śabdajananasāmarthyaviśiṣṭa iti yāvat ghrāṇe gandhajananayogyatāyukta iti bhautikam api na yuktam ahaṃ śṛṇomi ityādyanugamāc ca sphuṭam āhaṃkārikatvam karaṇatvena ca avaśyaṃ kartraṃśasparśitvam anyathā karaṇāntarayojanāyām anavasthādyāpātāt ||
children.translated_text: But in the ear it is specified by the capacity to generate sound; in the nose it is endowed with fitness to generate smell. Therefore it is not proper to regard it as merely material. And from the continuity expressed in "I hear" and the like, its derivation from <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is clear. Also, since it is an instrument, it must necessarily be in contact with the agent-aspect; otherwise, if another instrument had to be connected to it, infinite regress and the like would result.

children.text: kartraṃśaś ca ahaṃkāra eva tena mukhye karaṇe dve puṃsaḥ jñāne vidyā kriyāyāṃ kalā andhasya paṅgoś ca ahaṃtārūpajñānakriyānapagamāt udriktatanmātrabhāgaviśiṣṭāt tu sāttvikād eva ahaṃkārāt karmendriyapañcakam ahaṃ gacchāmi iti ahaṃkāraviśiṣṭaḥ kāryakaraṇakṣamaḥ pādendriyaṃ tasya mukhyādhiṣṭhānaṃ bāhyam anyatrāpi tad asty eva iti rugṇasyāpi na gativicchedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the agent-aspect is precisely <s>ahaṃkāra</s>. Therefore there are two principal instruments of the <s>puruṣa</s>: in cognition, <s>vidyā</s>, and in action, <s>kalā</s>, since knowledge and action in the form of "I" do not disappear in the blind and the lame. But from that same sāttvika <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, distinguished by an abundant portion of subtle elements, arises the group of five organs of action. The expression "I go" shows that the foot-organ, qualified by <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, is capable of producing the effect; the foot is its chief external support. It exists elsewhere too, and therefore even for an injured person there is no complete cessation of movement.

children.text: na ca kartavyasāṃkaryamuktād eva hetoḥ kriyā karaṇakāryā mukhyaṃ ca gamanādīnāṃ kriyātvaṃ na rūpādyupalambhasya tasya kāṇādatantre guṇatvāt tasmāt avaśyābhyupeyaḥ karmendriyavargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor is there any confusion about what is to be done, for the very reason just stated: action is the effect of an instrument. And going and the like are actions in the primary sense, but the apprehension of color and the like is not, since in the <s>Kāṇāda</s> system that is a quality. Therefore the class of organs of action must necessarily be accepted.

children.text: sa ca pañcakaḥ anusaṃdhes tāvattvāt ||
children.translated_text: And that group is fivefold, because practical activity extends just that far.

children.text: tathā hi bahis tāvat tyāgāya vā anusaṃdhiḥ ādānāya vā dvayāya vā ubhayarahitatvena svarūpaviśrāntaye vā tatra krameṇa pāyuḥ pāṇiḥ pāda upastha iti ||
children.translated_text: For thus, externally, attention is directed either toward abandonment, or toward taking up, or toward both, or, as free from both, toward repose in one's own nature. In that order the organs are the anus, the hand, the foot, and the generative organ.

children.text: antaḥ prāṇāśrayakarmānusaṃdhes tu vāgindriyam tena indriyādhiṣṭhāne haste yat gamanaṃ tad api pādendriyasyaiva karma iti mantavyam tena karmānantyam api na indriyānantyam āvahet iyati rājasasya upaśleṣakatvam ity āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: But with respect to internal attention to action based on <s>prāṇa</s>, the organ is speech. Therefore the movement that occurs in the hand, the seat of the organ, should also be understood as the action of the foot-organ itself. Thus even an infinity of actions would not entail an infinity of organs. So they say that the rājasic factor has this connective function.

children.text: anye tu rājasān mana ity āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Others, however, say that mind arises from the rājasic factor.

children.text: anye tu sāttvikāt mano rājasāc ca indriyāṇi iti ||
children.translated_text: Others say that mind arises from the sāttvic factor and the organs from the rājasic factor.

children.text: bhoktraṃśācchādakāt tu tamaḥpradhānāhaṃkārāt tanmātrāṇi vedyaikarūpāṇi pañca ||
children.translated_text: But from the tamas-dominant ego, which veils the enjoyer-aspect, come the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements), whose single form is that of the knowable.

children.text: śabdaviśeṣāṇāṃ hi kṣobhātmanāṃ yad ekam akṣobhātmakaṃ prāgbhāvi sāmānyam aviśeṣātmakaṃ tat śabdatanmātram ||
children.translated_text: For among particular sounds, whose nature is agitation, that one prior universal, whose nature is non-agitation and which is undifferentiated, is the sound-<s>tanmātra</s>.

children.text: evaṃ gandhānte 'pi vācyam ||
children.translated_text: The same should be said also down to smell.

children.text: tatra śabdatanmātrāt kṣubhitāt avakāśadānavyāpāraṃ nabhaḥ śabdasya vācyādhyāsāvakāśasahatvāt ||
children.translated_text: There, from the sound-<s>tanmātra</s> when agitated arises space, whose operation is the giving of room, because it is capable of providing room for the superimposition of the expressed object of sound.

children.text: śabdatanmātraṃ kṣubhitaṃ vāyuḥ śabdas tu asya nabhasā virahābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: The agitated sound-<s>tanmātra</s> is air; but sound belongs to it because it is not separated from space.

children.text: rūpaṃ kṣubhitaṃ tejaḥ pūrvaguṇau tu pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: Agitated form is fire, while the two preceding qualities belong to it as before.

children.text: rasaḥ kṣubhita āpaḥ pūrve trayaḥ pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: Agitated taste is water; the preceding three qualities belong to it as before.

children.text: gandhaḥ kṣubhito dharā pūrve catvāraḥ pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: Agitated smell is earth; the preceding four qualities belong to it as before.

children.text: anye śabdasparśābhyāṃ vāyuḥ ityādikrameṇa pañcabhyo dharaṇī iti manyante ||
children.translated_text: Others think that, in the sequence beginning 'air from sound and touch,' earth is produced from the five.

children.text: guṇasamudāyamātraṃ ca pṛthivī nānyo guṇī kaścit ||
children.translated_text: And earth is merely an aggregate of qualities; there is no other quality-bearer at all.

children.text: asmiṃś ca tattvakalāpe ūrdhvordhvaguṇaṃ vyāpakaṃ nikṛṣṭaguṇaṃ tu vyāpyam ||
children.translated_text: In this group of <s>tattvas</s>, each higher and higher quality is pervasive, while the lower quality is pervaded.

children.text: sa eva guṇasya utkarṣo yat tena vinā guṇāntaraṃ na upapadyate tena pṛthivītattvaṃ śivatattvāt prabhṛti jalatattvena vyāptam evaṃ jalaṃ tejasā ityādi yāvacchaktitattvam ||
children.translated_text: That indeed is the superiority of a quality: that without it another quality cannot be established. Therefore the earth-<s>tattva</s>, beginning with the <s>Śiva</s>-<s>tattva</s>, is pervaded by the water-<s>tattva</s>; similarly water by fire, and so on up to the <s>Śakti</s>-<s>tattva</s>.

children.text: Chapter 9
sa ca saptadhā ṣaḍardhaśāstra eva paraṃ parameśena uktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And this sevenfold supreme division has been taught by <s>Parameśa</s> himself in the <s>Ṣaḍardhaśāstra</s>.

children.text: tatra śivāḥ mantramaheśāḥ mantreśāḥ mantrāḥ vijñānākalāḥ pralayākalāḥ sakalā iti sapta śaktimantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are seven possessors of power: the <s>Śivas</s>, the <s>Mantramaheśas</s>, the <s>Mantreśas</s>, the <s>Mantras</s>, the <s>Vijñānākalas</s>, the <s>Pralayākalas</s>, and the <s>Sakalas</s>.

children.text: eṣāṃ saptaiva śaktayaḥ tadbhedāt pṛthivyādipradhānatattvāntaṃ caturdaśabhir bhedaiḥ pratyekaṃ svaṃ rūpaṃ pañcadaśam ||
children.translated_text: Their powers too are exactly seven. By their differentiation, each one's own form is fifteenth, along with the fourteen divisions extending down to the principal <s>tattva</s>s beginning with earth.

children.text: tatra svaṃ rūpaṃ prameyatāyogyaṃ svātmaniṣṭham aparābhaṭṭārikānugrahāt pramātṛṣu udriktaśaktiṣu yat viśrāntibhājanaṃ tat tasyaiva śāktaṃ rūpaṃ śrīmatparāparānugrahāt tac ca saptavidhaṃ śaktīnāṃ tāvattvāt ||
children.translated_text: There, one's own form is fit to be an object of knowledge and abides in itself; through the grace of <s>Aparābhaṭṭārikā</s>, that which, among knowers whose powers have become heightened, becomes the vessel of repose is the śākta form of that very one. Through the grace of glorious <s>Parāparā</s>, this too is sevenfold, because the powers are so many.

children.text: śaktimadrūpapradhāne tu pramātṛvarge yat viśrāntaṃ tacchaktimacchivarūpaṃ śrīmatparābhaṭṭārikānugrahāt tad api saptavidham ||
children.translated_text: But that which comes to rest in the class of knowers in which the power-possessor form is predominant is the <s>Śiva</s> form that possesses power, through the grace of glorious <s>Parābhaṭṭārikā</s>; this too is sevenfold.

children.text: pramātṝṇāṃ śivāt prabhṛti sakalāntānāṃ tāvatām uktatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For so many knowers have been stated, beginning with <s>Śiva</s> and ending with the <s>Sakala</s>.

children.text: tatra śaktibhedād eva pramātṝṇāṃ bhedaḥ sa ca sphuṭīkaraṇārthaṃ sakalādikrameṇa bhaṇyate tatra sakalasya vidyākale śaktiḥ tadviśeṣarūpatvāt buddhikarmākṣaśaktīnāṃ pralayākalasya tu te eva nirviṣayatvāt asphuṭe ||
children.translated_text: There, the difference among knowers comes solely from the difference of powers. To make this clear it is explained in the order beginning with the <s>Sakala</s>: in the <s>Sakala</s>, power consists in <s>vidyā</s> and <s>kalā</s>, because the powers of intellect and of the organs of action and cognition are specific forms of these. In the <s>Pralayākala</s>, those very powers are indistinct, because they have no object.

children.text: vijñānākalasya te eva vigalatkalpe tatsaṃskārasacivā prabudhyamānā śuddhavidyā mantrasya ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vijñānākala</s>, those same powers are as if slipping away; pure knowledge, assisted by their residual impressions and beginning to awaken, belongs to the <s>Mantra</s>.

children.text: tatsaṃskārahīnā saiva prabuddhā mantreśasya ||
children.translated_text: That same pure knowledge, awakened and free of those residual impressions, belongs to the <s>Mantreśa</s>.

children.text: saiva icchāśaktirūpatāṃ svātantryasvabhāvāṃ jighṛkṣantī mantramaheśvarasya ||
children.translated_text: That same power, wishing to take on the form of will-power, whose nature is freedom, belongs to the <s>Mantramaheśvara</s>.

children.text: icchātmikā sphuṭasvātantryātmikā śivasya iti śaktibhedāḥ sapta mukhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: As will itself, whose nature is manifest freedom, it belongs to <s>Śiva</s>. These are the seven principal differences of power.

children.text: taduparāgakṛtaś ca śaktimatsu pramātṛṣu bhedaḥ karaṇabhedasya kartṛbhedaparyavasānāt śakter eva ca avyatiriktāyāḥ karaṇīkartuṃ śakyatvāt na anyasya anavasthādyāpatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: And through the coloring caused by these powers there is difference among the power-possessing knowers, because difference of instrument culminates in difference of agent. Since only power, which is not distinct from the agent, can be made into an instrument, and not anything else, for that would entail infinite regress and the like.

children.text: vastutaḥ punar eka eva citsvātantryānandaviśrāntaḥ pramātā tatra pṛthivī svarūpamātraviśrāntā yadā vedyate tadā svarūpam asyāḥ kevalaṃ bhāti caitracakṣurdṛṣṭaṃ caitraviditaṃ jānāmīti tatra sakalaśaktikṛtaṃ sakalaśaktimadrūpakṛtaṃ svarūpāntaraṃ bhāty eva evaṃ śivāntam api vācyaṃ śivaśaktiniṣṭhaṃ śivasvabhāvaviśrāntaṃ ca viśvaṃ jānāmi iti pratyayasya vilakṣaṇasya bhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: In reality, however, there is only one knower, reposing in the bliss of the freedom of consciousness. When earth, resting merely in its own nature, is known, then only its own nature appears; and in the cognition 'I know that it was seen by <s>Caitra</s>'s eye and known by <s>Caitra</s>,' another form, produced by the <s>Sakala</s>'s power and produced by the <s>Sakala</s> power-possessor form, also appears. The same should be said up to <s>Śiva</s>: because there is the distinctive cognition, 'I know the universe as grounded in <s>Śiva</s>-power and as reposing in the nature of <s>Śiva</s>.'

children.text: nanu bhāvasya cet vedyatā svaṃ vapuḥ tat sarvān prati vedyatvaṃ vedyatvam api vedyam ity anavasthā tayā ca jagato 'ndhasuptatvaṃ suprakāśam eva tayā ca vedyatvāvedyatve viruddhadharmayoga iti doṣaḥ atra ucyate ||
children.translated_text: But, it may be objected, if the knowability of an entity is its own body, then it would be knowable to everyone; and if knowability too is knowable, there is infinite regress. Through that, the world would clearly be as if blind and asleep; and through that, the fault follows that knowability and unknowability, contrary properties, would belong to the same thing. To this it is replied:

children.text: na tat svaṃ vapuḥ svarūpasya pṛthaguktatvāt kiṃ tarhi tat pramātṛśaktau pramātari ca yat viśrāntibhājanaṃ yat rūpaṃ tat khalu tat tat svaprakāśam eva tat prakāśate na tu kiṃcid api prati iti sarvajñatvam anavasthāviruddhadharmayogaś ca iti dūrāpāstam ||
children.translated_text: It is not its own body, because the essential nature has been stated separately. What then is it? Whatever form is a vessel of repose in the power of the knower and in the knower, that indeed is that; that itself is self-luminous, and that shines, but not toward anything whatsoever. Thus omniscience, an infinite regress, and the conjunction of contradictory properties are all completely set aside.

children.text: anantapramātṛsaṃvedyam api ekam eva tat tasya rūpaṃ tāvati teṣām ekābhāsarūpatvāt iti na pramātrantarasaṃvedanānumānavighnaḥ kaścit tac ca tasya rūpaṃ satyam arthakriyākāritvāt tathaiva paradṛśyamānāṃ kāntāṃ dṛṣṭvā tasyai samīrṣyati śivasvabhāvaṃ viśrāntikumbhaṃ paśyan samāviśati samastānantapramātṛviśrāntaṃ vastu paśyan pūrṇībhavati nartakīprekṣaṇavat tasyaiva nīlasya tadrūpaṃ pramātari yat viśrāntaṃ tathaiva svaprakāśasya vimarśasyodayāt iti pañcadaśātmakatvaṃ pṛthivyāḥ prabhṛti pradhānatattvaparyantam ||
children.translated_text: Although it is knowable by infinitely many knowers, it is one alone, because that is its form, since to that extent they have the form of a single appearance. Thus there is no obstacle from inference about cognition by another knower. And that form of it is real, because it produces effective action. In just this way, seeing a beloved woman who is being seen by another, one becomes jealous of her; seeing the jar of repose whose nature is <s>Śiva</s>, one enters absorption; seeing an object in which all infinite knowers have come to rest, one becomes complete, as when watching a dancer. That very blue has as its form what has come to rest in the knower, because in just that way self-luminous reflective awareness arises. Thus, from earth onward up to the principal tattva, there is a fifteenfold character.

children.text: tāvaty udriktarāgādikañcukasya sakalasya pramātṛtvāt sakalasyāpi evaṃ pāñcadaśyaṃ tasyāpi tāvad vedyatvāt ||
children.translated_text: To that extent, because the sakala, whose coverings such as passion are strongly intensified, has knowership, that sakala too is included in the fifteenfold scheme, since it too is knowable to that extent.

children.text: vitatya caitat nirṇītaṃ tantrāloke ||
children.translated_text: And this has been determined at length in the <s>Tantrāloka</s>.

children.text: puṃsaḥ prabhṛti kalātattvāntaṃ trayodaśadhā ||
children.translated_text: From the puruṣa onward to the end of the kalā-tattva, it is thirteenfold.

children.text: sakalasya tatra pramātṛtāyogena tacchaktiśaktimadātmano bhedadvayasya pratyastamayāt tathā ca sakalasya svarūpatvam eva kevalaṃ pralayākalasya svarūpatve pañcānāṃ pramātṛtve ekādaśa bhedāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since the sakala has no connection with knowership there, the two distinctions whose nature is power and possessor of power come to rest. Accordingly there is only the own-nature of the sakala. When the pralayākala is the own-nature and the five are knowers, there are eleven distinctions.

children.text: vijñānākalasya svarūpatve caturṇāṃ pramātṛtve nava bhedāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the vijñānākala is the own-nature and four are knowers, there are nine distinctions.

children.text: mantrasya svarūpatve trayāṇāṃ pramātṛtve sapta ||
children.translated_text: When the mantra is the own-nature and three are knowers, there are seven.

children.text: mantreśasya svarūpatve dvayoḥ pramātṛtve pañca ||
children.translated_text: When the mantreśa is the own-nature and two are knowers, there are five.

children.text: mantramaheśasya svarūpatve bhagavata ekasyaiva pramātṛtve śaktiśaktimadbhedāt trayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the mantramaheśa is the own-nature and the Blessed One alone is the single knower, there are three, because of the distinction between power and possessor of power.

children.text: śivasya tu prakāśaikacitsvātantryanirbharasya na ko 'pi bhedaḥ paripūrṇatvāt ||
children.translated_text: But for <s>Śiva</s>, who is filled with the freedom of consciousness that is pure light alone, there is no distinction at all, because he is completely full.

children.text: evam ayaṃ tattvabheda eva parameśvarānuttaranayaikākhye nirūpitaḥ bhuvanabhedavaicitryaṃ karoti narakasvargarudrabhuvanānāṃ pārthivatve samāne 'pi dūratarasya svabhāvabhedasya uktatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Thus this very division of tattvas, explained in the single doctrine called the supreme unsurpassed way of <s>Parameśvara</s>, produces the varied differentiation of worlds; for although hells, heavens, and the worlds of the <s>Rudras</s> are equally made of earth, a very remote difference of nature has been stated.

children.text: atra ca parasparaṃ bhedakalanayā avāntarabhedajñānakutūhalī tantrālokam eva avadhārayet ||
children.translated_text: And here, one who is curious to know the intermediate distinctions by calculating their mutual differences should consult the <s>Tantrāloka</s> itself.

children.text: evam ekaikaghaṭādyanusāreṇāpi pṛthivyādīnāṃ tattvānāṃ bhedo nirūpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, even with reference to each individual pot and the like, the distinction of the tattvas such as earth has been explained.

children.text: adhunā samastaṃ pṛthivītattvaṃ pramātṛprameyarūpam uddiśya nirūpyate yo dharātattvābhedena prakāśaḥ sa śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now the whole earth-tattva, in the form of knower and known, is stated and explained. The light that is non-different from the earth-tattva is <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: yathā śrutiḥ pṛthivy evedaṃ brahma iti ||
children.translated_text: As scripture says: 'This brahman is earth itself.'

children.text: dharātattvasiddhipradān prerayati sa dharāmantramaheśvaraḥ preryo dharāmantreśaḥ tasyaivābhimānikavigrahatātmako vācako mantraḥ sāṃkhyādipāśavavidyottīrṇaśivavidyākrameṇa abhyastapārthivayogo 'prāptadhruvapadaḥ dharāvijñānākalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who impels by granting accomplishment of the earth-tattva is the dharā-mantramaheśvara; the one impelled is the dharā-mantreśa. The mantra is the signifier, constituted by the same one's assumed body. One who has practiced the earthy yoga through the sequence of <s>Śiva</s>-knowledge, beyond Sāṃkhya and other limited sciences, but has not attained the fixed station, is the dharā-vijñānākala.

children.text: pāśavavidyākrameṇa abhyastapārthivayogaḥ kalpānte maraṇe vā dharāpralayakevalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who has practiced the earthy yoga through the sequence of limited knowledge, at the end of an aeon or at death, is the dharā-pralayakevala.

children.text: sauṣupte hi tattvāveśavaśād eva citrasya svapnasya udayaḥ syāt gṛhītadharābhimānas tu dharāsakalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For in deep sleep, the arising of variegated dream occurs only through immersion in the tattva. But one who has taken on identification with earth is the dharā-sakala.

children.text: atrāpi śaktyudrekanyagbhāvābhyāṃ caturdaśatvam iti pramātṛtāpannasya dharātattvasya bhedāḥ svarūpaṃ tu śuddhaṃ prameyam iti evam aparatrāpi ||
children.translated_text: Here too, through the predominance and subordination of power, there is a fourteenfoldness. These are the distinctions of the earth-tattva when it has attained knowership; but its own-nature, as pure, is the object known. The same applies elsewhere as well.

children.text: atha ekasmin pramātari prāṇapratiṣṭhitatayā bhedanirūpaṇam iha nīlaṃ gṛhṇataḥ prāṇaḥ tuṭiṣoḍaśakātmā vedyāveśaparyantam udeti tatra ādyā tuṭir avibhāgaikarūpā dvitīyā grāhakollāsarūpā antyā tu grāhyābhinnā tanmayī upāntyā tu sphuṭībhūtagrāhakarūpā madhye tu yat tuṭidvādaśakaṃ tanmadhyāt ādyaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ nirvikalpasvabhāvaṃ vikalpācchādakaṃ ṣaṭtvaṃ ca asya svarūpeṇa ekā tuṭiḥ ācchādanīye ca vikalpe pañcarūpatvam unmimiṣā unmiṣattā sā ca iyaṃ sphuṭakriyārūpatvāt tuṭidvayātmikā spandanasya ekakṣaṇarūpatvābhāvāt unmiṣitatā svakāryakartṛtvaṃ ca ity evam ācchādanīyavikalpapāñcavidhyāt svarūpāc ca ṣaṭ kṣaṇā nirvikalpakāḥ tato 'pi nirvikalpasya dhvaṃsamānatā dhvaṃso vikalpasya unmimiṣā unmiṣattā tuṭidvayātmikā unmiṣitatā ca iti ṣaṭ tuṭayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, the explanation of distinction within a single knower, insofar as it is established in prāṇa. Here, for one apprehending blue, prāṇa, whose nature consists of sixteen tuṭis, arises up to the point of immersion in the knowable. There the first tuṭi has a single undivided form; the second has the form of the rise of the apprehender; the last is non-different from the apprehended and consists of that; the penultimate has the form of the apprehender become manifest. In the middle, there is a set of twelve tuṭis. Of these, the first group of six is non-conceptual in nature and covers conceptual construction. Its sixfoldness is as follows: one tuṭi is its own form, and in the conceptual construction to be covered there is fivefoldness: the desire to open, the state of opening, which itself, because it has the form of manifest activity, consists of two tuṭis, since vibration does not have the form of a single instant; the opened state; and the performance of its own function. Thus, because the conceptual construction to be covered is fivefold, and because of its own form, there are six non-conceptual moments. After that there are also six tuṭis: the state of the non-conceptual as it is being destroyed, its destruction, the desire of the conceptual construction to open, its state of opening, which consists of two tuṭis, and its opened state.

children.text: svakāryakartṛtā tu grāhakarūpatā iti uktaṃ na sā bhūyo gaṇyate ity evaṃ vivekadhanā gurūpaveśānuśīlinaḥ sarvatra pāñcadaśyaṃ pravibhāgena viviñcate ||
children.translated_text: The performance of its own function, however, is the state of being the apprehender; so it has been stated, and it is not counted again. Thus those rich in discrimination, who practice the instruction of the guru, discern the fifteenfoldness everywhere by division.

children.text: vikalpanyūnatve tu tuṭinyūnatā sukhādisaṃvittāv iva yāvat avikalpataiva ||
children.translated_text: But when conceptual construction is deficient, there is a deficiency of tuṭis, as in the awareness of pleasure and the like, up to the point where there is simply non-conceptuality.

children.text: lokās tu vikalpaviśrāntyā tām ahaṃtāmayīm ahaṃtācchāditedaṃbhāvavikalpaprasarāṃ nirvikalpāṃ vimarśabhuvam aprakāśitām iva manyante duḥkhāvasthāṃ sukhaviśrāntā iva vikalpanirhrāsena tu sā prakāśata eva iti iyam asau sambandhe grāhyagrāhakayoḥ sāvadhānatā iti abhinavaguptaguravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But ordinary people, because they repose in conceptual construction, think of that ground of reflective awareness, which is made of I-ness, in which the expansion of conceptual construction as this-ness is covered by I-ness, which is non-conceptual, as though it were unmanifested: they regard it as a state of pain, while they are as if reposing in pleasure. But through the decrease of conceptual construction, it does indeed become manifest. This is what the revered teachers <s>Abhinavagupta</s> call attentiveness in the relation between the grasper and the grasped.

children.text: evaṃ ca pāñcadaśye sthite yāvat sphuṭedaṃtātmano bhedasya nyūnatā tāvat dvayaṃ dvayaṃ hrasati yāvat dvituṭikaḥ śivāveśaḥ tatra ādyā tuṭiḥ sarvataḥ pūrṇā dvitīyā sarvajñānakaraṇāviṣṭābhyasyamānā sarvajñatvasarvakartṛtvāya kalpate na tu ādyā ||
children.translated_text: And when the fifteenfold scheme stands in this way, to the extent that there is a deficiency in the distinction whose nature is clearly this-ness, to that extent two by two are diminished, until there is the two-tuṭi absorption into <s>Śiva</s>. There, the first tuṭi is complete in every way; the second, when practiced as pervaded by all the instruments of knowledge, is fit for omniscience and omnipotence, but the first is not.

children.text: yad āha śrīkallaṭaḥ tuṭipāta iti atra pātaśabdaṃ saiva bhagavatī śrīmatkālī mātṛsadbhāvo bhairavaḥ pratibhā ity alaṃ rahasyārahasyanena ||
children.translated_text: As glorious <s>Kallaṭa</s> says, 'the fall of the tuṭi.' Here the word 'fall' refers to that very blessed glorious <s>Kālī</s>, the reality of the Mother, <s>Bhairava</s>, intuitive flash. Enough of this secret and non-secret matter.

children.text: evaṃ mantramaheśatuṭeḥ prabhṛti tattadabhyāsāt tattatsiddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, beginning with the tuṭi of the <s>Mantramaheśa</s>, through the practice of each respective one, the corresponding accomplishment arises.

children.text: athātraiva jāgradādyavasthā nirūpyante tatra vedyasya tadviṣayāyāś ca saṃvido yat vaicitryam anyonyāpekṣaṃ sat sā avasthā na vedyasya kevalasya na cāpi kevalāyāḥ saṃvido na cāpi pṛthak pṛthak dve ||
children.translated_text: Now, in this very context the states beginning with waking are explained. There, whatever variety belongs to the knowable and to the consciousness whose object it is, while they are mutually dependent, that is a state; it is not of the knowable alone, nor of consciousness alone, nor are there two separately.

children.text: tatra yadādhiṣṭheyatayā bahīrūpatayā bhānaṃ tadā jāgradavasthā meye mātari māne ca ||
children.translated_text: When there is manifestation as something external, in the manner of what is to be established, then there is the waking state in the object of knowledge, in the knower, and in the means of knowledge.

children.text: yadā tu tatraiva adhiṣṭhānarūpatayā bhānaṃ saṃkalpaḥ tadā svapnāvasthā ||
children.translated_text: But when, in that very same place, there is manifestation as the basis, as mental construction, then there is the dream state.

children.text: yadā tu tatraiva adhiṣṭhātṛrūpatayā bījātmatayaiva bhānaṃ tadā suṣuptāvasthā ||
children.translated_text: But when, in that very same place, there is manifestation only in seed form, as the establisher, then there is the deep-sleep state.

children.text: imā eva tisraḥ prameyapramāṇapramātravasthāḥ pratyekaṃ jāgradādibhedāt caturvidhā uktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These very three states of object, means of knowledge, and knower are each said to be fourfold according to the distinctions beginning with waking.

children.text: yadā tu tasminn eva pramātṛviśrāntigate pramātuḥ pūrṇataunmukhyāt taddvāreṇa pūrṇatonmukhatayā bhānaṃ tadā turyāvasthā sā ca rūpaṃ dṛśāham ity evaṃvidham aṃśatrayam uttīrya paśyāmīti anupāyikā pramātṛtā svātantryasārā naikaṭyamadhyatvadūratvaiḥ pramātṛpramāṇaprameyatābhiṣekaṃ dadatī tadavasthātrayānugrāhakatvāt tribhedā ||
children.translated_text: But when, in that same thing that has come to rest in the knower, there is manifestation through the knower's orientation toward fullness and, by that route, as oriented toward fullness, then there is the fourth state, turya. And this, having transcended the triad of parts expressed as 'form,' 'seeing,' and 'I,' is the immediate knowership expressed as 'I see'; its essence is freedom. Since it confers the consecration as knower, means of knowledge, and object of knowledge through nearness, middle position, and distance, and since it graciously supports those three states, it is threefold.

children.text: etad eva avasthācatuṣṭayaṃ piṇḍasthapadastharūpastharūpātītaśabdair yogino vyavaharanti prasaṃkhyānadhanās tu sarvatobhadraṃ vyāptiḥ mahāvyāptiḥ pracaya iti śabdaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This very tetrad of states is referred to by yogins with the terms piṇḍastha, padastha, rūpastha, and rūpātīta. But those rich in contemplative enumeration use the terms sarvatobhadra, vyāpti, mahāvyāpti, and pracaya.

children.text: anvarthaṃ cātra darśitaṃ tantrāloke ślokavārttike ca ||
children.translated_text: And this has been shown meaningfully in the <s>Tantrāloka</s> and in the <s>Ślokavārttika</s>.

children.text: yac ca sarvāntarbhūtaṃ pūrṇarūpaṃ tat turyātītaṃ sarvātītaṃ mahāpracayaṃ ca nirūpayanti ||
children.translated_text: And that which includes everything and has the form of fullness they describe as beyond the fourth, beyond all, and as the great accumulation.

children.text: kiṃca yasya yad yadā rūpaṃ sphuṭaṃ sthiram anubandhi tat jāgrat tasyaiva tadviparyayaḥ svapnaḥ yaḥ layākalasya bhogaḥ sarvāvedanaṃ suṣuptaṃ yo vijñānākalasya bhogaḥ bhogyābhinnīkaraṇaṃ turyaṃ mantrādīnāṃ sa bhogaḥ bhāvānāṃ śivābhedas turyātītaṃ sarvātītam ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, whatever form of something is clear, stable, and continuous, that is its waking state; the opposite of that very thing is dream. The experience of the <s>Layākala</s>, which is the non-perception of everything, is deep sleep. The experience of the <s>Vijñānākala</s>, which makes the object of enjoyment non-different from oneself, is turya. That experience belongs to the <s>Mantras</s> and the others. The non-difference of entities from <s>Śiva</s> is beyond the fourth, beyond all.

children.text: tatra svarūpasakalau 1 pralayākalaḥ 2 vijñānākalaḥ 3 mantratadīśatanmaheśavargaḥ 4 iti pañcadaśabhede pañca avasthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, in the fifteenfold division, the five states are: the own-nature and the <s>Sakala</s> together, the <s>Pralayākala</s>, the <s>Vijñānākala</s>, and the class of the <s>Mantras</s>, their lords, and their great lords.

children.text: svarūpaṃ pralayākala ityādikrameṇa trayodaśabhede svarūpaṃ vijñānākalaśaktiḥ vijñānākala ity ekādaśabhede svarūpaṃ mantrāḥ tadīśāḥ maheśāḥ śivaḥ iti navabhede svarūpaṃ mantreśāḥ maheśaḥ śaktiḥ śiva iti saptabhede svarūpaṃ maheśaśaktiḥ maheśaḥ śaktiḥ śiva iti pañcabhede svarūpaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ jñānaśaktiḥ icchāśaktiḥ śiva iti tribhede abhinne 'pi śivatattve kriyājñānecchānandacidrūpakﾱptyā prasaṃkhyānayogadhanāḥ pañcapadatvam āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the thirteenfold division, in the sequence beginning with own-nature, <s>Pralayākala</s>, and so on; in the elevenfold division, own-nature, the power of the <s>Vijñānākala</s>, and the <s>Vijñānākala</s>; in the ninefold division, own-nature, the <s>Mantras</s>, their lords, the great lords, and <s>Śiva</s>; in the sevenfold division, own-nature, the <s>Mantreśas</s>, the great lord, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>; in the fivefold division, own-nature, the power of the great lord, the great lord, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>; in the threefold division, action-power, knowledge-power, will-power, and <s>Śiva</s>. Although the <s>Śiva</s>-tattva is undivided, those rich in contemplative enumeration speak of its fivefold state on account of its conception as forms of action, knowledge, will, bliss, and consciousness.

children.text: Chapter 10
uktas tāvat tattvādhvā ||
children.translated_text: Thus the path of the tattvas has now been stated.

children.text: kalādyadhvā tu nirūpyate tatra yathā bhuvaneṣu anugāmi kiṃcid rūpaṃ tattvam ity uktam tathā tattveṣu vargaśo yat anugāmi rūpaṃ tat kalā ekarūpakalanāsahiṣṇutvāt ||
children.translated_text: Now the path beginning with the kalās is explained. There, just as a certain form that runs through the worlds has been called a tattva, so the form that runs through the tattvas by classes is a kalā, because it is capable of forming a single form.

children.text: tad yathā pṛthivyāṃ nivṛttiḥ nivartate yatas tattvasarga iti ||
children.translated_text: For example, in earth there is nivṛtti, because the creation of tattvas withdraws from it.

children.text: jalādipradhānānte varge pratiṣṭhā kāraṇatayāpyāyanapūraṇakāritvāt ||
children.translated_text: In the class from water through pradhāna there is pratiṣṭhā, because, as cause, it effects saturation and filling.

children.text: pumādimāyānte vidyā vedyatirobhāve saṃvidādhikyāt ||
children.translated_text: From puruṣa through māyā there is vidyā, because consciousness is predominant while the knowable is concealed.

children.text: śuddhavidyādiśaktyante śāntā kañcukataraṃgopaśamāt ||
children.translated_text: From pure knowledge through śakti there is śāntā, because the waves of the coverings have subsided.

children.text: etad eva aṇḍacatuṣṭayaṃ pārthivaprākṛtamāyīyaśāktābhidham ||
children.translated_text: This very thing is the fourfold cosmic egg, called pārthiva, prākṛta, māyīya, and śākta.

children.text: pṛthivyādiśaktīnām atra avasthānena śaktitattve yāvat parasparśo vidyate sparśasya ca sapratighatvam iti tāvati yuktam aṇḍatvam ||
children.translated_text: Because the powers beginning with earth are stationed here, and because contact with the supreme exists as far as the śakti-tattva, while contact has resistance, egghood is appropriate up to that point.

children.text: śivatattve śāntātītā tasyopadeśabhāvanārcādau kalyamānatvāt ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Śiva</s>-tattva there is śāntātītā, because it is formed in instruction, contemplation, worship, and the like concerning him.

children.text: svatantraṃ tu paraṃ tattvaṃ tatrāpi yat aprameyaṃ tat kalātītam ||
children.translated_text: But the supreme tattva is free; and even there, what is immeasurable is beyond kalā.

children.text: evaṃ pañcaiva kalāḥ ṣaṭtriṃśattattvāni ||
children.translated_text: Thus there are exactly five kalās and thirty-six tattvas.

children.text: tathāhi prameyatvaṃ dvidhā sthūlasūkṣmatvena iti daśa ||
children.translated_text: Thus, knowability is twofold, as gross and subtle; so there are ten.

children.text: karaṇatvaṃ dvidhā śuddhaṃ kartṛtāsparśi ca iti daśa ||
children.translated_text: Instrumentality is twofold: pure, and touching agency; so there are ten.

children.text: karaṇatopasarjanakartṛbhāvasphuṭatvāt pañca śuddhakartṛbhāvāt pañca vigalitavibhāgatayā vikāsonmukhatve pañca sarvāvacchedaśūnyaṃ śivatattvaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśam ||
children.translated_text: Because the state of agency subordinate to instrumentality is evident, there are five; because there is pure agency, five; because, with division dissolved, there are five in the state of beginning to unfold; and the <s>Śiva</s>-<s>tattva</s>, empty of every limitation, is the thirty-sixth.

children.text: tad yadā upadiśyate bhāvyate vā yat tatpratiṣṭhāpadam tat saptatriṃśam tasminn api bhāvyamāne aṣṭātriṃśam na ca anavasthā tasya bhāvyamānasya anavacchinnasvātantryayogino vedyīkaraṇe saptatriṃśa eva paryavasānāt ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ tu sarvatattvottīrṇatayā saṃbhāvyāvacchedam iti pañcakalāvidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When that is taught or contemplated, whatever is the station in which it is established is the thirty-seventh. When that too is contemplated, it is the thirty-eighth. Nor is there an infinite regress, because, when that which is being contemplated and possesses unrestricted freedom is made an object of knowledge, the process comes to rest precisely in the thirty-seventh. But the thirty-sixth, as transcending all <s>tattvas</s>, has a conceivable limitation. This is the method of the five <s>kalās</s>.

children.text: vijñānākalaparyantam ātmakalā īśāntaṃ vidyākalā śiṣṭaṃ śivakalā iti tritattvavidhiḥ ||
