children.translated_text: Up to the <s>Vijñānākala</s> is the self-<s>kalā</s>; up to <s>Īśa</s> is the knowledge-<s>kalā</s>; what remains is the <s>Śiva</s>-<s>kalā</s>. This is the method of the three <s>tattvas</s>.

children.text: evaṃ navatattvādy api ūhayet iti ||
children.translated_text: In this way one should also infer the method beginning with nine <s>tattvas</s>, and so on.

children.text: meyāṃśagāmī sthūlasūkṣmapararūpatvāt trividho bhuvanatattvakalātmādhvabhedaḥ mātṛviśrāntyā tathaiva trividhaḥ tatra pramāṇatāyāṃ padādhvā pramāṇasyaiva kṣobhataraṃgaśāmyattāyāṃ mantrādhvā tatpraśame pūrṇapramātṛtāyāṃ varṇādhvā sa eva ca asau tāvati viśrāntyā labdhasvarūpo bhavati iti ekasyaiva ṣaḍvidhatvaṃ yuktam ||
children.translated_text: Because it pertains to the knowable aspect and has gross, subtle, and supreme forms, the distinction of the <s>adhvan</s> consisting of worlds, <s>tattvas</s>, and <s>kalās</s> is threefold. Through repose in the knower it is likewise threefold. There, in the condition of means of knowledge, it is the word-<s>adhvan</s>; when the waves of agitation of the means of knowledge are becoming quiet, it is the mantra-<s>adhvan</s>; when that has become quiet and there is complete knowership, it is the phoneme-<s>adhvan</s>. And that very one, by repose to that extent, becomes one whose own form has been obtained. Thus the sixfoldness of one and the same reality is reasonable.

children.text: Chapter 11
tatra yāvat idam uktam tat sākṣāt kasyacit apavargāptaye yathoktasaṃgrahanītyā bhavati kasyacit vakṣyamāṇadīkṣāyām upayogagamanāt iti dīkṣādikaṃ vaktavyam ||
children.translated_text: All that has been said here serves directly for someone's attainment of liberation, according to the concise procedure already stated; and for another it is useful in the initiation that will be explained. Therefore initiation and related matters must now be stated.

children.text: tatra kaḥ adhikārī iti nirūpaṇārthaṃ śaktipāto vicāryate ||
children.translated_text: There, in order to determine who is qualified, <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power) is examined.

children.text: tatra kecit āhuḥ jñānābhāvāt ajñānamūlaḥ saṃsāraḥ tadapagame jñānodayāt śaktipāta iti teṣāṃ samyak jñānodaya eva vikṛta iti vācyam karmajanyatve karmaphalavat bhogatvaprasaṅge bhogini ca śaktipātābhyupagatau atiprasaṅgaḥ īśvarecchānimittatve tu jñānodayasya anyonyāśrayatā vaiyarthyaṃ ca īśvare rāgādiprasaṅgaḥ viruddhayoḥ karmaṇoḥ samabalayoḥ anyonyapratibandhe karmasāmyaṃ tataḥ śaktipāta iti cet na kramikatve virodhāyogāt virodhe 'pi anyasya aviruddhasya karmaṇo bhogadānaprasaṅgāt aviruddhakarmāpravṛttau tadaiva dehapātaprasaṅgāt jātyāyuṣpradaṃ karma na pratibadhyate bhogapradam eva tu pratibadhyate iti cet kutaḥ tatkarmasadbhāve yadi śaktiḥ patet tarhi sā bhogapradāt kiṃ bibhiyāt ||
children.translated_text: On this point some say: because bondage arises from ignorance through the absence of knowledge, when that is removed, knowledge arises, and this is <s>śaktipāta</s>. To them it must be said that the very arising of true knowledge would be distorted. If it were produced by karma, then, like the fruit of karma, it would have to be an experience; and if <s>śaktipāta</s> were admitted in the experiencer, the consequence would be overextension. But if the arising of knowledge has the will of <s>Īśvara</s> as its cause, there is mutual dependence and uselessness, and attachment and the like would follow in <s>Īśvara</s>. If one says that, when two opposed karmas of equal strength mutually obstruct one another, there is equality of karma and from that <s>śaktipāta</s>, no: if they occur in sequence, opposition is impossible; and even if there is opposition, some other non-opposed karma would have to give its experience. If the non-opposed karma did not operate, the body would have to fall at that very time. If one says that karma producing birth and lifespan is not obstructed, but only karma producing experience is obstructed, why should that be so? If power were to descend while that karma exists, why would it fear the karma that produces experience?

children.text: atha malaparipāke śaktipātaḥ so 'pi kiṃsvarūpaḥ kiṃ ca tasya nimittam iti etena vairāgyaṃ dharmaviśeṣo vivekaḥ satsevā satprāptiḥ devapūjā ityādihetuḥ pratyukta iti bhedavādināṃ sarvam asamañjasam ||
children.translated_text: Or, if <s>śaktipāta</s> occurs when impurity has ripened, what is the nature of that ripening, and what is its cause? By this, explanations such as dispassion, a special merit, discrimination, service to the good, attainment of the good, worship of the deity, and so forth as causes have also been refuted. Thus everything taught by the proponents of difference is incoherent.

children.text: svatantraparameśādvayavāde tu upapadyate etat yathāhi parameśvaraḥ svarūpācchādanakrīḍayā paśuḥ pudgalo 'ṇuḥ sampannaḥ na ca tasya deśakālasvarūpabhedavirodhaḥ tadvat svarūpasthaganavinivṛttyā svarūpapratyāpattiṃ jhaṭiti vā krameṇa vā samāśrayan śaktipātapātram aṇuḥ ucyate svātantryamātrasāraś ca asau paramaśivaḥ śakteḥ pātayitā iti nirapekṣa eva śaktipāto yaḥ svarūpaprathāphalaḥ yas tu bhogotsukasya sa karmāpekṣaḥ lokottararūpabhogotsukasya tu sa eva śaktipātaḥ parameśvarecchāpreritamāyāgarbhādhikārīyarudraviṣṇubrahmādidvāreṇa mantrādirūpatvaṃ māyāpuṃvivekaṃ puṃskalāvivekaṃ puṃprakṛtivivekaṃ puṃbuddhivivekam anyac ca phalaṃ prasnuvānaḥ tadadharatattvabhogaṃ pratibadhnāti bhogamokṣobhayotsukasya bhoge karmāpekṣo mokṣe tu tannirapekṣaḥ iti sāpekṣanirapekṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But in the doctrine of the independent, nondual <s>Parameśa</s>, this is intelligible. For <s>Parameśvara</s>, through the play of concealing his own nature, has become the bound soul, the individual, the atomic subject; and there is no contradiction for him through difference of place, time, or own-nature. In the same way, when the atomic subject, through the cessation of the covering of its own nature, adopts the recovery of its own nature either suddenly or gradually, it is called a vessel of <s>śaktipāta</s>. And that <s>Paramaśiva</s>, whose essence is mere freedom, is the one who causes the descent of power. Therefore <s>śaktipāta</s> is independent, and its fruit is the manifestation of one's own nature. But the descent that belongs to one eager for enjoyment depends on karma. For one eager for a supramundane enjoyment, that very <s>śaktipāta</s>, through the agency of <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and others who hold office in the womb of māyā and are impelled by the will of <s>Parameśvara</s>, brings forth the state of mantra and other results: discrimination between māyā and the person, between the person and <s>kalā</s>, between the person and prakṛti, between the person and buddhi, and further fruits; and it blocks enjoyment of the lower <s>tattvas</s>. For one eager for both enjoyment and liberation, with respect to enjoyment it depends on karma, but with respect to liberation it is independent of that. Thus it is both dependent and independent.

children.text: na ca vācyaṃ kasmāt kasmiṃścid eva puṃsi śaktipāta iti sa eva parameśvaraḥ tathā bhāti iti satattve ko 'sau pumān nāma yaduddeśena viṣayakṛtā codanā iyam ||
children.translated_text: Nor should one ask, 'Why does <s>śaktipāta</s> occur only in some particular person?' That very <s>Parameśvara</s> appears in that way. In the true reality, who is this so-called person, with reference to whom this object-oriented question is being urged?

children.text: sa cāyaṃ śaktipāto navadhā tīvramadhyamandasya utkarṣamādhyasthyanikarṣaiḥ punas traividhyāt tatra utkṛṣṭatīvrāt tadaiva dehapāte parameśatā madhyatīvrāt śāstrācāryānapekṣiṇaḥ svapratyayasya prātibhajñānodayaḥ yadudaye bāhyasaṃskāraṃ vinaiva bhogāpavargapradaḥ prātibho gurur ity ucyate tasya hi na samayyādikalpanā kācit atrāpi tāratamyasadbhāvaḥ icchāvaicitryāt iti saty api prātibhatve śāstrādyapekṣā saṃvādāya syād api iti nirbhittisabhittyādibahubhedatvam ācāryasya prātibhasyāgameṣu uktam sarvathā pratibhāṃśo balīyān tatsaṃnidhau anyeṣām anadhikārāt ||
children.translated_text: And this śaktipāta is ninefold, because the intense, the middling, and the weak are each again threefold through superiority, middleness, and inferiority. There, from the superior intense kind there is lordship as <s>Parameśvara</s> at that very moment when the body falls. From the middling intense kind there arises, for one who does not depend on scripture or teacher, self-certainty in the form of intuitive knowledge; when it arises, the intuitive guru, who grants enjoyment and liberation without any external consecration, is so called. For him there is no imagined requirement such as samaya-initiation. Here too there is gradation, because of the variety of will. Thus, even where intuitive knowledge exists, there may still be dependence on scripture and the like for confirmation. Therefore the scriptures state many distinctions, such as unsupported and supported, in the intuitive teacher. In every case the portion of intuition is stronger, since in its presence the others have no authority.

children.text: bhedadarśana iva anādiśivasaṃnidhau muktaśivānāṃ sṛṣṭilayādikṛtyeṣu mandatīvrāt śaktipātāt sadguruviṣayā yiyāsā bhavati asadguruviṣayāyāṃ tu tirobhāva eva asadgurutas tu sadgurugamanaṃ śaktipātād eva ||
children.translated_text: As, in a doctrine of difference, the liberated <s>Śivas</s> have only a slight role in acts such as creation and dissolution in the presence of the beginningless <s>Śiva</s>, so from the weak intense śaktipāta there arises a desire to approach a true guru. But when the object is a false guru, there is only concealment. Still, going from a false guru to a true guru occurs only because of śaktipāta.

children.text: sadgurus tu samastaitacchāstratattvajñānapūrṇaḥ sākṣāt bhagavadbhairavabhaṭṭāraka eva yogino 'pi svabhyastajñānatayaiva mocakatve tatra yogyatvasya saubhāgyalāvaṇyādimattvasyevānupayogāt ||
children.translated_text: The true guru, however, is directly the blessed venerable <s>Bhairava</s> himself, full of knowledge of all these scriptural principles. Even in the case of yogins, their power to liberate is only through their own practiced knowledge; for in that matter fitness has no use, just as the possession of good fortune, beauty, and the like has none.

children.text: asadgurus tu anyaḥ sarva eva ||
children.translated_text: A false guru, however, is everyone else.

children.text: evaṃ yiyāsuḥ guroḥ jñānalakṣaṇāṃ dīkṣāṃ prāpnoti yayā sadya eva mukto bhavati jīvann api atra avalokanāt kathanāt śāstrasambodhanāt caryādarśanāt carudānāt ityādayo bhedāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus one who wishes to approach obtains from the guru an initiation characterized by knowledge, by which he becomes liberated immediately, even while living. Here there are distinctions such as by looking, by speaking, by instruction in scripture, by showing conduct, by giving caru-oblation, and so on.

children.text: abhyāsavato vā tadānīṃ sadya eva prāṇaviyojikāṃ dīkṣāṃ labhate sā tu maraṇakṣaṇa eva kāryā iti vakṣyāma iti ||
children.translated_text: Or, if he has practice, he then immediately receives an initiation that separates him from the vital breath. But that is to be performed only at the moment of death; so we shall explain.

children.text: tīvrās tridhā utkṛṣṭamadhyāt śaktipātāt kṛtadīkṣāko 'pi svātmanaḥ śivatāyāṃ na tathā dṛḍhapratipattiḥ bhavati pratipattiparipākakrameṇa tu dehānte śiva eva madhyamadhyāt tu śivatotsuko 'pi bhogaprepsuḥ bhavati iti tathaiva dīkṣāyāṃ jñānabhājanam sa ca yogābhyāsalabdham anenaiva dehena bhogaṃ bhuktvā dehānte śiva eva ||
children.translated_text: The intense forms are threefold. From the superior middling śaktipāta, even one who has received initiation does not have such firm conviction in the <s>Śiva</s>-nature of his own self; but through the gradual maturation of realization, at the end of the body he is <s>Śiva</s> alone. From the middling middling kind, however, although he is eager for <s>Śiva</s>-nature, he also desires enjoyment; accordingly, at initiation he is a vessel of knowledge, and, having gained yogic practice, he enjoys experience in this very body and at the end of the body is <s>Śiva</s> alone.

children.text: nikṛṣṭamadhyāt tu dehāntareṇa bhogaṃ bhuktvā śivatvam eti iti ||
children.translated_text: From the inferior middling kind, however, after enjoying experience through another body, he reaches <s>Śiva</s>-hood.

children.text: madhyas tu tridhā bhogotsukatā yadā pradhānabhūtā tadā mandatvaṃ pārameśvaramantrayogopāyatayā yatas tatra autsukyam pārameśamantrayogādeś ca yato mokṣaparyantatvam ataḥ śaktipātarūpatā ||
children.translated_text: The middling type is threefold. When eagerness for enjoyment is predominant, then there is weakness, since the eagerness there concerns the means of <s>Parameśvara</s>'s mantra-yoga; and because the yoga of <s>Parameśvara</s>'s mantra and the like culminates in liberation, it has the nature of śaktipāta.

children.text: tatrāpi tāratamyāt traividhyam ity eṣa mukhyaḥ śaktipātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too, because of gradation, there is a threefold division. This is the principal śaktipāta.

children.text: vaiṣṇavādīnāṃ tu rājānugrahavat na mokṣāntatā iti na iha vivecanam ||
children.translated_text: But in the case of Vaiṣṇavas and others, as with royal favor, there is no culmination in liberation; therefore it is not analyzed here.

children.text: śivaśaktyadhiṣṭhānaṃ tu sarvatra iti uktam sā paraṃ jyeṣṭhā na bhavati api tu ghorā ghoratarā vā sa eṣa śaktipāto vicitro 'pi tāratamyavaicitryāt bhidyate kaścid vaiṣṇavādisthaḥ samayyādikrameṇa srotaḥpañcake ca prāptaparipākaḥ sarvottīrṇabhagavatṣaḍardhaśāstraparamādhikāritām eti anyas tu ullaṅghanakrameṇa anantabhedena ko 'pi akramam iti ata eva adharādharaśāsanasthā guravo 'pi iha maṇḍalamātradarśane 'pi anadhikāriṇaḥ ūrdhvaśāsanasthas tu guruḥ adharādharaśāsanaṃ pratyuta prāṇayati pūrṇatvāt iti sarvādhikārī ||
children.translated_text: It has been said, however, that the presiding power of <s>Śiva</s>'s śakti is present everywhere. It is not the supreme Jyeṣṭhā, but rather the Ghorā or Ghoratarā. This śaktipāta, though varied, is divided by the variety of gradation. Some śaktipāta, situated among Vaiṣṇavas and others, after maturing through the sequence beginning with samaya-initiation and in the five streams, reaches the highest eligibility for the all-transcending blessed scripture of the Six-and-a-Half. Another, by a sequence of overstepping with endless distinctions, proceeds in some cases without sequence. Therefore even gurus established in lower and still lower teachings are not qualified here even for the mere sight of the maṇḍala. But a guru established in the higher teaching, because he is complete, can in turn animate the lower and still lower teaching; he is qualified for everything.

children.text: sa ca daiśiko guruḥ ācāryo dīkṣakaḥ cumbakaḥ sa cāyaṃ pūrṇajñāna eva sarvottamaḥ tena vinā dīkṣādyasampatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that instructor-guru is a teacher, initiator, and attractor; being complete in knowledge, he is the best of all, because without him initiation and the rest cannot be accomplished.

children.text: yogī tu phalotsukasya yukto yadi upāyopadeśena avyavahitam eva phalaṃ dātuṃ śaktaḥ upāyopadeśena tu jñāne eva yukto mokṣe 'pi abhyupāyāt jñānapūrṇatākāṅkṣī ca bahūn api gurūn kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: But a yogin is suitable for one who is eager for the result if he is able to give the result immediately through instruction in the means. Through instruction in the means, however, he is suitable only with respect to knowledge, and also with respect to liberation through a secondary means. One who longs for completeness of knowledge may take many gurus.

children.text: uttamottamādijñānabhedāpekṣayā teṣu varteta sampūrṇajñānagurutyāge tu prāyaścittam eva ||
children.translated_text: He should relate to them according to distinctions of knowledge such as best of the best and so on. But if he abandons a guru of complete knowledge, only expiation is appropriate.

children.text: nanu so 'pi abruvan viparītaṃ vā bruvan kiṃ na tyājyaḥ naiva iti brūmaḥ tasya hi pūrṇajñānatvāt eva rāgādyabhāva iti avacanādikaṃ śiṣyagatenaiva kenacit ayogyatvānāśvastatvādinā nimittena syāt iti tadupāsane yatanīyaṃ śiṣyeṇa na tattyāge ||
children.translated_text: Now, one may ask: if even he does not speak, or speaks wrongly, should he not be abandoned? We say: certainly not. For precisely because he has complete knowledge, he is free from passion and the like; therefore his silence and so forth may have some cause in the disciple, such as unfitness or lack of trust. The disciple should therefore strive in service to him, not in abandoning him.

children.text: evam anugrahanimittaṃ śaktipāto nirapekṣa eva karmādiniyatyapekṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Thus śaktipāta, as the cause of grace, is entirely independent, since it does not depend on karma and the like or on destiny.

children.text: tirobhāva iti tirobhāvo hi karmādyapekṣagāḍhaduḥkhamohabhāgitvaphalaḥ yathāhi prakāśasvātantryāt prabuddho 'pi mūḍhavat ceṣṭate hṛdayena ca mūḍhaceṣṭāṃ nindati tathā mūḍho 'pi prabuddhaceṣṭāṃ mantrārādhanādikāṃ kuryāt nindec ca yathā ca asya mūḍhaceṣṭā kriyamāṇāpi prabuddhasya dhvaṃsam eti tathā asya prabuddhaceṣṭā sā tu nindyamānā niṣiddhācaraṇarūpatvāt svayaṃ ca tayaiva viśaṅkamānatvāt enaṃ duḥkhamohapaṅke nimajjayati na tu utpannaśaktipātasya tirobhāvo 'sti atrāpi ca karmādyapekṣā pūrvavat niṣedhyā tatrāpi ca icchāvaicitryāt etad dehamātropabhogyaduḥkhaphalatvaṃ vā dīkṣāsamayacaryāgurudevāgnyādau sevānindanobhayaprasaktānām iva prāk śivaśāsanasthānāṃ tattyāginām iva ||
children.translated_text: Concealment is so called. For concealment has as its result participation in intense suffering and delusion, dependent on karma and the like. Just as, through the freedom of light, even one who is awakened may behave like a fool and, in his heart, condemn foolish behavior, so too even a fool may perform awakened practices such as worship of mantras, and may also condemn them. And just as this foolish behavior, although being done, perishes for the awakened person, so his awakened practice, when it is condemned, because it has the form of doing what is forbidden and because he himself is made apprehensive by that very act, plunges him into the mire of suffering and delusion. But there is no concealment for one in whom <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power) has arisen. Here too, dependence on karma and the like is to be rejected as before. And even there, because of the variety of will, it may have the result of suffering to be experienced in this body alone, as in the case of those formerly established in the <s>Śiva</s>-teaching who become involved in both service and denigration toward initiation, the observances of initiation, the guru, the deity, the fire, and so on, or as in the case of those who abandon that teaching.

children.text: tatrāpi icchāvaicitryāt tirobhūto 'pi svayaṃ vā śaktipātena yujyate mṛto vā bandhugurvādikṛpāmukhena ity evaṃ kṛtyabhāgitvaṃ svātmani anusaṃdadhat parameśvara eva iti na khaṇḍitam ātmānaṃ paśyet ||
children.translated_text: Even there, because of the variety of will, one who has been concealed may either himself be joined with <s>śaktipāta</s>, or after death may be joined with it through the compassion of relatives, the guru, and so on. Thus, while recognizing in himself the condition of being subject to what is to be done, he should see that it is <s>Parameśvara</s> alone, and should not regard himself as fragmented.

children.text: Chapter 12
dīkṣādikaṃ vaktavyam iti uktam ato dīkṣāsvarūpanirūpaṇārthaṃ prāk kartavyaṃ snānam upadiśyate ||
children.translated_text: It was said that initiation and the like must be explained. Therefore, in order to determine the nature of initiation, the bath that is to be performed first is taught.

children.text: snānaṃ ca śuddhatā ucyate śuddhatā ca parameśvarasvarūpasamāveśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And bathing is called purity; and purity is immersion into the nature of <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: kāluṣyāpagamo hi śuddhiḥ kāluṣyaṃ ca tadekarūpe 'pi atatsvabhāvarūpāntarasaṃvalanābhimānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For purity is the removal of impurity; and impurity is the conceit that, although one is of one form with that, there is mixture with another form that is not of that nature.

children.text: tad iha svatantrānandacinmātrasāre svātmani viśvatrāpi vā tadanyarūpasaṃvalanābhimānaḥ aśuddhiḥ sā ca mahābhairavasamāveśena vyapohyate so 'pi kasyacit jhaṭiti bhavet kasyāpi upāyāntaramukhaprekṣī ||
children.translated_text: Thus here, in one's own self, whose essence is free blissful consciousness alone, or in the whole universe, the conceit of mixture with a form other than that is impurity. And that is removed by immersion into <s>Mahābhairava</s>. For some this may occur instantly; for another it waits for the approach of some other means.

children.text: tatrāpi ca ekadvitryādibhedena samastavyastatayā kvacit kasyacit kadācit ca tathā āśvāsopalabdheḥ vicitro bhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And even there, according to distinctions of one, two, three, and so on, collectively or separately, in some case, for some person, and at some time, there is a varied difference because such reassurance is obtained.

children.text: sa ca aṣṭadhā kṣitijalapavanahutāśanākāśasomasūryātmarūpāsu aṣṭāsu mūrtiṣu mantranyāsamahimnā parameśvararūpatayā bhāvitāsu tādātmyena ca dehe parameśvarasamāviṣṭe śarīrādivibhāgavṛtteḥ caitanyasyāpi parameśvarasamāveśaprāptiḥ kasyāpi tu snānavastrādituṣṭijanakatvāt parameśopāyatām etīti uktaṃ ca śrīmadānandādau dhṛtiḥ āpyāyo vīryaṃ maladāho vyāptiḥ sṛṣṭisāmarthyaṃ sthitisāmarthyam abhedaś ca ity etāni teṣu mukhyaphalāni teṣu teṣu upāhitasya mantrasya tattadrūpadhāritvāt ||
children.translated_text: And it is eightfold. In the eight forms whose nature is earth, water, wind, fire, space, moon, sun, and self, when these have been imagined as the form of <s>Parameśvara</s> through the greatness of mantra-installation, and when the body has been entered by <s>Parameśvara</s> through identity with them, then consciousness too, which functions through divisions such as the body, attains immersion into <s>Parameśvara</s>. For someone else, because it produces satisfaction through bathing, clothing, and the like, it becomes a means to the supreme Lord. And it is said in the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and other scriptures: steadiness, refreshment, vigor, burning of impurity, pervasion, capacity for creation, capacity for maintenance, and non-difference are the chief results in those forms, because the mantra placed in each of them bears that particular form.

children.text: vīroddeśena tu viśeṣaḥ tad yathā raṇareṇuḥ vīrāmbhaḥ mahāmarut vīrabhasma śmaśānanabhaḥ tadupahitau candrārkau ātmā nirvikalpakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But there is a special form in relation to the hero. It is as follows: the dust of heroes, the water of heroes, the great wind, the ash of heroes, the cremation-ground sky, the moon and sun conditioned by that, and the self free from conceptual construction.

children.text: punar api bāhyābhyantaratayā dvitvam bahir upāsyamantratādātmyena tanmayīkṛte tatra tatra nimajjanam ity uktam ||
children.translated_text: Again, because it is external and internal, there is a twofold division. Externally, it has been said to be immersion here and there, after each has been made of that nature through identity with the worshiped mantra.

children.text: viśeṣas tu ānandadravyaṃ vīrādhāragataṃ nirīkṣaṇena śivamayīkṛtya tatraiva mantracakrapūjanam tataḥ tenaiva dehaprāṇobhayāśritadevatācakratarpaṇam iti mukhyaṃ snānam ||
children.translated_text: But the special form is this: having made the bliss-substance, situated in the hero's vessel, into <s>Śiva</s> by gazing, one worships the circle of mantras right there; then with that very substance one satisfies the circle of deities abiding in the body, in the vital breath, or in both. This is the chief bath.

children.text: ābhyantaraṃ yathā tattaddharādirūpadhāraṇayā tatra tatra pārthivādau cakre tanmayībhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The internal bath is as follows: through assuming the form of each of those, beginning with earth, there is becoming of that nature in each circle, such as the earthy one.

children.text: Chapter 13

atha prasannahṛdayo yāgasthānaṃ yāyāt tac ca yatraiva hṛdayaṃ prasādayuktaṃ parameśvarasamāveśayogyaṃ bhavati tad eva na tu asya anyal lakṣaṇam uktāv api dhyeyatādātmyam eva kāraṇam tad api bhāvaprasādād eva iti nānyat sthānam ||
children.translated_text: Then, with a clear heart, one should go to the place of sacrifice. And that is precisely wherever the heart becomes clear and fit for immersion into <s>Parameśvara</s>; no other mark of it is stated. Even when stated, identity with what is to be meditated upon alone is the cause, and that too comes only from clarity of disposition. Therefore there is no other place.

children.text: pīṭhaparvatāgram ityādis tu śāstre sthānoddeśa etatpara eva boddhavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the statements in scripture about a sacred seat, a mountaintop, and so on as places should be understood as aimed at this very point.

children.text: teṣu teṣu pīṭhādisthāneṣu parameśaniyatyā parameśvarāviṣṭānāṃ śaktīnāṃ dehagrahaṇāt āryadeśā iva dhārmikāṇāṃ mlecchadeśā iva adhārmikāṇām parvatāgrādeś caikāntatvena vikṣepaparihārāt aikāgryapadatvam iti ||
children.translated_text: In those various places such as sacred seats, because powers entered by <s>Parameśvara</s> have assumed bodies through the order of <s>Parameśvara</s>, just as noble lands do for the righteous and barbarian lands for the unrighteous; and because mountaintops and the like, by their solitude, remove distraction, there is the condition of one-pointedness.

children.text: tatra yāgagṛhāgre bahir eva sāmānyanyāsaṃ kuryāt karayoḥ pūrvaṃ tato dehe ||
children.translated_text: There, outside, in front of the sacrificial house, he should perform the general installation first on the hands and then on the body.

children.text: hrīṃ na pha hrīṃ hrīṃ ā kṣa hrīṃ ity ābhyāṃ śaktiśaktimadvācakābhyāṃ mālinīśabdarāśimantrābhyām ekenaiva ādau śaktiḥ tataḥ śaktimān iti muktau pādāgrāc chiro'ntam bhuktau tu sarvo viparyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With these two <s>Mālinī</s> masses of phonemes and mantras, 'hrīṃ na pha hrīṃ' and 'hrīṃ ā kṣa hrīṃ,' which express power and the possessor of power, by just one of them at first the power is installed and then the possessor of power. For liberation the sequence is from the tips of the feet to the head; but for enjoyment, everything is the reverse.

children.text: mālinī hi bhagavatī mukhyam śāktaṃ rūpaṃ bījayonisaṃghaṭṭena samastakāmadugham ||
children.translated_text: For the blessed <s>Mālinī</s> is the principal śākta form, granting all desires through the union of seed and womb.

children.text: anvarthaṃ caitan nāma rudraśaktimālābhir yuktā phaleṣu puṣpitā saṃsāraśiśirasaṃhāranādabhramarī siddhimokṣadhāriṇī dānādānaśaktiyuktā iti ralayor ekatvasmṛteḥ ||
children.translated_text: And this name is meaningful: she is furnished with garlands of <s>Rudra</s>'s powers, flowered with results, a humming bee whose sound destroys the winter of saṃsāra, bearing accomplishment and liberation, and endowed with the powers of giving and taking, since the unity of ra and la is remembered.

children.text: ata eva hi bhraṣṭavidhir api mantra etannyāsāt pūrṇo bhavati sāñjano 'pi gāruḍavaiṣṇavādir nirañjanatām etya mokṣaprado bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For just this reason, even a mantra whose procedure has been corrupted becomes complete through this <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual installation); and even a sāñjana mantra, such as a <s>Gāruḍa</s> or <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> one, attains the stainless state and becomes a giver of liberation.

children.text: dehanyāsānantaram arghapātre ayam eva nyāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After the bodily <s>nyāsa</s>, this same <s>nyāsa</s> is performed in the arghya vessel.

children.text: iha hi kriyākārakāṇāṃ parameśvarābhedapratipattidārḍhyasiddhaye pūjākriyā udāharaṇīkṛtā tatra ca sarvakārakāṇām itthaṃ parameśvarībhāvaḥ tatra yaṣṭrādhārasya sthānaśuddhyāpādānakaraṇayor arghapātraśuddhinyāsābhyām yaṣṭur dehanyāsāt yājyasya sthaṇḍilādinyāsāt ||
children.translated_text: Here the act of worship has been set forth as an example in order to establish firm recognition of the non-difference of actions and ritual factors from <s>Parameśvara</s>. In it, all ritual factors become forms of the supreme Lord in this way: the support of the sacrificer is made so by the purification of the place; the materials and instruments, by the purification and <s>nyāsa</s> of the arghya vessel; the sacrificer, by bodily <s>nyāsa</s>; and the deity to be worshipped, by <s>nyāsa</s> on the <s>sthaṇḍila</s> altar and the like.

children.text: evaṃ kriyākrameṇāpi parameśvarīkṛtasamastakārakaḥ tayaiva dṛśā sarvakriyāḥ paśyan vināpi pramukhajñānayogābhyāṃ parameśvara eva bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the sequence of ritual action too, one whose entire set of ritual factors has been made divine sees all actions with that very vision and, even without the chief disciplines of knowledge and yoga, becomes <s>Parameśvara</s> himself.

children.text: evam arghapātre nyasya puṣpadhūpādyaiḥ pūjayitvā tadvipruḍbhir yāgasāraṃ puṣpādi ca prokṣayet ||
children.translated_text: Having thus installed it in the arghya vessel and worshipped it with flowers, incense, and the like, he should sprinkle the essence of the sacrifice and the flowers and other offerings with drops from that vessel.

children.text: tataḥ prabhāmaṇḍale bhūmau khe vā oṃ bāhyaparivārāya nama iti pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the circle of radiance, on the ground or in the sky, he should worship, saying, '<s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the outer retinue.'

children.text: tato dvārasthāne oṃ dvāradevatācakrāya nama iti pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: Then at the place of the doorway he should worship, saying, '<s>Oṃ</s>, homage to the circle of doorway deities.'

children.text: agupte tu bahiḥsthāne sati praviśya maṇḍalasthaṇḍilāgra eva bāhyaparivāradvāradevatācakrapūjāṃ pūrvoktaṃ ca nyāsādi kuryāt na bahiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if the outer place is not protected, then after entering he should perform the worship of the outer retinue and the circle of doorway deities, along with the previously stated <s>nyāsa</s> and so on, right in front of the maṇḍala altar, not outside.

children.text: tato 'pi phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ iti astrajaptapuṣpaṃ prakṣipya vighnān apasāritān dhyātvā antaḥ praviśya parameśvarakiraṇeddhayā dṛṣṭyā abhito yāgagṛhaṃ paśyet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after that, throwing a flower empowered by the weapon-mantra while saying '<s>phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ</s>,' and visualizing the obstacles as driven away, he should enter within and look all around the sacrificial chamber with his gaze kindled by the rays of <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: tatra mumukṣur uttarābhimukhas tiṣṭhet yathā bhagavadaghoratejasā jhaṭity eva pruṣṭapāśo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: There the seeker of liberation should stand facing north, so that through the blessed terrible radiance of <s>Aghora</s> his bonds may be burned away at once.

children.text: tatra parameśvarasvātantryam eva mūrtyābhāsanayā diktattvam avabhāsayati ||
children.translated_text: There the very freedom of <s>Parameśvara</s>, by manifesting itself as form, reveals the principle of direction.

children.text: tatra citprakāśa eva madhyaṃ tata itarapravibhāgapravṛtteḥ prakāśasvīkāryam ūrdhvam atathābhūtam adhaḥ prakāśanasammukhīnaṃ pūrvam itarat aparam saṃmukhībhūtaprakāśatvāt anantaraṃ tatprakāśadhārārohasthānaṃ dakṣiṇam ānukūlyāt tatsammukhaṃ tu avabhāsyatvāt uttaram iti dikcatuṣkam ||
children.translated_text: There the light of consciousness itself is the center, since from it the other divisions proceed. What is accepted by the light is above; what is not so is below. What faces illumination is east; the other is west, because it is light that has turned away. Next, the place where the stream of that light rises is south, because it is favorable; and what faces it is north, because it is what is to be illuminated. This is the fourfold set of directions.

children.text: tatra madhye bhagavān ūrdhve 'sya aiśānaṃ vaktram adhaḥ pātālavaktram pūrvādidikcatuṣke śrītatpuruṣāghorasadyovāmākhyaṃ dikcatuṣkamadhye anyāś catasraḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, in the middle, is the Blessed Lord. Above him is the <s>Īśāna</s> face; below is the face of the netherworld. In the four directions beginning with east are the four faces called <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Sadya</s>, and <s>Vāma</s>; and between the four directions are four others.

children.text: ity evaṃ saṃvinmahimaiva mūrtikṛtaṃ digbhedaṃ bhāsayati iti dik na tattvāntaram ||
children.translated_text: Thus it is the very greatness of consciousness that, taking form, manifests the division of directions; direction is not some separate reality.

children.text: yathā yathā ca svacchāyā laṅghayitum iṣṭā satī puraḥ puro bhavati tathā parameśvaramadhyatām eti sarvādhiṣṭhātṛtaiva mādhyasthyam ity uktam ||
children.translated_text: And just as, when one wishes to overstep one's own shadow, it comes to be farther and farther in front, so one attains the centrality of <s>Parameśvara</s>. It has been said that being the ground of all is centrality.

children.text: evaṃ yathā bhagavān digvibhāgakārī tathā sūryo 'pi sa hi pārameśvary eva jñānaśaktir ity uktaṃ tatra tatra tatra pūrvaṃ vyakteḥ pūrvā yatraiva ca tathā tatraiva evaṃ svātmādhīnāpi svasammukhīnasya deśasya purastāttvāt ||
children.translated_text: Just as the Blessed Lord is the maker of directional divisions, so too is the sun; for it has been said that the sun is precisely the knowledge-power belonging to <s>Parameśvara</s>. In each case, what is prior to manifestation is east; and wherever that is so, there alone it is east, since even though it depends on oneself, the region facing oneself has the nature of being in front.

children.text: evaṃ svātmasūryaparameśatritayaikībhāvanayā dikcarcā iti abhinavaguptaguravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by contemplating the unity of the triad consisting of oneself, the sun, and the supreme Lord, there is the discussion of the directions: so say the teachers headed by <s>Abhinavagupta</s>.

children.text: evaṃ sthite uttarābhimukham upaviśya dehapuryaṣṭakādau ahambhāvatyāgena dehatāṃ dahet saṃnidhāv api paradehavat adehatvāt tato nistaraṅgadhruvadhāmarūḍhasya dṛṣṭisvābhāvyāt yā kila ādyā spandakalā saiva mūrtiḥ tadupari yathopadiṣṭayājyadevatācakranyāsaḥ prādhānyena ca iha śaktayo yājyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When this is established, sitting facing north, he should burn away the status of body in the body, the city of the eight constituents, and so forth by abandoning the sense of 'I' in them; for even though it is nearby, it is bodiless, like another's body. Then, because the gaze of one who has ascended into the waveless, fixed abode is naturally such, that very first vibration-power is the form. Upon it is performed, as instructed, the <s>nyāsa</s> of the circle of the deity to be worshipped; and here the powers are chiefly the deities to be worshipped.

children.text: tadāsanatvāt bhagavannavātmādīnāṃ śakter eva ca pūjyatvāt iti guravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because they are the seat of the Blessed <s>Navātman</s> and the others, and because it is <s>Śakti</s> herself who is to be worshipped: so say the teachers.

children.text: tatra ca pañca avasthā jāgradādyāḥ ṣaṣṭhī ca anuttarā nāma svabhāvadaśā anusaṃdheyā ||
children.translated_text: And there the five states beginning with waking, together with the sixth, called <s>anuttarā</s>, the natural condition, are to be kept in contemplative awareness.

children.text: iti ṣoḍhā nyāso bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>nyāsa</s> is sixfold.

children.text: tatra kāraṇānāṃ brahmaviṣṇurudreśasadāśivaśaktirūpāṇāṃ pratyekam adhiṣṭhānāt ṣaṭtriṃśattattvakalāpasya laukikatattvottīrṇasya bhairavabhaṭṭārakābhedavṛtte nyāse pūrṇatvāt bhairavībhāvaḥ tena etat anavakāśam ||
children.translated_text: There, because each of the causes in the forms of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, and <s>Śakti</s> presides over the aggregate of the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>, and because the <s>nyāsa</s> functions as non-different from Lord <s>Bhairava</s>, who transcends worldly <s>tattvas</s>, it is complete and has the nature of <s>Bhairavī</s>. Therefore this objection has no scope.

children.text: yad āhuḥ ataraṅgarūḍhau labdhāyāṃ punaḥ kiṃ tattvasṛṣṭir nyāsādinā iti ||
children.translated_text: For they say: when ascent into the waveless state has been obtained, what further need is there for the creation of <s>tattvas</s> by <s>nyāsa</s> and the like?

children.text: tāvat hi tad ataraṅgaṃ bhairavavapuḥ yat svātmani avabhāsitasṛṣṭisaṃhārāvaicitryakoṭi ||
children.translated_text: For that waveless body of <s>Bhairava</s> extends only so far as the countless variety of creation and dissolution manifested within oneself.

children.text: evam anyonyamelakayogena parameśvarībhūtaṃ prāṇadehabuddhyādi bhāvayitvā bahir antaḥ puṣpadhūpatarpaṇādyair yathāsambhavaṃ pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having contemplated prāṇa, body, intellect, and the rest as made into forms of <s>Parameśvara</s> through the yoga of mutual union, he should worship, outwardly and inwardly, as far as possible with flowers, incense, libations, and the like.

children.text: tatra śarīre prāṇe dhiyi ca tadanusāreṇa śūlābjanyāsaṃ kuryāt tad yathā ādhāraśaktimūle mūlaṃ kanda āmūlasārakaṃ lambikānte kalātattvānto daṇḍaḥ māyātmako granthiḥ catuṣkikātmā śuddhavidyāpadmaṃ tatraiva sadāśivabhaṭṭārakaḥ sa eva mahāpretaḥ prakarṣeṇa līnatvāt bodhāt prādhānyena vedyātmakadehakṣayāt nādāmarśātmakatvāc ca iti ||
children.translated_text: There, in the body, in the vital breath, and in the intellect, according to that sequence, one should perform the installation of the trident and lotus. This is as follows: at the root of the support-power is the root; the bulb is the core extending from the root; up to the end of the uvula is the staff ending in the <s>kalā</s>-<s>tattva</s>; the knot, whose nature is <s>māyā</s>, consists of the tetrad; the pure-knowledge lotus is there itself; there the venerable <s>Sadāśiva</s> abides. He himself is the great corpse, because he is dissolved in the highest degree, because from awakening there is chiefly the destruction of the knowable-formed body, and because he has the nature of the vibration of sound.

children.text: tan nābhyutthitaṃ tanmūrdharandhratrayanirgataṃ nādāntarvartiśaktivyāpinīsamanārūpamarātrayaṃ dviṣaṭkāntaṃ tadupari śuddhapadmatrayam aunmanasam etasmin viśvamaye bhede āsanīkṛte adhiṣṭhātṛtayā vyāpakabhāvena ādheyabhūtāṃ yathābhimatāṃ devatāṃ kalpayitvā yat tatraiva samasvabhāvanirbharātmani viśvabhāvārpaṇaṃ tad eva pūjanaṃ yad eva tanmayībhavanaṃ tad dhyānaṃ yat tathāvidhāntaḥparāmarśasadbhāvanādāndolanaṃ sa japaḥ yat tathāvidhaparāmarśakramaprabuddhamahātejasā tathābalād eva viśvātmīkaraṇaṃ sa homaḥ tad evaṃ kṛtvā parivāraṃ tata eva vahnirāśer visphuliṅgavat dhyātvā tathaiva pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: That, risen from the navel and issuing through the three apertures in the crown of the head, consists of the three powers abiding within sound, namely <s>Vyāpinī</s>, <s>Samanā</s>, and <s>Unmanā</s>; it ends at the two sets of six. Above it are the three pure lotuses and the state beyond mind. When this difference, which consists of the universe, has been made into a seat, one should imagine there, as the presiding power and in an all-pervading mode, the desired deity as that which is supported. The offering of the universe into that very deity, whose self is full of the equal nature, is worship. Becoming identical with that deity is meditation. The movement of the gift of the real presence of such inward reflective awareness is japa. The making of everything into the self, by the great radiance awakened through the sequence of such reflective awareness and by that very force, is homa. Having done this, one should meditate on the retinue as arising from that very mass of fire like sparks, and should worship it in the same way.

children.text: dvādaśāntam idaṃ prāgraṃ viśūlaṃ mūlataḥ smaran ||
children.translated_text: Remembering this twelve-ended, forward-pointed, trident-free form from the root,

children.text: devīcakrāgragaṃ tyaktakramaḥ khecaratāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: one should reach the state of moving in the sky, having abandoned sequence and gone to the summit of the circle of goddesses.

children.text: mūlādhārād dviṣaṭkāntavyomāgrāpūraṇātmikā ||
children.translated_text: It has the nature of filling from the <s>mūlādhāra</s> up to the sky at the end of the two sets of six.

children.text: khecarīyaṃ khasaṃcāram sthitibhyāṃ khāmṛtāśanāt ||
children.translated_text: This is <s>khecarī</s>, because of moving in space, because of its states, and because of feeding on the nectar of space.

children.text: evam antaryāgamātrād eva vastutaḥ kṛtakṛtyatā ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by internal worship alone, in truth, all that is to be done has been accomplished.

children.text: satyataḥ tadāviṣṭasya tathāpi bahir api kāryo yāgo 'vacchedahānaya eva yo 'pi tathā samāveśabhāk na bhavati tasya mukhyo bahiryāgaḥ tadabhyāsāt samāveśalābho yatas tasyāpi tu paśutātirodhānāyāntaryāgaḥ tadarūḍhāv api tatsaṃkalpabalasya śuddhipradatvāt ||
children.translated_text: For one who is truly possessed by that, nevertheless external worship too should be performed precisely for the removal of limitation. For one who does not share in such absorption, external worship is primary, since through practice of it absorption is obtained. Yet for him too internal worship is for the concealment of his bound-animal condition, because even when he has not ascended to it, the force of its intention gives purification.

children.text: atha yadā dīkṣāṃ cikīrṣet tadādhivāsanārthaṃ bhūmiparigrahaṃ gaṇeśārcanaṃ kumbhakalaśayoḥ pūjāṃ sthaṇḍilārcanaṃ havanaṃ ca kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Now, when he wishes to perform initiation, then, for the sake of preliminary consecration, he should undertake the taking possession of the ground, the worship of <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, the worship of the pot and water-vessel, the worship of the altar, and the fire offering.

children.text: nityanaimittikayos tu sthaṇḍilādyarcanahavane eva ||
children.translated_text: But in the regular and occasional rites, only the worship of the altar and related rites, and the fire offering, are required.

children.text: tatra adhivāsanaṃ śiṣyasya saṃskṛtayogyatādhānam amblīkaraṇam iva dantānāṃ devasya kartavyonmukhatvagrāhaṇam guros tadgrahaṇam ||
children.translated_text: There, preliminary consecration is the imparting to the disciple of fitness for sanctification, like the souring of teeth; it is making the deity apprehend an orientation toward what is to be done, and the guru's receiving of that.

children.text: upakaraṇadravyāṇāṃ yāgagṛhāntarvartitayā parameśatejobṛṃhaṇena pūjopakaraṇayogyatārpaṇam iti ||
children.translated_text: For the auxiliary substances, it is the bestowal of fitness as worship implements, since they are within the sacrificial house and are strengthened by the radiance of <s>Parameśa</s>.

children.text: tatra sarvopakaraṇapūrṇaṃ yāgagṛhaṃ vidhāya bhagavatīṃ mālinīṃ mātṛkāṃ vā smṛtvā tadvarṇatejaḥpuñjabharitaṃ gṛhītaṃ bhāvayan puṣpāñjaliṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: There, having prepared a sacrificial house filled with all the implements, and having remembered the blessed <s>Mālinī</s> or <s>Mātṛkā</s>, one should cast a handful of flowers while visualizing it as grasped and filled with the mass of radiance of her phonemes.

children.text: tata uktāstrajaptāni yathāsambhavaṃ siddhārthadhānyākṣatalājādīni tejorūpāṇi vikīrya aiśānyāṃ diśi krameṇa saṃghaṭṭayet iti bhūparigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having scattered, as far as possible, mustard seeds, grain, unbroken rice, parched grain, and the like, which have been recited over with the stated weapon-mantra and are forms of radiance, one should gradually gather them together in the northeastern direction. This is the taking possession of the ground.

children.text: tataḥ śuddhavidyāntam āsanaṃ dattvā gaṇapateḥ pūjā tataḥ kumbham ānandadravyapūritam alaṃkṛtaṃ pūjayet tato yājyam anu pūgaṃ nyasya tatra mukhyaṃ mantraṃ sarvādhiṣṭhātṛtayā vidhipūrvakatvena smaran aṣṭottaraśatamantritaṃ tena taṃ kumbhaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, having given a seat up to pure knowledge, there is the worship of <s>Gaṇapati</s>. Next one should worship the decorated pot filled with bliss-substance. Then, after placing betel-nut after the sacrificer, remembering the principal mantra there as the presiding power of all and as being according to rule, one should make that pot empowered by one hundred and eight recitations of that mantra.

children.text: dvitīyakalaśe vighnaśamanāya astraṃ yajet ||
children.translated_text: In the second vessel one should worship the weapon-mantra for the pacification of obstacles.

children.text: tataḥ svasvadikṣu lokapālān sāstrān pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: Then one should worship the guardians of the worlds, together with their weapons, in their respective directions.

children.text: tataḥ śiṣyasya prāk dīkṣitasya haste astrakalaśaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Then he should give the weapon-vessel into the hand of the disciple who has previously been initiated.

children.text: svayaṃ ca guruḥ kumbham ādadīta ||
children.translated_text: And the guru himself should take up the pot.

children.text: tataḥ śiṣyaṃ gṛhaparyanteṣu vighnaśamanāya dhārāṃ pātayantaṃ sakumbho 'nugacchet imaṃ mantraṃ paṭhan bho bhoḥ śakra tvayā svasyāṃ diśi vighnapraśāntaye ||
children.translated_text: Then, carrying the pot, he should follow the disciple as he pours a stream around the edges of the house for the pacification of obstacles, reciting this mantra: 'Ho, ho, <s>Śakra</s>, in your own direction, for the pacification of obstacles,

children.text: sāvadhānena karmāntaṃ bhavitavyaṃ śivājñayā ||
children.translated_text: you must remain attentive until the end of the rite, by the command of <s>Śiva</s>.'

children.text: tryakṣare nāmni bho ity ekam eva ||
children.translated_text: In the three-syllable name, the single word 'bho' is used.

children.text: tata aiśānyāṃ diśi kumbhaṃ sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Then he should place the pot in the northeastern direction.

children.text: vikiropari astrakalaśam ||
children.translated_text: The weapon-vessel should be placed above the scattered grains.

children.text: tata ubhayapūjanam ||
children.translated_text: Then there is the worship of both.

children.text: tataḥ sthaṇḍilamadhye parameśapūjanam ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the middle of the altar, there is the worship of <s>Parameśa</s>.

children.text: tataḥ agnikuṇḍaṃ parameśvaraśaktirūpatayā bhāvayitvā tatra agniṃ prajvālya hṛdayāntarbodhāgninā saha ekīkṛtya mantraparāmarśasāhityena jvalantaṃ śivāgniṃ bhāvayitvā tatra nyasya abhyarcya mantrān tarpayet ājyena tilaiś ca ||
children.translated_text: Then, having contemplated the fire-pit as the form of the power of <s>Parameśvara</s>, kindled the fire there, united it with the fire of awareness within the heart, and contemplated the blazing <s>Śiva</s>-fire accompanied by the reflective awareness of mantra, he should install it there, worship it, and satisfy the mantras with clarified butter and sesame seeds.

children.text: arghapātreṇa ca prokṣaṇam eva tilājyādīnāṃ saṃskāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the consecration of sesame seeds, clarified butter, and the like is simply sprinkling them with the argha-vessel.

children.text: sruksruvayoś ca parameśābhedadṛṣṭir eva hi saṃskāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, the consecration of the offering ladle and spoon is just the vision that they are non-different from <s>Parameśa</s>.

children.text: tato yathāśakti hutvā sruksruvau ūrdhvādhomukhatayā śaktiśivarūpau parasparonmukhau vidhāya samapādotthito dvādaśāntagaganoditaśivapūrṇacandraniḥsṛtapatatparāmṛtadhārābhāvanāṃ kurvan vauṣaḍantaṃ mantram uccārayan ca ājyakṣayāntaṃ tiṣṭhet iti pūrṇāhutiḥ mantracakrasaṃtarpaṇī ||
children.translated_text: Then, having offered oblations according to his ability, he should arrange the ladle and offering-spoon as the forms of <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śiva</s>, one facing upward and the other downward, turned toward each other. Standing with his feet together, meditating on the stream of supreme nectar falling and flowing out from the full moon of <s>Śiva</s> arisen in the sky at the dvādaśānta, and uttering the mantra ending in vauṣaṭ, he should remain until the ghee is exhausted. This is the full oblation, which satisfies the circle of mantras.

children.text: tataś caruṃ prokṣitam ānīya sthaṇḍilakalaśakumbhavahniṣu bhāgaṃ bhāgaṃ nivedya ekabhāgam avaśeṣya śiṣyāya bhāgaṃ dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, bringing the sprinkled caru-oblation, he should offer a portion each to the altar-ground, the kalaśa, the kumbha, and the fire; leaving one portion aside, he should give a portion to the disciple.

children.text: tato dantakāṣṭham ||
children.translated_text: Then the tooth-stick.

children.text: tatpāto 'gniyamanirṛtidikṣu adhaś ca na śubha iti ||
children.translated_text: If its fall is toward the directions of Agni, Yama, or Nirṛti, or downward, that is not auspicious.

children.text: tatra homo 'stramantreṇa kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There an oblation should be performed with the weapon-mantra.

children.text: tato vikṣepaparihāreṇa bhāvimantradarśanayogyatāyai baddhanetraṃ śiṣyaṃ praveśya jānusthitaṃ taṃ kṛtvā puṣpāñjaliṃ kṣepayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, for the removal of distraction and in order that he may become fit for the future vision of the mantra, he should bring in the disciple with his eyes bound, make him kneel, and have him cast a handful of flowers.

children.text: tataḥ sahasā apāsitanetrabandho 'sau śaktipātānugṛhītakaraṇatvāt saṃnihitamantraṃ tatsthānaṃ sākṣātkāreṇa paśyan tanmayo bhavati anugṛhītakaraṇānāṃ mantrasaṃnidhiḥ pratyakṣaḥ yatas trasyatām iva bhūtānām ||
children.translated_text: Then, when his eye-bandage has suddenly been removed, because his faculties have been favored by <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power), he sees directly the present mantra and its place, and becomes identical with it; for to those whose faculties have been favored, the presence of the mantra is perceptible, just as the presence of beings is to those who are frightened.

children.text: tataḥ svadakṣiṇahaste dīpyatayā devatācakraṃ pūjayitvā taṃ hastaṃ mūrdhahṛnnābhiṣu śiṣyasya pāśān dahantaṃ nikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after worshiping the circle of deities in his own right hand as blazing, he should place that hand on the disciple's head, heart, and navel, burning up his bonds.

children.text: tato vāme somyatayā pūjayitvā śuddhatattvāpyāyinaṃ tataḥ praṇāmaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, after worshiping in the left hand as gentle and as nourishing the pure <s>tattvas</s>, he should have him make obeisance.

children.text: tato bhūtadevatādigbaliṃ madyamāṃsajalādipūrṇaṃ bahir dadyāt ācāmeta ||
children.translated_text: Then he should give outside a bali-offering to the beings, deities, and directions, filled with wine, meat, water, and the like, and should sip water.

children.text: tataḥ svayaṃ carubhojanaṃ kṛtvā śiṣyātmanā saha aikyam āpannaḥ prabuddhavṛttiḥ tiṣṭhet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having himself eaten the caru-oblation, he should remain with awakened awareness, having attained unity with the disciple's self.

children.text: svapan api prabhāte śiṣyaḥ cet aśubhaṃ svapnaṃ vadet tat asmai na vyākuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Even if the disciple, after sleeping, tells of an inauspicious dream in the morning, he should not interpret it for him.

children.text: śaṅkātaṅkau hi tathāsya syātām kevalam astreṇa tanniṣkṛtiṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: For doubt and anxiety would arise in him in that way; he should merely perform its expiation with the weapon-mantra.

children.text: tatas tathaiva parameśvaraṃ pūjayitvā tadagre śiṣyasya prāṇakrameṇa praviśya hṛtkaṇṭhatālulalāṭarandhradvādaśānteṣu ṣaṭsu kāraṇaṣaṭkasparśaṃ kurvan pratyekam aṣṭau saṃskārān cintayan kaṃcit kālaṃ śiṣyaprāṇaṃ tatraiva viśramayya punar avarohet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having worshiped <s>Parameśvara</s> in the same way, before him he should enter the disciple by the sequence of the vital breath. Touching the six places, the heart, throat, palate, forehead, aperture, and dvādaśānta, with the sixfold group of causes, and contemplating eight sacraments in each, he should let the disciple's breath rest there for some time and then descend again.

children.text: ity evāpāditāṣṭācatvāriṃśatsaṃskāroparikṛtarudrāṃśāpattiḥ samayībhavati ||
children.translated_text: In this way, having been furnished with forty-eight sacraments and having attained a portion of <s>Rudra</s> placed above, he becomes a samayin.

children.text: tataḥ asmai pūjyaṃ mantraṃ puṣpādyaiḥ saha arpayet ||
children.translated_text: Then he should offer to him the mantra to be worshiped, together with flowers and the like.

children.text: tataḥ samayān asmai nirūpayet ||
children.translated_text: Then he should set forth the samayas for him.

children.text: gurau sarvātmanā bhaktiḥ tathā śāstre deve tatpratidvaṃdvini parāṅmukhatā guruvat guruputrādeḥ vidyāsambandhakṛtasya tatpūrvadīkṣitādeḥ saṃdarśanam yaunasambandhasya tadārādhanārtham na tu svata iti mantavyam ||
children.translated_text: There should be devotion to the guru with one's whole self, and likewise to the scripture and the deity; turning away from what opposes them; regard for the guru's son and others as for the guru, for those connected by the vidyā, and for those initiated before him; and sexual relations are to be considered as for the purpose of propitiating that, not for their own sake.

children.text: striyo vandhyāyās tajjugupsāhetuṃ na kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: He should not do anything to women, even to a barren woman, that would be a cause of disgust toward her.

children.text: devatānāma gurunāma tathā mantraṃ pūjākālāt ṛte na uccārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should not utter the names of deities, the name of the guru, or the mantra, except at the time of worship.

children.text: gurūpabhuktaṃ śayyādi na bhuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: He should not use a bed or the like used by the guru.

children.text: yat kiṃcit laukikaṃ krīḍādi tat gurusaṃnidhau na kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: He should not perform any worldly amusement, games, or the like in the presence of the guru.

children.text: tadvyatirekeṇa na anyatra utkarṣabuddhiṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Apart from him, he should not form the idea of superiority anywhere else.

children.text: sarvatra śrāddhādau gurum eva pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: Everywhere, at śrāddha rites and the like, he should worship the guru alone.

children.text: sarveṣu ca naimittikeṣu śākinītyādiśabdān na vadet ||
children.translated_text: And in all occasional rites he should not utter words such as śākinī.

children.text: parvadināni pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: He should perform worship on festival days.

children.text: vaiṣṇavādyair adhodṛṣṭibhiḥ saha saṃgatiṃ na kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: He should not associate with Vaiṣṇavas and others whose vision is lower.

children.text: etacchāsanasthān pūrvajātibuddhyā na paśyet ||
children.translated_text: He should not look upon those established in this teaching with ideas based on their former birth-caste.

children.text: guruvarge gṛhāgate yathāśakti yāgaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: When the guru's circle has come to his house, he should perform sacrifice according to his ability.

children.text: adhomārgasthitaṃ kaṃcit vaiṣṇavādyaṃ tacchāstrakulāt gurūkṛtyāpi tyajet ||
children.translated_text: He should abandon anyone situated on a lower path, such as a Vaiṣṇava, even if that person has been made a guru by the family of that scripture.

children.text: tadāpi na utkarṣabuddhyā paśyet ||
children.translated_text: Even then he should not look upon him with an idea of superiority.

children.text: liṅgibhiḥ saha samācāramelanaṃ na kuryāt tān kevalaṃ yathāśakti pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: He should not mingle in conduct with liṅgins; he should merely worship them according to his ability.

children.text: śaṅkās tyajet ||
children.translated_text: He should abandon doubts.

children.text: cakre sthitaś caramāgryādivibhāgaṃ janmakṛtaṃ na saṃkalpayet ||
children.translated_text: When standing in the circle, he should not conceive divisions such as lowest and highest that are produced by birth.

children.text: śarīrāt ṛte na anyat āyatanatīrthādikaṃ bahumānena paśyet ||
children.translated_text: Apart from the body, he should not look with great reverence upon any other shrine, sacred ford, or the like.

children.text: mantrahṛdayam anavarataṃ smaret ity evaṃ śiṣyaḥ śrutvā praṇamya abhyupagamya guruṃ dhanadāraśarīraparyantayā dakṣiṇayā paritoṣya pūrvadīkṣitāṃś ca dīnānāthādikān tarpayet ||
children.translated_text: He should constantly remember the heart of the mantra. Having heard this, bowed, accepted it, and satisfied the guru with a fee extending to wealth, wife, and body, the disciple should also gratify those initiated before him, and the poor, the helpless, and others.

children.text: bhāvividhinā ca mūrticakraṃ tarpayet ||
children.translated_text: And by the procedure to be stated later he should satisfy the circle of embodied deities.

children.text: itthaṃ samayībhavati ||
children.translated_text: In this way he becomes a samayin.

children.text: mantrābhyāse nityapūjāyāṃ śravaṇe 'dhyayane adhikārī naimittike tu sarvatra gurum eva abhyarthayet ||
children.translated_text: He is qualified for mantra-practice, daily worship, hearing, and study; but in all occasional rites he should request the guru alone.

children.text: iti sāmayiko vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the procedure for a samayin.

children.text: Chapter 14
atha putrakadīkṣāvidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, the procedure for putraka-initiation.

children.text: sa ca vistīrṇaḥ tantrālokāt avadhāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that, in its extended form, is to be ascertained from the <s>Tantrāloka</s>.

children.text: saṃkṣiptas tu ucyate ||
children.translated_text: But the concise form is now stated.

children.text: samayyantaṃ vidhiṃ kṛtvā tṛtīye 'hni triśūlābje maṇḍale sāmudāyikaṃ yāgaṃ pūjayet tatra bāhyaparivāraṃ dvāradevatācakraṃ ca bahiḥ pūjayet tato maṇḍalapūrvabhāge aiśakoṇāt ārabhya āgneyāntaṃ paṅktikrameṇa gaṇapatiṃ guruṃ paramaguruṃ parameṣṭhinaṃ pūrvācāryān yoginīcakraṃ vāgīśvarīṃ kṣetrapālaṃ ca pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the rite that ends the <s>samaya</s> observance, on the third day, in the trident-lotus maṇḍala, he should worship the communal sacrifice. There he should worship outside the external retinue and the circle of doorway deities. Then, in the eastern part of the maṇḍala, beginning from the north-eastern corner and ending at the south-eastern, in row order, he should worship <s>Gaṇapati</s>, the guru, the guru's guru, the supreme teacher, the former teachers, the circle of yoginīs, <s>Vāgīśvarī</s>, and <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>.

children.text: tata ājñāṃ samucitām ādāya śūlamūlāt prabhṛti sitakamalāntaṃ samastam adhvānaṃ nyasya arcayet tato madhyame triśūle madhyārāyāṃ bhagavatī śrīparābhaṭṭārikā bhairavanāthena saha vāmārāyāṃ tathaiva śrīmadaparā dakṣiṇārāyāṃ śrīparāparā dakṣiṇe triśūle madhye śrīparāparā vāme triśūle madhye śrīmadaparā dve tu yathāsvam ||
children.translated_text: Then, having received the appropriate permission, he should install the entire <s>adhvan</s> (cosmic course), from the base of the trident up to the white lotus, and worship it. Then, on the middle trident, on the middle spoke, is the blessed goddess <s>Śrīparābhaṭṭārikā</s> together with lord <s>Bhairava</s>; on the left spoke, likewise, <s>Śrīmadaparā</s>; on the right spoke, <s>Śrīparāparā</s>; on the right trident, in the middle, <s>Śrīparāparā</s>; on the left trident, in the middle, <s>Śrīmadaparā</s>; the two are according to their own proper places.

children.text: evaṃ sarvasthānādhiṣṭhātṛtve bhagavatyāḥ sarvaṃ pūrṇaṃ tadadhiṣṭhānāt bhavati iti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, because the goddess presides over all places, everything becomes complete through her presiding presence.

children.text: tato madhyaśūlamadhyārāyāṃ samastaṃ devatācakraṃ lokapālāstraparyantam abhinnatayaiva pūjayet tadadhiṣṭhānāt sarvatra pūjitam ||
children.translated_text: Then, on the middle spoke of the middle trident, he should worship the whole circle of deities, down to the world-protectors and weapons, precisely as non-different. Because of her presiding presence, it is worshiped everywhere.

children.text: tataḥ kumbhe kalaśe maṇḍale agnau svātmani ca abhedabhāvanayā pañcādhikaraṇam anusaṃdhiṃ kuryāt tataḥ parameśvarādvayarasabṛṃhitena puṣpādinā viśeṣapūjāṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the pot, the pitcher, the maṇḍala, the fire, and his own self, he should make the fivefold support-reflection through contemplation of non-difference. After that he should perform the special worship with flowers and the like, strengthened by the savor of the nondual supreme Lord.

children.text: kiṃ bahunā tarpaṇanaivedyaparipūrṇaṃ vittaśāṭhyavirahito yāgasthānaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: In short, without stinginess regarding wealth, he should make the place of sacrifice complete with libations and food-offerings.

children.text: asati vitte tu mahāmaṇḍalayāgo na kartavya eva ||
children.translated_text: But if there is no wealth, the great maṇḍala sacrifice simply should not be performed.

children.text: paśūṃś ca jīvato nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: And he should offer the sacrificial animals while they are alive.

children.text: te 'pi hi evam anugṛhītā bhavanti iti kāruṇikatayā paśuvidhau na vicikitset ||
children.translated_text: For they too, being favored in this way, receive grace; therefore, out of compassion, one should not hesitate over the rule concerning animals.

children.text: tato 'gnau parameśvaraṃ tilājyādibhiḥ saṃtarpya tadagre 'nyaṃ paśuṃ vapāhomārthaṃ kuryāt devatācakraṃ tadvapayā tarpayet punar maṇḍalaṃ pūjayet tataḥ parameśvaraṃ vijñapya sarvābhinnasamastaṣaḍadhvaparipūrṇam ātmānaṃ bhāvayitvā śiṣyaṃ puro 'vasthitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, having satisfied <s>Parameśvara</s> in the fire with sesame, ghee, and the like, he should place another animal before it for the purpose of the omentum-offering; he should satisfy the circle of deities with its omentum, and again worship the maṇḍala. Then, after informing <s>Parameśvara</s>, and having contemplated himself as complete with all the six <s>adhvans</s> that are non-different from everything, he should place the disciple before him.

children.text: parokṣadīkṣāyāṃ jīvanmṛtarūpāyām agre taṃ dhyāyet tadīyāṃ vā pratikṛtiṃ darbhagomayādimayīm agre sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: In indirect initiation, whether for one living or dead, he should first meditate on that person, or place in front of him an image of that person made of darbha grass, cow-dung, and the like.

children.text: tathāvidhaṃ śiṣyam arghapātravipruṭprokṣitaṃ puṣpādibhiś ca pūjitaṃ kṛtvā samastam adhvānaṃ taddehe nyaset ||
children.translated_text: Having made such a disciple sprinkled with drops from the argha-vessel and worshiped with flowers and the like, he should install the entire <s>adhvan</s> in that disciple's body.

children.text: tata itthaṃ vicārayet bhogecchoḥ śubhaṃ na śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Then he should consider in this way: for one who desires enjoyment, he should not purify the auspicious.

children.text: mumukṣos tu śubhāśubham ubhayam api ||
children.translated_text: But for one who desires liberation, he should purify both the auspicious and the inauspicious.

children.text: nirbījāyāṃ tu samayapāśān api śodhayet sā ca āsannamaraṇasya atyantamūrkhasyāpi kartavyā iti parameśvarājñā tasyāpi tu gurudevatāgnibhaktiniṣṭhatvamātrāt siddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the seedless initiation, he should also purify the bonds of <s>samaya</s>; and that is to be performed even for one who is near death or utterly foolish. This is the command of <s>Parameśvara</s>. Even for such a person, success comes merely from steadfast devotion to the guru, the deity, and the fire.

children.text: atra ca sarvatra vāsanāgrahaṇam eva bhedakam mantrāṇāṃ vāsanānuguṇyena tattatkāryakāritvāt ||
children.translated_text: And here, everywhere, the grasping of the intentional conception alone is what differentiates, because mantras perform their respective functions in accordance with the intentional conception.

children.text: evaṃ vāsanābhedam anusaṃdhāya mukhyamantraparāmarśaviśeṣeṇa samastam adhvānaṃ svadehagataṃ śivādvayabhāvanayā śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having attended to the difference of intentional conceptions, by a particular reflective application of the chief mantra he should purify the entire <s>adhvan</s> located in his own body through contemplation of nondual <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: evaṃ krameṇa pādāṅguṣṭhāt prabhṛti dvādaśāntaparyantaṃ svātmadehasvātmacaitanyābhinnīkṛtadehacaitanyasya śiṣyasya āsādya tatraiva anantānandasarasi svātantryaiśvaryasāre samastecchājñānakriyāśaktinirbharasamastadevatācakreśvare samastādhvabharite cinmātrāvaśeṣaviśvabhāvamaṇḍale tathāvidharūpaikīkāreṇa śiṣyātmanā saha ekībhūto viśrāntim āsādayet ity evaṃ parameśvarābhinno 'sau bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In this sequence, from the big toe up to the twelve-finger limit, he should reach the disciple whose body-consciousness has been made non-different from his own self, body, and self-consciousness; and right there, in the lake of infinite bliss, in the essence of the sovereign freedom of autonomy, in the lord of the whole circle of deities filled with all powers of will, knowledge, and action, in the maṇḍala of world-being filled with all the <s>adhvans</s> and leaving only pure consciousness, through unification with such a form, he should reach repose, having become one with the self of the disciple. In this way that disciple becomes non-different from <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: tato yadi bhogecchuḥ syāt tato yatraiva tattve bhogecchā asya bhavati tatraiva samastavyastatayā yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, if he is one who desires enjoyment, he should yoke him, collectively and distributively, precisely to whatever <s>tattva</s> in which his desire for enjoyment exists.

children.text: tadanantaraṃ śeṣavṛttaye parameśvarasvabhāvāt jhaṭiti prasṛtaṃ śuddhatattvamayaṃ deham asmai cintayet ity eṣā samastapāśaviyojikā dīkṣā ||
children.translated_text: Immediately after that, for the remaining course of life, he should imagine for him a body made of pure <s>tattva</s>, suddenly issued from the nature of <s>Parameśvara</s>. This is the initiation that separates one from all bonds.

children.text: tataḥ śiṣyo guruṃ dakṣiṇābhiḥ pūrvavat pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: Then the disciple should worship the guru with honoraria as before.

children.text: tato 'gnau śiṣyasya vidhiṃ kuryāt śrīparāmantraḥ amukasyāmukaṃ tattvaṃ śodhayāmi iti svāhāntaṃ pratitattvaṃ tisra āhutayaḥ ante pūrṇā vauṣaḍantā ||
children.translated_text: Then he should perform the rite for the disciple in the fire: with the <s>Śrīparā</s> mantra, saying, 'I purify such-and-such a <s>tattva</s> of so-and-so,' ending with svāhā, there are three oblations for each <s>tattva</s>; at the end there is the full oblation ending with vauṣaṭ.

children.text: evaṃ śivāntatattvaśuddhiḥ tato yojanikoktakrameṇa pūrṇāhutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus there is purification of the <s>tattvas</s> up to <s>Śiva</s>; then comes the full oblation according to the sequence stated in the yojanikā.

children.text: bhogecchoḥ bhogasthāne yojanikārtham aparā śuddhatattvasṛṣṭyartham anyā ||
children.translated_text: For one who desires enjoyment, there is one further oblation for the purpose of yoking him to the place of enjoyment, and another for the creation of a pure-<s>tattva</s> body.

children.text: tato guroḥ dakṣiṇābhiḥ pūjanam ity eṣā putrakadīkṣā ||
children.translated_text: Then there is worship of the guru with honoraria. This is the <s>putraka-dīkṣā</s> (initiation as a spiritual son).

children.text: yatra vartamānam ekaṃ varjayitvā bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyac ca karma śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: In it, except for the single karma now being experienced, past and future karma are purified.

children.text: Chapter 15
yadā punar āsannamaraṇasya svayaṃ vā bandhumukhena śaktipāta upajāyate tadā asmai sadyaḥ samutkramaṇadīkṣāṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: But when, for one near death, <s>śaktipāta</s> arises either directly in him or through the mouth of a relative, then one should perform for him the immediate <s>samutkramaṇa-dīkṣā</s> (initiation for upward departure).

children.text: samastam adhvānaṃ śiṣye nyasya taṃ ca krameṇa śodhayitvā bhagavatīṃ kālarātrīm marmakartanīṃ nyasya tayā kramāt kramaṃ marmapāśān vibhidya brahmarandhravarti śiṣyacaitanyaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Having placed the entire path in the disciple and purified him step by step, he should install the goddess <s>Kālarātrī</s>, the cutter of vital points; and with her, in due sequence, he should pierce the bonds at the vital points and make the disciple's consciousness abide in the aperture of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: tataḥ pūrvoktakrameṇa yojanikārthaṃ pūrṇāhutiṃ dadyāt yathā pūrṇāhutyante jīvo niṣkrāntaḥ paramaśivābhinno bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Then, for the sake of conjunction, he should offer the full oblation according to the procedure stated earlier, so that at the end of the full oblation the individual soul, having gone forth, becomes non-different from <s>Paramaśiva</s>.

children.text: bubhukṣos tu dvitīyā pūrṇāhutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But for one who seeks enjoyment, there is a second full oblation.

children.text: bhogasthāne yojanāya tatkāle ca tasya jīvalayaḥ nātra śeṣavartanam brahmavidyāṃ vā karṇe paṭhet sā hi parāmarśasvabhāvā sadyaḥ prabuddhapaśucaitanye prabuddhavimarśaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: It is for conjunction with the place of enjoyment; at that time his individual soul dissolves there, and there is no remaining activity here. Or he should recite the <s>Brahmavidyā</s> in his ear, for it has the nature of reflective awareness and at once produces awakened reflective awareness in the animal-bound consciousness that has been awakened.

children.text: samayyāder api ca etatpāṭhe 'dhikāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: And even a samayin and the like have authority to recite this.

children.text: sapratyayāṃ nirbījāṃ tu yadi dīkṣāṃ mūḍhāya āyātaśaktipātāya ca darśayet tadā hi śivahastadānakāle ayaṃ vidhiḥ trikoṇam āgneyaṃ jvālākarālaṃ rephavisphuliṅgaṃ bahirvātyācakradhyāyamānaṃ maṇḍalaṃ dakṣiṇahaste cintayitvā tatraiva haste bījaṃ kiṃcit nikṣipya ūrdhvādhorephavibodhitaphaṭkāraparamparābhiḥ asya tāṃ jananaśaktiṃ dahet evaṃ kurvan taṃ hastaṃ śiṣyasya mūrdhani kṣipet iti dvayor api eṣā dīkṣā nirbījā svakāryakaraṇasāmarthyavidhvaṃsinī bhavati sthāvarāṇām api dīkṣyatvena uktatvāt vāyupurāntarvyavasthitaṃ dodhūyamānaṃ śiṣyaṃ laghūbhūtaṃ cintayet yena tulayā laghuḥ dṛśyate iti ||
children.translated_text: But if he should show an initiation that is sapratyaya and nirbīja to a deluded person in whom the descent of power has occurred, then this is the procedure at the time of giving the hand of <s>Śiva</s>: having visualized in his right hand a triangular fiery maṇḍala, terrible with flames, sparkling with the syllable repha, and contemplated as encircled outside by a whirling wind-wheel, and having placed some seed in that very hand, he should burn that person's power of generation by successive utterances of phaṭ awakened by upward and downward rephas. Doing this, he should place that hand on the disciple's head. Thus, for both of them, this initiation is nirbīja, destroying the capacity to perform its own function. Since even immobile beings are said to be fit for initiation, he should visualize the disciple as situated within the enclosure of wind, trembling, and made light, so that he appears light on a balance.

children.text: Chapter 16
atha parokṣasya dīkṣā dvividhaś ca saḥ mṛto jīvaṃś ca ||
children.translated_text: Now, indirect initiation is twofold: the person is either dead or living.

children.text: tatra kṛtaguruseva eva mṛta udvāsito vā abhicārādihato ḍimbāhato mṛtyukṣaṇoditatathāruciḥ mukhāntarāyātaśaktipāto vā tathā dīkṣya ity ājñā ||
children.translated_text: There the command is that one who has served the guru, even if dead, expelled from the body, killed by sorcery or the like, struck by a child-spirit, one whose proper inclination arose at the moment of death, or one in whom the descent of power came through another mouth, is to be initiated in this way.

children.text: atra ca mṛtadīkṣāyām adhivāsādi na upayujyate ||
children.translated_text: And here, in initiation of the dead, preliminary lodging and the like are not used.

children.text: maṇḍale mantraviśeṣasaṃnidhaye yatra bahulā kriyā uttamam upakaraṇaṃ puṣpādi sthānaṃ pīṭhādi maṇḍalaṃ triśūlābjādi ākṛtiḥ dhyeyaviśeṣaḥ mantraḥ svayaṃ dīptaś ca dhyānaparasya yoginaḥ tadekabhaktisamāveśaśālino jñāninaś ca sambandhaḥ ity ete saṃnidhānahetavo yathottaram uktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In a maṇḍala, for the presence of a particular mantra, abundant ritual action, excellent implements such as flowers, a place such as a sacred seat, a maṇḍala such as a trident-lotus, a form, a special object to be meditated upon, the mantra itself, its own luminosity, the relation of a yogin intent on meditation, and of a knower endowed with absorption in devotion to that alone: these, each stronger than the preceding, are said to be causes of presence.

children.text: samuditatve tu kā kathā syāt iti parameśvareṇa uktam ||
children.translated_text: But when they are all combined, what need be said? So it has been stated by <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: tato devaṃ pūjayitvā tadākṛtiṃ kuśādimayīm agre sthāpayitvā gurvāsāditajñānopadeśakrameṇa tāṃ paśyet sa ca mūlādhārād udetya prasṛtasuvitatānantanāḍyadhvadaṇḍaṃ vīryeṇākramya nāsāgaganaparigataṃ vikṣipan vyāptum īṣṭe ||
children.translated_text: Then, having worshiped the deity and placed before himself an image of that person made of kuśa grass or the like, he should look at it according to the sequence of the instruction in knowledge received from the guru. And that person, rising from the root-support, forcefully occupying the staff of the path of the channels, which extends outward, is well spread out, and is endless, and casting it into the sky of the nose, seeks to pervade it.

children.text: yāvad dhūmābhirāmapracitataraśikhājālakenādhvacakraṃ saṃchādyābhīṣṭajīvānayanam iti mahāñ jālanāmā prayogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Until, with a net of densely massed flames delightful like smoke, he covers the wheel of the path and brings the desired soul: this is the great practice called the Net.

children.text: etenācchādanīyaṃ vrajati paravaśaṃ saṃmukhīnatvam ādau paścād ānīyate cet sakalam atha tato 'py adhvamadhyād yatheṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: By this, what is to be covered first comes under control and becomes face to face; if it is then brought, the whole of it is brought, and thereafter, from the middle of the path, as desired.

children.text: ākṛṣṭāv uddhatau vā mṛtajanaviṣaye karṣaṇīye 'tha jīve yogaḥ śrīśaṃbhunāthāgamaparigamito jālanāmā mayoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether in attracting or raising up, with regard to a dead person who is to be drawn, or then with regard to a living one, the yoga called the Net, learned from the tradition of venerable <s>Śambhunātha</s>, has been stated by me.

children.text: bahir api itthaṃ kathaṃ na bhavati ākarṣaṇādau vinābhyāsāt iti cet rāgadveṣādiyogavaśena tatpravṛttau aiśvaryāveśāyogāt ||
children.translated_text: If one asks, why does this not also occur externally in attraction and the like without practice? It is because, when such activity proceeds under the influence of attachment, aversion, and the like, there is no entrance into lordly power.

children.text: tato niyatiniyantritatvāt abhyāsādyapekṣā syād eva ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, since it is constrained by necessity, it certainly depends on practice and the like.

children.text: iha tu anugrahātmakaparameśvaratāveśāt tathābhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But here, because there is entrance into the state of <s>Parameśvara</s> whose nature is grace, the situation is otherwise.

children.text: parameśvara eva hi guruśarīrādhiṣṭhānadvāreṇa anugrāhyān anugṛhṇāti ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Parameśvara</s> himself, through the medium of occupying the guru's body, bestows grace upon those who are to be favored.

children.text: sa ca acintyamahimā iti uktaprāyam ||
children.translated_text: And he is of inconceivable greatness; this has almost already been stated.

children.text: evaṃ jālaprayogākṛṣṭo jīvo dārbhaṃ jātīphalādi vā śarīraṃ samāviṣṭo bhavati na ca spandate manaḥpraṇādisāmagryabhāvāt tadanudhyānabalāt tu spandate 'pi tādṛśe 'pi tasmin pūrvavat prokṣaṇādisaṃskāraḥ pūrṇāhutiyojanikāntaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the soul drawn by the Net practice enters a body made of darbha grass, a nutmeg, or the like, and does not move because the aggregate of mind, breath, and so on is absent. But through the power of meditation upon it, it may indeed move. Even in such a case, the consecration of sprinkling and the rest is performed on it as before, ending with the full oblation and conjunction.

children.text: atra paraṃ pūrṇāhutyā tasya dārbhādyākārasya paratejasi layaḥ kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, however, by the full oblation, the dissolution of that form made of darbha and so on into the supreme light must be effected.

children.text: evam uddhṛto 'sau pūrṇāhutyaiva apavṛjyate yadi svarnarakapretatiryakṣu sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, if he is situated among heaven, hell, ghosts, or animals, he is raised up and released by the full oblation alone.

children.text: manuṣyas tu tadaiva jñānaṃ yogaṃ dīkṣāṃ vivekaṃ vā labhate ||
children.translated_text: But a human being then and there obtains knowledge, yoga, initiation, or discernment.

children.text: adhikāriśarīratvāt iti mṛtoddharaṇam ||
children.translated_text: This is because he has a body fit for qualification. Thus ends the raising of the dead.

children.text: jīvato 'pi parokṣasya utpanne śaktipāte 'yam eva kramaḥ dārbhākṛtikalpanajīvākṛṣṭivarjam ||
children.translated_text: For an absent person who is living too, when the descent of power has arisen, this same procedure applies, except for the imagining of a darbha image and the drawing of the soul.

children.text: dhyānamātropasthāpitasyaiva asya saṃskāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: His consecration is performed simply when he has been made present by meditation.

children.text: dīkṣā ca bhogabhokṣobhayadāyinī ||
