children.translated_text: And initiation grants enjoyment, liberation, or both.

children.text: svavāsanābalīyastvāt bhogavāsanāvicchedasya ca asaṃbhāvyamānatvāt bahubhiḥ dīkṣāyām ūrdhvaśāsanasaṃskāro balavān anyas tu tatsaṃskārāya syāt ||
children.translated_text: Because one's own latent dispositions are very strong, and because the cutting off of the latent disposition toward enjoyment cannot be assumed, in the initiation of many people the sacramental impression of the higher teaching is powerful, while another rite serves for the sake of that sacramental impression.

children.text: paroṣasyāpi dīkṣitasya tathaiva jñānādyāvirbhāvaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: Even for one who is initiated while absent, the manifestation of knowledge and the like occurs in just the same way.

children.text: Chapter 17

vaiṣṇavādidakṣiṇatantrānteṣu śāsaneṣu ye sthitāḥ tadgṛhītavratā vā ye ca uttamaśāsanasthā api anadhikṛtādharaśāsanagurūpasevinaḥ te yadā śaktipātena pārameśvareṇa unmukhīkriyante tadā teṣām ayaṃ vidhiḥ tatra enaṃ kṛtopavāsam anyadine sādhāraṇamantrapūjitasya tadīyāṃ ceṣṭāṃ śrāvitasya bhagavato 'gre praveśayet tatrāsya vrataṃ gṛhītvā ambhasi kṣipet tato 'sau snāyāt tataḥ prokṣya carudantakāṣṭhābhyāṃ saṃskṛtya baddhanetraṃ praveśya sādhāraṇena mantreṇa parameśvarapūjāṃ kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Those who are established in scriptures such as the Vaiṣṇava and other right-hand tantras, or who have taken vows from them, and those who, though established in the highest scripture, serve gurus of lower scriptures without being authorized, when they are turned toward it by the <s>śaktipāta</s> of <s>Parameśvara</s>, have the following procedure. In this case, on another day, when he has fasted, after he has heard the relevant rite of the Lord, worshiped with the common mantra, he should lead him before the Lord. There, having taken his vow, he should cast it into water. Then that man should bathe. Then, after sprinkling him, consecrating him with caru and a tooth-stick, bringing him in with his eyes bound, he should have him perform worship of <s>Parameśvara</s> with the common mantra.

children.text: tataḥ sādhāraṇamantreṇa śivīkṛte agnau vrataśuddhiṃ kuryāt tanmantrasampuṭaṃ nāma kṛtvā prāyaścittaṃ śodhayāmi iti svāhāntaṃ śataṃ juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the fire that has been made into <s>Śiva</s> by the common mantra, he should perform the purification of the vow. Having made what is called an enclosure with that mantra, he should offer a hundred oblations ending in svāhā, with the words, 'I purify the expiation.'

children.text: tato 'pi pūrṇāhutiḥ vauṣaḍantena ||
children.translated_text: After that too, there is the full oblation, with a formula ending in vauṣaṭ.

children.text: tato vrateśvaram āhūya pūjayitvā tasya śivājñayā akiṃcitkaraḥ tvam asya bhava iti śrāvaṇāṃ kṛtvā taṃ tarpayitvā visṛjya agniṃ visṛjet iti liṅgoddhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having invoked and worshiped the lord of the vow, he should make him hear, 'By the command of <s>Śiva</s>, become ineffective for this person.' Having satisfied him and dismissed him, he should dismiss the fire. This is the removal of the liṅga.

children.text: tato 'sya adhivāsādi prāgvat ||
children.translated_text: After that, his preparatory residence and the rest are as before.

children.text: dīkṣā yatheccham ||
children.translated_text: Initiation is according to his wish.

children.text: Chapter 18
svabhyastajñāninaṃ sādhakatve gurutve vā abhiṣiñcet yataḥ sarvalakṣaṇahīno 'pi jñānavān eva sādhakatve anugrahakaraṇe ca adhikṛtaḥ na anyaḥ abhiṣikto 'pi ||
children.translated_text: One should consecrate as a sādhaka or as a guru a man who is well practiced in knowledge; for even if he lacks all the marks, only a man possessing knowledge is qualified for sādhaka-ship and for bestowing grace, not another, even if he has been consecrated.

children.text: svādhikārasamarpaṇe guruḥ dīkṣādi akurvan api na pratyavaiti pūrvaṃ tu pratyavāyena adhikārabandhena vidyeśapadadāyinā bandha eva asya dīkṣādyakaraṇam so 'bhiṣikto mantradevatātādātmyasiddhaye ṣāṇmāsikaṃ pratyahaṃ japahomaviśeṣapūjācaraṇena vidyāvrataṃ kuryāt tadanantaraṃ labdhatanmayībhāvo dīkṣādau adhikṛtaḥ tatra na ayogyān dīkṣeta na ca yogyaṃ pariharet dīkṣitam api jñānadāne parīkṣeta chadmagṛhītajñānam api jñātvā upekṣeta atra ca abhiṣekavibhavena devapūjādikam ||
children.translated_text: When surrendering his own authority, a guru does not incur fault even if he does not perform initiation and the like. Previously, however, failure to perform initiation and the like was itself bondage for him, through the fault of the bond of authority that grants the station of a <s>Vidyeśa</s>. Having been consecrated, for the sake of attaining identity with the mantra-deity, he should observe the vidyā-vow for six months, every day, through japa, oblation, special worship, and ritual conduct. After that, having attained a state of identity with it, he is qualified for initiation and the like. In that matter he should not initiate the unfit, nor should he pass over one who is fit. Even one already initiated he should examine in the giving of knowledge. And if he knows that someone has taken knowledge deceitfully, he should disregard him. Here too, according to the capacity of the consecration, there are deity-worship and the other rites.

children.text: Chapter 19

atha adharaśāsanasthānāṃ gurvantānām api maraṇasamanantaraṃ mṛtoddhāroditaśaktipātayogād eva antyasaṃskārākhyāṃ dīkṣāṃ kuryāt ūrdhvaśāsanasthānām api luptasamayānām akṛtaprāyaścittānām iti parameśvarājñā ||
children.translated_text: Now, even for those established in lower scriptures, up to and including their gurus, immediately after death, by connection with the <s>śaktipāta</s> taught in the rite for raising the dead, he should perform the initiation called the final sacrament. This is also for those established in higher scriptures whose samayas have lapsed and who have not performed expiation: such is the command of <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: tatra yo mṛtoddhāre vidhiḥ uktaḥ sa sarva eva śarīre kartavyaḥ pūrṇāhutyā śavaśarīradāhaḥ mūḍhānāṃ tu pratītirūḍhaye sapratyayām antyeṣṭiṃ kriyājñānayogabalāt kuryāt tatra śavaśarīre saṃhārakrameṇa mantrān nyasya jālakrameṇa ākṛṣya rodhanavedhanaghaṭṭanādi kuryāt prāṇasaṃcārakrameṇa hṛdi kaṇṭhe lalāṭe ca ity evaṃ śavaśarīraṃ kampate ||
children.translated_text: In that case, whatever procedure was taught for raising the dead is to be performed in full upon the body. With the full oblation there is the burning of the corpse. But for the sake of establishing confidence in the dull-minded, by the power of ritual, knowledge, and yoga, he should perform a perceptible funeral rite. In that rite, he should place the mantras on the corpse-body in the sequence of withdrawal, draw them in by the net sequence, and perform blocking, piercing, shaking, and the like. By the sequence of transmitting the vital breath, in the heart, throat, and forehead, and so on, the corpse-body trembles.

children.text: tataḥ paramaśive yojanikāṃ kṛtvā tat dahet pūrṇāhutyā antyeṣṭyā śuddhānām anyeṣām api vā śrāddhadīkṣāṃ tryahaṃ turye dine māsi māsi saṃvatsare saṃvatsare kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, having effected its union with <s>Paramaśiva</s>, he should burn it with the full oblation. For those purified by the funeral rite, and for others as well, he should perform śrāddha-initiation for three days, on the fourth day, month by month, and year by year.

children.text: tatra homāntaṃ vidhiṃ kṛtvā naivedyam ekahaste kṛtvā tadīyāṃ vīryarūpāṃ śaktiṃ bhogyākārāṃ paśugatabhogyaśaktitādātmyapratipannāṃ dhyātvā parameśvare bhoktari arpayet ity evaṃ bhogyabhāve nivṛtte patir eva bhavati antyeṣṭimṛtoddharaṇaśrāddhadīkṣāṇām anyatamenāpi yadyapi kṛtārthatā tathāpi bubhukṣoḥ kriyābhūyastvaṃ phalabhūyastvāya iti sarvam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: There, having performed the procedure up to the end of the oblation, and having placed the food-offering in one hand, he should meditate on that person's power, which is in the form of vitality, as assuming the form of what is to be enjoyed and as having attained identity with the enjoyability belonging to the bound soul; then he should offer it to <s>Parameśvara</s> as the enjoyer. In this way, when the condition of being enjoyed has ceased, he becomes the Lord. Although fulfillment is attained even by any one of the funeral rite, raising of the dead, or śrāddha-initiation, nevertheless, for one who desires enjoyment, greater abundance of rites is for the sake of greater abundance of result; therefore he should perform them all.

children.text: mumukṣor api tanmayībhāvasiddhaye ayam jīvataḥ pratyaham anuṣṭhānābhyāsavat ||
children.translated_text: For one who desires liberation too, this is like the living person's daily practice of observance, for the attainment of identity with that.

children.text: tattvajñāninas tu na ko 'py ayam antyeṣṭyādiśrāddhānto vidhiḥ upayogī tanmaraṇaṃ tadvidyāsaṃtānināṃ parvadinaṃ saṃvidaṃśapūraṇāt tāvataḥ saṃtānasya ekasaṃvinmātraparamārthatvāt jīvato jñānalābhasaṃtānadivasavat ||
children.translated_text: But for the knower of reality, no procedure at all, from funeral rite through śrāddha, is useful. His death is a festival day for those in the succession of his knowledge, because it fills out a portion of consciousness, since that much of the lineage has, in ultimate truth, the nature of a single consciousness alone, just like the day on which knowledge is obtained in life.

children.text: sarvatra ca atra śrāddhādividhau mūrtiyāgaḥ pradhānam iti śrīsiddhāmatam tadvidhiś ca vakṣyate naimittikaprakāśane ||
children.translated_text: And everywhere in this procedure of śrāddha and the like, the sacrifice of the image is principal: so says the venerable <s>Siddhāmata</s>. Its procedure will be explained in the exposition of occasional rites.

children.text: Chapter 20
tatra yā dīkṣā saṃskārasiddhyai jñānayogyān prati yā ca tadaśaktān prati mokṣadīkṣā sabījā tasyāṃ kṛtāyām ājīvaṃ śeṣavartanaṃ guruḥ upadiśet ||
children.translated_text: In that context, for the initiation that is directed toward those fit for knowledge for the accomplishment of the sacrament, and also for the seed-possessing liberation-initiation directed toward those incapable of that, when it has been performed, the guru should teach the remaining lifelong observance.

children.text: tatra nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyam iti trividhaṃ śeṣavartanam antyaṃ ca sādhakasyaiva tat na iha niścetavyam ||
children.translated_text: There the remaining observance is threefold: daily, occasional, and optional. The last belongs only to the sādhaka; it is not to be determined here.

children.text: tatra niyatabhavaṃ nityaṃ tanmayībhāva eva naimittikaṃ tadupayogi saṃdhyopāsanaṃ pratyaham anuṣṭhānaṃ parvadinaṃ pavitrakam ityādi ||
children.translated_text: There, the daily observance has a fixed occurrence and is nothing but the state of identity with that. The occasional observance is what is useful for that: daily twilight worship, daily ritual practice, festival days, the pavitraka rite, and so on.

children.text: tad api nityaṃ svakālanaiyatyāt iti kecit ||
children.translated_text: Some say that even that is daily, because its own time is fixed.

children.text: naimittikaṃ tu tacchāsanasthānām api aniyatam tadyathā gurutadvargāgamanaṃ tatparvadinaṃ jñānalābhadinam ityādikam iti kecit ||
children.translated_text: But the occasional rite is irregular even for those who stand within that teaching, as, for example, the arrival of the guru or his group, that festival day, the day of obtaining knowledge, and so on; so some say.

children.text: tatra niyatapūjā saṃdhyopāsā gurupūjā parvapūjā pavitrakam iti avaśyaṃbhāvi ||
children.translated_text: Among these, regular worship, twilight worship, worship of the guru, festival worship, and the pavitraka rite are inevitable.

children.text: naimittikam jñānalābhaḥ śāstralābho gurutadvargagṛhāgamanaṃ tadīyajanmasaṃskāraprāyaṇadināni laukikotsavaḥ śāstravyākhyā ādimadhyāntā devatādarśanaṃ melakaṃ svapnājñā samayaniṣkṛtilābhaḥ ity etat naimittikaṃ viśeṣārcanakāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: The occasional rite consists of obtaining knowledge, obtaining a scripture, the arrival at the house of the guru or his group, days of his birth, consecration, or departure, a worldly festival, the explanation of scripture, the beginning, middle, and end, the vision of a deity, an assembly, a command in a dream, and the obtaining of release from a <s>samaya</s> obligation. This occasional rite is the cause for special worship.

children.text: tatra kṛtadīkṣākasya śiṣyasya pradhānaṃ mantraṃ savīryakaṃ saṃvittisphuraṇasāram alikhitaṃ vaktrāgamenaiva arpayet tataḥ tanmayībhāvasiddhyarthaṃ sa śiṣyaḥ saṃdhyāsu tanmayībhāvābhyāsaṃ kuryāt taddvāreṇa sarvakālaṃ tathāvidhasaṃskāralābhasiddhyarthaṃ pratyahaṃ ca parameśvaraṃ ca sthaṇḍile vā liṅge vā abhyarcayet ||
children.translated_text: There, to a disciple who has received initiation, one should bestow the chief mantra, endowed with power and having as its essence the flashing forth of consciousness, unwritten and only through oral transmission. Then, in order to accomplish identification with it, that disciple should practice identification with it at the twilights; and, through that, for the accomplishment of obtaining such a sacramental impression at all times, he should worship <s>Parameśvara</s> every day, either on a sthaṇḍila altar or in a liṅga.

children.text: tatra hṛdye sthaṇḍile vimalamakuravad dhyāte svam eva rūpaṃ yājyadevatācakrābhinnaṃ mūrtibimbitam iva dṛṣṭvā hṛdyapuṣpagandhāsavatarpaṇanaivedyadhūpadīpopahārastutigītavādyanṛttādinā pūjayet japet stuvīta tanmayībhāvam aśaṅkitaṃ labdhum ||
children.translated_text: There, when a pleasing sthaṇḍila altar has been meditated upon like a spotless mirror, he should see his own form, non-different from the circle of the deity to be worshiped, as if reflected in a visible image; and he should worship with pleasing flowers, perfumes, water, tarpaṇa, naivedya, incense, lamp, offerings, praise, song, instrumental music, dance, and the like; he should recite and praise, in order to obtain unhesitating identification with it.

children.text: ādarśe hi svamukham aviratam avalokayataḥ tatsvarūpaniścitiḥ acireṇaiva bhavet na cātra kaścit kramaḥ pradhānam ṛte tanmayībhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: For when one continually looks at one's own face in a mirror, certainty about its form arises very quickly. And here there is no sequence that is principal, apart from identification with it.

children.text: paramantratanmayībhāvāviṣṭasya nivṛttapaśuvāsanākalaṅkasya bhaktirasānuvedhavidrutasamastapāśajālasya yat adhivasati hṛdayaṃ tad eva paramam upādeyam iti asmadguravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Our teachers say that the heart occupied by one who is absorbed in identification with the supreme mantra, whose stain of animal-bound latent tendencies has ceased, and whose entire net of bonds has been dissolved by the penetration of the flavor of devotion, is itself the highest thing to be adopted.

children.text: adhiśayya pāramārthikaḥ bhāvaprasaraṃ prakāśam ullasati yā ||
children.translated_text: That which, resting upon the ultimate, shines forth as light, the expansion of being,

children.text: paramāmṛtadṛktvaṃ tayārcayante rahasyavidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is the vision of the supreme nectar; with that, the knowers of the secret perform worship.

children.text: kṛtvādhāradharāṃ camatkṛtirasaprokṣākṣaṇakṣālitām āttair mānasataḥ svabhāvakusumaiḥ svāmodasaṃdohibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made the supporting ground, washed by the sprinkling drops of the savor of wonder, with natural flowers taken mentally, heaped with their own fragrance,

children.text: ānandāmṛtanirbharasvahṛdayānarghārghapātrakramāt tvāṃ devyā saha dehadevasadane devārcaye 'harniśam ||
children.translated_text: from the sequence of priceless argha-vessels that are my own heart filled with the nectar of bliss, I worship you, together with the goddess, day and night in the temple of the deity that is the body.

children.text: iti ślokadvayoktam artham antar bhāvayan devatācakraṃ bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: Thus, inwardly contemplating the meaning stated in the two verses, he should contemplate the circle of deities.

children.text: tato mudrāpradarśanaṃ japaḥ tannivedanam ||
children.translated_text: Then comes the display of mudrās, recitation, and the dedication of that recitation.

children.text: bodhyaikātmyena visarjanam ||
children.translated_text: The dismissal is through identity with what is to be awakened.

children.text: mukhyaṃ naivedyaṃ svayam aśnīyāt sarvaṃ vā jale kṣipet jalajā hi prāṇinaḥ pūrvadīkṣitāḥ carubhojanadvāreṇa iti āgamavidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should himself eat the chief naivedya, or else cast it all into water; for aquatic beings, according to the knowers of the āgama, have been initiated previously through eating the caru.

children.text: mārjāramūṣakaśvādibhakṣaṇe tu śaṅkā janitā nirayāya iti jñānī api lokānugrahecchayā na tādṛk kuryāt lokaṃ vā parityajya āsīta iti sthaṇḍilayāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if it is eaten by cats, mice, dogs, and the like, the doubt that is produced leads to hell; therefore even a knower, wishing to benefit the world, should not do such a thing, or else should remain after abandoning the world. This is the sthaṇḍila sacrifice.

children.text: atha liṅge tatra na rahasyamantraiḥ liṅgaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayet viśeṣāt vyaktam iti pūrvapratiṣṭhiteṣu āvāhanavisarjanakrameṇa pūjāṃ kuryāt ādhāratayā ||
children.translated_text: Now, in the case of a liṅga, he should not consecrate the liṅga with secret mantras, since it is especially manifest; rather, with liṅgas already consecrated before, he should perform worship by the sequence of invocation and dismissal, treating it as a support.

children.text: tatra gurudehaṃ svadehaṃ śaktidehaṃ rahasyaśāstrapustakaṃ vīrapātram akṣasūtraṃ prāharaṇaṃ bāṇīyaṃ mauktikaṃ sauvarṇaṃ puṣpagandhadravyādihṛdyavastukṛtaṃ makuraṃ vā liṅgam arcayet ||
children.translated_text: There he may worship as a liṅga the guru's body, his own body, the body of the śakti, a book of the secret scripture, a hero's vessel, a rosary, a weapon, something made of beryl, pearl, or gold, a mirror made from pleasing things such as flowers, perfumes, and substances, or another such object.

children.text: tatra ca ādhārabalād eva adhikādhikamantrasiddhiḥ bhavati iti pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ pradhānam ādhāraguṇānuvidhāyitvāt ca mantrāṇāṃ tatra tatra sādhye tattatpradhānam iti śāstraguravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And there, from the strength of the support itself, greater and greater mantra-siddhi occurs. Therefore each preceding support is principal, because mantras conform to the qualities of the support; and in each respective thing to be accomplished, that corresponding support is principal, according to the teachers of scripture.

children.text: sarvatra parameśvarābhedābhimāna eva paramaḥ saṃskāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Everywhere, the supreme sacramental impression is precisely the conviction of non-difference from <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: atha parvavidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, the rule concerning festivals.

children.text: tatra sāmānyaṃ sāmānyasāmānyaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣo viśeṣasāmānyaṃ viśeṣo viśeṣaviśeṣaś ca iti ṣoḍhā parva ||
children.translated_text: There, a festival is sixfold: general, generally general, generally specific, specifically general, specific, and specifically specific.

children.text: pūraṇāt vidheḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is because the rite is brought to completion.

children.text: tatra māsi māsi prathamaṃ pañcamaṃ dinaṃ sāmānyam caturthāṣṭamanavamacaturdaśapañcadaśāni dvayor api pakṣayoḥ sāmānyasāmānyam anayor ubhayor api rāśyoḥ vakṣyamāṇatattattithyucitagrahanakṣatrayoge sāmānyaviśeṣaḥ mārgaśīrṣasya prathamarātribhāgaḥ kṛṣṇanavamyām pauṣasya tu rātrimadhyaṃ kṛṣṇanavamyām māghasya rātrimadhyaṃ śuklapañcadaśyām phālgunasya dinamadhyaṃ śukladvādaśyām caitrasya śuklatrayodaśyām vaiśākhasya kṛṣṇāṣṭamyām jyaiṣṭhasya kṛṣṇanavamyām āṣāḍhasya prathame dine śrāvaṇasya divasapūrvabhāgaḥ kṛṣṇaikādaśyām bhādrapadasya dinamadhyaṃ śuklaṣaṣṭyām āśvayujasya śuklanavamīdinam kārttikasya prathamo rātribhāgaḥ śuklanavamyām iti viśeṣaparva ||
children.translated_text: There, in every month, the first and fifth days are general. The fourth, eighth, ninth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days in both fortnights are generally general. In both of these groups, when there is a conjunction with the planet and lunar mansion appropriate to the particular lunar date to be stated below, it is generally specific. The first part of the night in <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, on the dark ninth; the middle of the night in <s>Pauṣa</s>, on the dark ninth; the middle of the night in <s>Māgha</s>, on the bright fifteenth; midday in <s>Phālguna</s>, on the bright twelfth; in <s>Caitra</s>, on the bright thirteenth; in <s>Vaiśākha</s>, on the dark eighth; in <s>Jyaiṣṭha</s>, on the dark ninth; in <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, on the first day; the earlier part of the day in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, on the dark eleventh; midday in <s>Bhādrapada</s>, on the bright sixth; in <s>Āśvayuja</s>, the day of the bright ninth; and the first part of the night in <s>Kārttika</s>, on the bright ninth: these are the specific festivals.

children.text: citrācandrau maghājīvau tiṣyacandrau pūrvaphālgunībudhau śravaṇabudhau śatabhiṣakcandrau dityau rohiṇīśukrau viśākhābṛhaspatī śravaṇacandrau iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Citrā</s> with the moon, <s>Maghā</s> with Jupiter, <s>Tiṣya</s> with the moon, <s>Pūrvaphālgunī</s> with Mercury, <s>Śravaṇa</s> with Mercury, <s>Śatabhiṣaj</s> with the moon, the <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s> with Venus, <s>Viśākhā</s> with <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and <s>Śravaṇa</s> with the moon: thus it is stated.

children.text: yadi mārgaśīrṣādikrameṇa yathāsaṃkhyaṃ bhavati āśvayujaṃ varjayitvā tadā viśeṣaviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, in the sequence beginning with <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, these occur respectively, excluding <s>Āśvayuja</s>, then there is a particularly special distinction.

children.text: anyaviśeṣaś cet anyaparvaṇi tadā tat anuparva ity āhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if another special conjunction occurs on another festival day, then they call that an auxiliary festival.

children.text: bhagrahayoge ca na velā pradhānam ||
children.translated_text: And in a conjunction of asterism and planet, the time of day is not the main factor.

children.text: tither eva viśeṣalābhāt anuyāgakālānuvṛttis tu parvadine mukhyā anuyāgaprādhānyāt parvayāgānām anuyāgo mūrtiyāgaḥ cakrayāgaḥ iti paryāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the special benefit is obtained from the lunar day itself. But the continuation of the time for the auxiliary rite is principal on the festival day, because the auxiliary rite is primary. 'Auxiliary rite,' 'mūrtiyāga,' and 'cakrayāga' are synonyms for the festival sacrifices.

children.text: tatra guruḥ tadvargyaḥ sasaṃtānaḥ tattvavit kanyā antyā veśyā aruṇā tattvavedinī vā iti cakrayāge mukhyapūjyāḥ viśeṣāt sāmastyena ||
children.translated_text: There, in the cakrayāga, the chief persons to be worshiped, especially and collectively, are the guru, one belonging to his group together with his lineage, a knower of reality, a maiden, a low-born woman, a courtesan, a ruddy woman, or a woman who knows reality.

children.text: tatra madhye guruḥ tadāvaraṇakrameṇa gurvādisamayyantaṃ vīraḥ śaktiḥ iti krameṇa ity evaṃ cakrasthityā vā paṅktisthityā vā āsīta tato gandhadhūpapuṣpādibhiḥ krameṇa pūjayet tataḥ pātraṃ sadāśivarūpaṃ dhyātvā śaktyamṛtadhyātena āsavena pūrayitvā tatra bhoktrīṃ śaktiṃ śivatayā pūjayitvā tayaiva devatācakratarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā naraśaktiśivātmakatritayamelakaṃ dhyātvā āvaraṇāvataraṇakrameṇa mokṣabhogaprādhānyaṃ bahir antaś ca tarpaṇaṃ kuryāt punaḥ pratisaṃcaraṇakrameṇa evaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhramaṇaṃ cakraṃ puṣṇāti ||
children.translated_text: There the guru should sit in the middle; or, according to the order of his enclosures, there should be a hero and a śakti in sequence, from the guru down to the samayin; or they may sit in the arrangement of a circle or in a row. Then he should worship them in order with sandal paste, incense, flowers, and the like. Next, having meditated on the vessel as the form of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, he should fill it with liquor contemplated as the nectar of the śakti. In it he should worship the enjoying śakti as <s>Śiva</s>, and through her he should perform the satiation of the circle of deities. Having meditated on the union of the triad consisting of man, śakti, and <s>Śiva</s>, he should perform satiation outwardly and inwardly, in the order of the descent of the enclosures, with liberation and enjoyment as predominant. Again, in the order of reabsorption, this complete rotation nourishes the circle.

children.text: tatra ādhāre viśvamayaṃ pātraṃ sthāpayitvā devatācakraṃ tarpayitvā svātmānaṃ vanditena tena tarpayet pātrābhāve bhadraṃ vellitaśuktiḥ vā dakṣahastena pātrākāraṃ bhadraṃ dvābhyām uparigatadakṣiṇābhyāṃ niḥsaṃdhīkṛtābhyām vellitaśuktiḥ patadbhiḥ bindubhiḥ vetālaguhyakāḥ saṃtuṣyanti dhārayā bhairavaḥ atra praveśo na kasyacit deyaḥ pramādāt praviṣṭasya vicāraṃ na kuryāt kṛtvā punar dviguṇaṃ cakrayāgaṃ kuryāt tato 'vadaṃśān bhojanādīn ca agre yatheṣṭaṃ vikīryeta guptagṛhe vā saṃketābhidhānavarjaṃ devatāśabdena sarvān yojayet iti vīrasaṃkarayāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, having placed the vessel that contains the whole universe on the support, and having satiated the circle of deities, he should satiate his own self with that which has been honored. If there is no vessel, the auspicious substitute is a rolled shell; or with the right hand he may make the auspicious vessel-shape, and with both hands, the right hands placed above and joined without gaps, the rolled-shell form. The <s>Vetālas</s> and <s>Guhyakas</s> are satisfied by falling drops; <s>Bhairava</s> is satisfied by a stream. Here admission must not be given to anyone. If someone enters through negligence, one should not deliberate about him; after doing so, one should perform the cakrayāga again in double measure. Then he should scatter morsels, foods, and the like in front as desired, or in a hidden house, and should connect everyone with the word 'deity,' avoiding conventional names. This is the heroic mixed sacrifice.

children.text: tato 'nte dakṣiṇātāmbūlavastrādibhiḥ tarpayet iti pradhānatamo 'yaṃ mūrtiyāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, at the end, he should satisfy them with honoraria, betel, garments, and the like. This is the most important mūrtiyāga.

children.text: adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo 'pi mūrtiyāgena parvadināni pūjayan varṣād eva putrakoktaṃ phalam eti vinā saṃdhyānuṣṭhānādibhiḥ iti vṛddhānāṃ bhogināṃ strīṇāṃ vidhir ayam śaktipāte sati upadeṣṭavyo guruṇā ||
children.translated_text: Even one who has not seen a maṇḍala, if he worships on the festival days by means of the mūrtiyāga, obtains in one year the result taught for a putraka, even without twilight observances and the like. This is the rule for the aged, for enjoyers, and for women, and it is to be taught by the guru when there is descent of power.

children.text: atha pavitrakavidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, the procedure for the pavitraka.

children.text: sa ca śrīratnamālātriśiromataśrīsiddhāmatādau vidhipūrvakaḥ pārameśvarājñāpūrakaś ca uktaṃ caitat śrītantrāloke vinā pavitrakeṇa sarvaṃ niṣphalam iti ||
children.translated_text: This has been taught, preceded by due procedure, in the <s>Śrīratnamālā</s>, the <s>Triśiromata</s>, the <s>Śrīsiddhāmata</s>, and other works, and it fulfills the command of <s>Parameśvara</s>. And this is stated in the <s>Śrītantrāloka</s>: without the pavitraka everything is fruitless.

children.text: tatra āṣāḍhaśuklāt kulapūrṇimādināntaṃ kāryaṃ pavitrakam tatra kārttikakṛṣṇapañcadaśī kulacakraṃ nityācakraṃ pūrayati iti śrīnityātantravidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the pavitraka should be performed from the bright fortnight of <s>Āṣāḍha</s> up to the day beginning with the kula full-moon. In this regard, those who know the <s>Śrīnityātantra</s> say that the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight of <s>Kārttika</s> completes the kula-circle and the nitya-circle.

children.text: māghaśuklapañcadaśī iti śrībhairavakulormividaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who know the <s>Śrībhairavakulormi</s> say: the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight of <s>Māgha</s>.

children.text: dakṣiṇāyanāntapañcadaśī iti śrītantrasadbhāvavidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who know the <s>Śrītantrasadbhāva</s> say: the fifteenth day at the end of the southern course of the sun.

children.text: tatra vibhavena devaṃ pūjayitvā āhutyā tarpayitvā pavitrakaṃ dadyāt sauvarṇamuktāratnaviracitāt prabhṛti paṭasūtrakārpāsakuśagarbhāntam api kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: There, after worshiping the deity according to his means and satisfying him with oblations, he should offer the pavitraka. He may make it of gold, pearls, and jewels, and so forth, down to cloth thread, cotton, or kuśa grass wrapped within.

children.text: tac ca tattvasaṃkhyagranthikaṃ padakalābhuvanavarṇamantrasaṃkhyagranthi ca jānvantam ekaṃ nābhyantam aparaṃ kaṇṭhāntam anyat śirasi anyat iti catvāri pavitrakāṇi devāya gurave ca samastādhvaparipūrṇatadrūpabhāvanena dadyāt śeṣebhya ekam iti ||
children.translated_text: And it should have knots equal to the number of the tattvas, or knots equal to the number of the padas, kalās, worlds, phonemes, and mantras. There are four pavitrakas: one reaching to the knees, another to the navel, another to the throat, and another on the head. He should offer them to the deity and to the guru with the contemplation that they are that form, complete with the entire adhvan. To the others he should give one.

children.text: tato mahotsavaḥ kāryaḥ cāturmāsyaṃ saptadinaṃ tridinaṃ ca iti mukhyānvāpatkalpāḥ sati vibhave māsi māsi pavitrakam atha vā caturṣu māseṣu atha vā sakṛt tadakaraṇe prāyaścittaṃ japet jñānī api sambhavadvitto 'pi akaraṇe pratyavaiti lobhopahitajñānākaraṇe jñānanindāpatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a great festival should be performed. Four months, seven days, and three days are the principal and secondary alternatives. If means are available, the pavitraka should be performed every month, or else in the four months, or else once. If it is not done, he should recite an expiation. Even a knower, if he has available wealth and still does not perform it, incurs fault, because when knowledge, obstructed by greed, does not act, there is the fault of disparaging knowledge.

children.text: yadā prāpyāpi vijñānaṃ dūṣitaṃ parameśaśāsanaṃ tadā prāyaścittī ||
children.translated_text: When, though knowledge has been obtained, the command of <s>Parameśa</s> is defiled, then one must perform expiation.

children.text: iti vacanāt ||
children.translated_text: So says the authoritative statement.

children.text: ity eṣa pavitrakavidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus this is the procedure for the pavitraka.

children.text: jñānalābhādau laukikotsavānte 'pi sarvatra saṃvidullāsādhikyaṃ devatācakrasaṃnidhiḥ viśeṣato bhavati iti tathāvidhādhikyaparyālocanayā tathāvidham eva viśeṣam anuyāgādau kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: At the attainment of knowledge and the like, and even at the end of a worldly festival, everywhere there is a special abundance of the expansion of consciousness and a special presence of the circle of deities. Therefore, considering such a particular abundance, one should perform just such a special observance in the auxiliary rite and so on.

children.text: atha vyākhyāvidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, the procedure for explanation.

children.text: sarvaśāstrasampūrṇaṃ guruṃ vyākhyārtham abhyarthayeta so 'pi svaśiṣyāya paraśiṣyāyāpi vā samucitasaṃskārocitaṃ śāstraṃ vyācakṣīta adharaśāsanasthāyāpi karuṇāvaśāt īśvarecchāvaicitryodbhāvitaśaktipātasambhāvanābhāvitahṛdayo vyācakṣīta marmopadeśavarjam ||
children.translated_text: One should request a guru who is complete in all the scriptures to explain the meaning. He too should explain to his own disciple, or even to another's disciple, the scripture appropriate to the proper sacrament. Even to one established in a lower teaching he should explain it, out of compassion, when his heart has been prepared by the possibility of <s>śaktipāta</s> produced by the varied will of <s>Īśvara</s>, but excluding instruction in the secrets.

children.text: tatra nimnāsanasthitebhyaḥ tatparebhyo niyamitavāṅmanaḥkāyebhyo vyākhyā kriyamāṇā phalavatī bhavati prathamaṃ gandhādiliptāyāṃ bhuvi ullikhya saṃkalpya vā padmādhāraṃ caturaśraṃ padmatrayaṃ padmamadhye vāgīśīṃ vāmadakṣiṇayoḥ gaṇapatigurū ca pūjayet ādhārapadme vyākhyeyakalpadevatām ||
children.translated_text: There, when an explanation is given to those seated on lower seats, intent upon it, and restrained in speech, mind, and body, it becomes fruitful. First, on ground anointed with perfumes and the like, having drawn or mentally formed a square lotus-support, three lotuses, he should worship <s>Vāgīśī</s> in the middle lotus, and <s>Gaṇapati</s> and the guru on the left and right. In the supporting lotus he should worship the deity presiding over the section to be explained.

children.text: tataḥ sāmānyārghapātrayogena cakraṃ tarpayet tato vyācakṣīta sūtravākyapaṭalagrantham pūrvāparāviruddhaṃ kurvan tantrāvṛttiprasaṅgasamuccayavikalpādiśāstranyāyaucityena pūrvaṃ pakṣaṃ samyak ghaṭayitvā samyak ca dūṣayan sādhyaṃ sādhayan tātparyavṛttiṃ pradarśayan paṭalāntaṃ vyācakṣīta nādhikam tatrāpi vastvante vastvante tarpaṇaṃ pūjanam iti yāvad vyākhyāsamāptiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, by means of the common argha-vessel, he should satisfy the circle. After that he should explain the sūtra, statement, chapter, or book, making it free from contradiction between what precedes and what follows. In accordance with scriptural reasoning such as tantric repetition, context, combination, and alternative, he should first establish the prima facie view correctly, refute it correctly, establish the thesis, and show the purport and the gloss. He should explain up to the end of the chapter, not beyond. There too, at each change of topic, there is satisfaction and worship, until the explanation is complete.

children.text: tato 'pi pūjayitvā vidyāpīṭhaṃ visarjya upalipya agādhe tat kṣepayet ||
children.translated_text: After that also, having worshiped, he should dismiss the seat of knowledge, smear the place, and cast that into deep water.

children.text: iti vyākhyāvidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the procedure for exposition.

children.text: atha samayaniṣkṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, the expiation of <s>samaya</s> obligations.

children.text: yady api tattvajñānaniṣṭhasya prāyaścittādi na kiṃcit tathāpi caryāmātrād eva mokṣabhāginaḥ tān anugrahītum ācāravartanīṃ darśayet ||
children.translated_text: Although for one established in knowledge of reality there is no expiation or anything of the sort, still, in order to favor those who have a share in liberation merely through ritual conduct, he should show the path of observance.

children.text: atattvajñānī tu caryaikāyattabhogamokṣaḥ samayollaṅghane kṛte prāyaścittam akurvan varṣaśataṃ kravyādo bhavatīti iti prāyaścittavidhiḥ vaktavyaḥ tatra strīvadhe prāyaścittaṃ nāsti anyatra tu balābalaṃ jñātvā akhaṇḍāṃ bhagavatīṃ mālinīm ekavārāt prabhṛti trilakṣāntam āvartayet yāvat śaṅkāvicyutiḥ bhavati tadante viśeṣapūjā tatrāpi cakrayāgaḥ sa hi sarvatra śeṣabhūtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But one who does not know reality, whose enjoyment and liberation depend solely on ritual conduct, if he transgresses a <s>samaya</s> and does not perform expiation, becomes a flesh-eater for a hundred years. Therefore the procedure of expiation must be stated. In that matter, for the killing of a woman there is no expiation. In other cases, having understood the relative gravity, he should repeat the unbroken divine <s>Mālinī</s> from once up to three hundred thousand times, until doubt falls away. At the end of that there is special worship, and there too the cakra-sacrifice; for that is subsidiary everywhere.

children.text: iti samayaniṣkṛtividhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the procedure for expiation of <s>samaya</s> obligations.

children.text: atha gurupūjāvidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, the procedure for worship of the guru.

children.text: sarvayāgānteṣu upasaṃhṛte yāge aparedyuḥ gurupūjāṃ kuryāt pūrvaṃ hi sa vidhyaṅgatayā toṣito na tu prādhānyena iti tāṃ prādhānyena akurvan adhikārabandhena baddho bhavati ||
children.translated_text: At the end of all sacrifices, when the sacrifice has been withdrawn, on the following day he should perform worship of the guru. Previously he was satisfied only as an auxiliary to the rite, not as the principal object. Therefore, if one does not perform that worship with him as principal, one becomes bound by the bond of authority.

children.text: iti tāṃ sarvathā caret ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should perform it in every way.

children.text: tatra svāstikaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā tatra sauvarṇaṃ pīṭhaṃ dattvā tatra samastam adhvānaṃ pūjayitvā tatpīṭhaṃ tena adhiṣṭhāpya tasmai pūjāṃ kṛtvā tarpaṇaṃ bhojanaṃ dakṣiṇām ātmānam iti nivedya naivedyocchiṣṭaṃ prārthya vanditvā svayaṃ prāśya cakrapūjāṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: There, having made a svastika maṇḍala, placed a golden seat there, worshiped the entire course upon it, and installed that seat with it, he should perform worship for him. Having offered satisfaction, food, a fee, and himself, having requested the remainder of the naivedya, bowed, and eaten it himself, he should perform the cakra-worship.

children.text: ita gurupūjāvidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the procedure for worship of the guru.

children.text: Chapter 21
evaṃ samastaṃ nityaṃ naimittikaṃ karma nirūpitam ||
children.translated_text: In this way all daily and occasional rites have been explained.

children.text: adhunā asyaiva āgamasya prāmāṇyam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Now the authority of this very āgama is stated.

children.text: tatra saṃvinmātramaye viśvasmin saṃvidi ca vimarśātmikāyāṃ vimarśasya ca śabdanātmakatāyāṃ siddhāyāṃ sakalajaganniṣṭhavastunaḥ tadgatasya ca karmaphalasambandhavaicitryasya yat vimarśanaṃ tad eva śāstram iti parameśvarasvabhāvābhinna eva samastaḥ śāstrasaṃdarbho vastuta ekaphalaprāpakaḥ ekādhikāryuddeśenaiva tatra tu parameśvaraniyatiśaktimahimnaiva bhāge bhāge rūḍhiḥ lokānām iti ||
children.translated_text: There, when it has been established that the universe consists of consciousness alone, that consciousness has the nature of reflective awareness, and that reflective awareness has the nature of verbal expression, the reflective consideration of the objects established in the whole world, and of the varied relation between action and result within them, is itself scripture. Thus the whole complex of scripture is in reality not different from the nature of <s>Parameśvara</s>, and it leads to one result, with reference to one qualified recipient. But through the greatness of <s>Parameśvara</s>'s power of ordering necessity, people become conventionally established in different portions of it.

children.text: kecit māyocitabhedaparāmarśātmani vedāgamādiśāstre rūḍhāḥ anye tathāvidha eva mokṣābhimānena sāṃkhyavaiṣṇavaśāstrādau pare tu viviktaśivasvabhāvāmarśanasāre śaivasiddhāntādau anye sarvamayaparameśvaratāmarśanasāre mataṃgādiśāstre kecit tu viralaviralāḥ samastāvacchedavandhyasvātantryānandaparamārthasaṃvinmayaparameśvarasvarūpāmarśanātmani śrītrikaśāstrakrame kecit tu pūrvapūrvatyāgakrameṇa laṅghanena vā ity evam ekaphalasiddhiḥ ekasmād eva āgamāt ||
children.translated_text: Some are established in scriptures such as the Vedas and Āgamas, whose nature is the apprehension of difference appropriate to <s>māyā</s>. Others, with the notion of liberation, are established in scriptures of that same kind, such as the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> systems. Others are established in the <s>Śaivasiddhānta</s> and the like, whose essence is the apprehension of the distinct nature of <s>Śiva</s>. Others are established in scriptures such as the <s>Mataṅga</s>, whose essence is the apprehension of <s>Parameśvara</s> as consisting of all. But a few, exceedingly rare, are established in the sequence of the venerable Trika scripture, whose nature is the apprehension of the form of <s>Parameśvara</s> as the ultimate reality, made of consciousness, freedom, and bliss, barren of all limitation. Some attain by successively abandoning the previous stages, or by overleaping them. Thus the accomplishment of the one result comes from one āgama alone.

children.text: bhedavāde 'pi samastāgamānām ekeśvarakāryatve 'pi prāmāṇyaṃ tāvat avasthitam prāmāṇyanibandhanasya ekadeśasaṃvādasya avigītatāyā anidaṃtāpravṛtteś ca tulyatvāt parasparabādho viṣayabhedāt akiṃcitkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even in the doctrine of difference, and even when all āgamas are the work of one Lord, their authority remains established. For the grounds of authority are the same: agreement in one part, being undisputed, and proceeding from a source that is not merely this-worldly. Mutual contradiction is ineffectual because their domains are different.

children.text: brahmahananatanniṣedhavat saṃskārabhedaḥ saṃskārātiśayaḥ tadabhāve kvacit anadhikṛtatvam iti samānam āśramabhedavat phalotkarṣācca utkarṣaḥ tatraiva upaniṣadbhāgavat bhinnakartṛkatve 'pi sarvasarvajñakṛtatvam atra saṃbhāvyate taduktatadatiriktayuktārthayogāt nityatve 'pi āgamānāṃ prasiddhiḥ tāvat avaśyopagamyā anvayavyatirekādhyakṣādīnāṃ tatprāmāṇyasya tanmūlatvāt satyaṃ rajataṃ paśyāmi iti hi sauvarṇikādiparaprasiddhyaiva prasiddhir eva āgamaḥ sā kācit dṛṣṭaphalā bubhukṣito bhuṅkte iti bālasya prasiddhita eva tatra tatra pravṛttiḥ nānvayavyatirekābhyāṃ tadā tayoḥ abhāvāt yauvanāvasthāyāṃ tadbhāvo 'pi akiṃcitkaraḥ prasiddhiṃ tu mūlīkṛtya so 'stu kasmaicit kāryāya kācit adṛṣṭavaidehyaprakṛtilayapuruṣakaivalyaphaladā kācit śivasamānatvaphaladā kācit aikyaparyavasāyinī sā ca pratyekam anekavidhā ity evaṃ bahutaraprasiddhipūrṇe jagati yo yādṛśo bhaviṣyan sa tādṛśīm eva prasiddhiṃ balād eva hṛdayaparyavasāyinīm abhimanyate ||
children.translated_text: As with the prohibition against killing a brāhmaṇa, there is a difference of sacramental impressions, an excellence of sacramental impression; in its absence, in some case there is non-qualification. This is the same as with the difference of āśramas. And because there is superiority of result, there is superiority, as in the Upaniṣadic portion itself. Even though the agents are different, here it is possible that everything is made by the omniscient one, because what is stated there is connected with meanings that are appropriate and not contradictory. Even if the āgamas are eternal, their established currency must first be accepted, since the validity of inference from concomitance and difference, perception, and so on has that as its root. For when I say, 'I see real silver,' its established status is only through the established usage of goldsmiths and others. Established usage itself is āgama. Some such usage has a visible result: a hungry person eats. A child acts here and there only from established usage, not from inference by agreement and difference, because at that time those two are absent. Even if they exist in youth, that accomplishes nothing; let them be for some purpose after taking established usage as the basis. Some established usage grants unseen results, such as the bodiless state, absorption into prakṛti, the isolation of puruṣa; some grants equality with <s>Śiva</s>; some terminates in unity. And each of these is manifold. Thus, in a world filled with very many established usages, whatever sort of person one is to become, that person necessarily accepts just such an established usage, one that comes to rest in his heart by force.

children.text: iti riktasya jantoḥ atiriktā vācoyuktiḥ tāsāṃ kāṃcana prasiddhiṃ pramāṇīkurvatā abhyupagantavyam eva āgamaprāmāṇyam iti sa āgama āśrayaṇīyo yatra utkṛṣṭaṃ phalam ity alam anyena ||
children.translated_text: Thus, for an empty creature, these additional verbal reasonings, while they make some established usage of theirs into a means of knowledge, must necessarily accept the authority of āgama. Therefore that āgama is to be relied upon in which the result is highest. Enough of anything else.

children.text: saṃvitprakāśaparamārthatayā yathaiva bhāty āmṛśaty api tatheti vivecayantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Discerning that, just as it shines by having the ultimate reality of the manifestation of consciousness, so too it reflects upon itself,

children.text: santaḥ samastamayacitpratibhāvimarśasāraṃ samāśrayata śāstram anuttarātma ||
children.translated_text: good people, take refuge in the unsurpassed scripture whose self is the essence of the reflective awareness in which all this consists as the appearance of consciousness.

children.text: jissa daḍhapasiddhighaḍie vavahāre soi asmi ṇīsaṃko
children.translated_text: In the practical dealings fashioned by his own firm established conviction, he is indeed without doubt.

children.text: taha hohi jahuttiṇa pasiddhirūḍhie paramasivo ||
children.translated_text: So, through the fixed force of a tradition transcending ordinary people, he becomes <s>Paramaśiva</s>.

children.text: nijadṛḍhaprasiddhighaṭite vyavahāre loka asti niḥśaṅkaḥ
children.translated_text: In worldly dealings formed by his own firm established conviction, a person is free from doubt;

children.text: tadā bhavati janottīrṇaprasiddhirūḍhaḥ paramaśivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, established in a convention that has gone beyond people, he becomes <s>Paramaśiva</s>.

children.text: Chapter 22
atha samastā iyam upāsā samunmiṣattādṛśadṛḍhavāsanārūḍhān adhikāriṇaḥ prati śrīmatkaulikaprakriyayā nirūpyate tatra uktaṃ yogasaṃcārādau ānandaṃ brahma taddehe tridhauṣṭyāntyavyavasthitam ||
children.translated_text: Now this whole worship is explained, according to the venerable Kaula procedure, for qualified practitioners who have mounted upon such a firmly emerging latent disposition. There it is said in the <s>Yogasaṃcāra</s> and related texts: Bliss is brahman; in that body it is established in three ways, at the lips, and at the end.

children.text: abrahmacāriṇas tasya tyāgād ānandavarjitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who are not celibate, by abandoning it, are deprived of bliss.

children.text: ānandakṛtrimāhāravarjaṃ cakrasya yājakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sacrificers of the circle, except for artificial food consisting of bliss,

children.text: dvaye 'pi narake ghore tasmād enāṃ sthitiṃ bhajet ||
children.translated_text: both go to a terrible hell; therefore one should adopt this condition.

children.text: tad anayā sthityā kulayāgaḥ sa ca ṣoḍhā bāhye śaktau svadehe yāmale prāṇe saṃvidi ca iti ||
children.translated_text: By this condition, therefore, there is the <s>kulayāga</s> (clan sacrifice), and it is sixfold: in the external support, in the śakti, in one's own body, in the couple, in the breath, and in consciousness.

children.text: tatra ca uttara uttara utkṛṣṭaḥ pūrvaḥ pūrvas tadrucyartham ||
children.translated_text: And among these, each later one is superior to the preceding one; each preceding one is for the sake of taste for that later one.

children.text: siddhikāmasya dvitīyaturyapañcamāḥ sarvathā nirvartyāḥ ṣaṣṭhas tu mumukṣoḥ mukhyaḥ tasyāpi dvitīyādyā naimittike yathāsambhavam anuṣṭheyā eva vidhipūraṇārthaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: For one who desires siddhi, the second, fourth, and fifth are to be performed in every way; but the sixth is primary for one who desires liberation. Even for him, the second and the others are to be performed on occasional rites as far as possible, and for the completion of the injunction.

children.text: tatra bāhyaṃ sthaṇḍilam ānandapūrṇaṃ vīrapātram aruṇaḥ paṭaḥ pūrvoktam api vā liṅgādi ||
children.translated_text: There, the external support is a sthaṇḍila altar filled with bliss, a hero's vessel, a red cloth, or the liṅga and other supports already mentioned before.

children.text: tatra snānādikartavyānapekṣayaiva pūrṇānandaviśrāntyaiva labdhaśuddhiḥ prathamaṃ prāṇasaṃviddehaikībhāvaṃ bhāvayitvā saṃvidaś ca paramaśivarūpatvāt saptaviṃśativāraṃ mantram uccārya mūrdhavaktrahṛdguhyamūrtiṣu anulomavilomābhyāṃ viśvādhvaparipūrṇatā parameśvare aparatve parāparatve paratve 'pi ca ||
children.translated_text: There, without regard for the duties of bathing and the like, since purity has been obtained simply by repose in complete bliss, first, having contemplated the unity of breath, consciousness, and body, and because consciousness has the form of <s>Paramaśiva</s>, he should utter the mantra twenty-seven times. In the head, face, heart, secret place, and image, by the forward and reverse sequences, there is the fullness of the whole course of the universe in <s>Parameśvara</s>, in the lower state, in the higher-lower state, and also in the higher state.

children.text: tathāhi māyāpuṃprakṛtiguṇadhīprabhṛti dharāntaṃ saptaviṃśatitattvāni kalādīnāṃ tatraiva antarbhāvāt vidyāśaktāv api parāparatve brahmapañcakasya sadyastvājātatvabhavodbhavatvādīnāṃ dharmāṇāṃ saptaviṃśatirūpatvam eva uktaṃ śrīmallakuleśādipādaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For thus, from māyā, puruṣa, prakṛti, guṇas, buddhi, and the rest down to earth, there are twenty-seven tattvas, because kalā and the others are included there itself. And in the power of vidyā too, in the higher-lower state, the fivefold brahman, with properties such as being Sadya, being Ajāta, being Bhavodbhava, and so on, has precisely the form of twenty-seven, as was stated by the venerable <s>Lakuleśa</s> and other masters.

children.text: paratve 'pi pañcaśaktiḥ hi parameśvaraḥ pratiśakti ca pañcarūpatā evaṃ pañcaviṃśatiḥ śaktayaḥ tāś ca anyonyam anudbhinnavibhāgā ity ekā śaktiḥ sā cānudbhinnavibhāgā ity evaṃ saptaviṃśatirūpayā vyāptyā saṃvidagneḥ śikhāṃ buddhiprāṇarūpāṃ sakṛduccāramātreṇaiva baddhāṃ kuryāt yena paramaśiva eva pratibaddhā tantrātiriktaṃ na kiṃcid abhidhāvati tathāvidhabuddhyadhiṣṭhitakaraṇacakrānuvedhena purovartino yāgadravyagṛhadigādhārādīn api tanmayībhūtān kuryāt tato 'rghapātram api śikhābandhavyāptyaiva pūrayet pūjayec ca tadvipruḍbhiḥ sthaṇḍilāny api tadrasena vāmānāmāṅguṣṭhayogāt dehacakreṣu mantracakraṃ pūjayet tarpayet ca tataḥ prāṇāntaḥ tataḥ sthaṇḍile triśūlātmakaṃ śaktitrayāntam āsanaṃ kalpayet māyāntaṃ hi sārṇe aukāre ca śaktitrayāntam āsanaṃ kalpayet māyāntaṃ hi sārṇe aukāre ca śaktitrayāntaṃ tadupari yājyā vimarśarūpā śaktiḥ ity evaṃ sakṛd uccāreṇaiva ādhārādheyanyāsaṃ kṛtvā tatraiva ādheyabhūtāyām api saṃvidi viśvaṃ paśyet tad api ca saṃvinmayam ity evaṃ viśvasya saṃvidā tena ca tasyāḥ saṃpuṭībhāvo bhavati saṃvida uditaṃ tatraiva paryavasitaṃ yato viśvaṃ vedyāc ca saṃvit udeti tatraiva ca viśrāmyati iti etāvattvaṃ saṃvittattvaṃ saṃpuṭībhāvadvayāt labhyate ||
children.translated_text: Although he is supreme, <s>Parameśvara</s> is indeed fivefold power; and since each power has five forms, there are thus twenty-five powers. Since these are not divided from one another by distinct partitions, they are one power; and since that too is without divided partitions, by such a pervasion of twenty-seven forms he should, with the mere single utterance, bind the flame of the fire of consciousness, which has the form of intellect and vital breath, as the śikhā. By this, <s>Paramaśiva</s> himself is bound in place and does not run after anything outside the tantra. Likewise, by the penetration of the circle of instruments presided over by an intellect of that kind, he should make even the ritual substances, house, directions, supports, and so on before him become of that nature. Then he should also fill the argha vessel by that very pervasion of the binding of the śikhā, and worship; and with its drops he should worship even the sthaṇḍila altars. With that savor, through the joining of the left-hand ring finger and thumb, he should worship the mantra-cakra in the bodily cakras and make tarpaṇa. Then, up to the vital breath, and then on the sthaṇḍila, he should imagine a seat whose nature is the trident and which extends to the triad of powers. For in the syllable with the bindu, in the au-kāra, he should imagine a seat extending to the triad of powers, up to māyā; and above it is the worshiped power, whose form is reflective awareness. Thus, having made the placing of support and supported by the single utterance itself, he should see the universe in that very consciousness which is also the supported thing; and that too is made of consciousness. In this way there occurs an enclosing of the universe by consciousness and of consciousness by that universe. For what has arisen from consciousness comes to rest there itself; the universe arises from the knowable, and consciousness also rises from it and rests there itself. Such is the nature of consciousness, attained from the twofold enclosing.

children.text: tad uktam sṛṣṭiṃ tu saṃpuṭīkṛtya iti ||
children.translated_text: This has been said: 'Having enclosed creation,' and so on.

children.text: tato gandhadhūpāsavakusumādīn ātmaprahvībhāvāntān arpayitvā svaviśrāntyā japtvā upasaṃhṛtya jale nikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having offered perfumes, incense, liquor, flowers, and the like, ending with the humbling of the self, having recited by resting in himself, and having withdrawn the rite, he should cast it into water.

children.text: iti bāhyayāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the outer sacrifice.

children.text: atha śaktau tatra anyonyaṃ śaktitālāsāvīrāṇām ubhayeṣām ubhayātmakatvena prollāsaprārambhasṛṣṭyantaśivaśaktiprabodhe parasparaṃ vyāpārāt parameśaniyatyā ca śuddharūpatayā tatra prādhānyam etena ca viśiṣṭacakrasyāpi śaktitvaṃ vyākhyātam tatra śikhābandhavyāptyaiva pūjanaṃ śaktitrayāntam āsanaṃ koṇatraye madhye visargaśaktiḥ iti tu vyāptau viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, in regard to the śakti: there, because the śakti, the tāla, the liquor, and the heroes mutually operate upon one another in the awakening of <s>Śiva</s> and śakti, beginning with the arising and ending with creation, since both sides have the nature of both, and because by the ordinance of <s>Parameśa</s> they are pure in form, the śakti has primacy there. By this, the śakti-nature of the special cakra too has been explained. There the worship is performed by the very pervasion of śikhā-binding; the seat extends to the triad of powers, and in the three corners and the middle is the power of emission. This is the particular feature in the pervasion.

children.text: evaṃ svadehe tatraiva cakre tato brahmarandhrādyanucakreṣu ||
children.translated_text: In this way, in one's own body, in that very cakra, and then in the subsidiary cakras beginning with the brahmarandhra.

children.text: atha yāmale śakter lakṣaṇam etat tadvad abhedas tato 'napekṣya vayaḥ
children.translated_text: Now, in the yāmala, this is the characteristic of the śakti: like that, through non-difference, one should not take age into account,

children.text: jātyādīṃś cāsaṅgāt loketarayugalajaṃ hi tādātmyam ||
children.translated_text: nor caste and the like, because of non-attachment; for identity born from a worldly or non-worldly pair is such.

children.text: kāryahetusahotthatvāt traidhaṃ sākṣād athānyathā
children.translated_text: Because effect, cause, and co-arising are involved, it is threefold, directly and otherwise.

children.text: kﾱptāvato mitho 'bhyarcya tarpyānandāntikatvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having mutually worshiped those so arranged, they are to be satisfied because of their nearness to bliss.

children.text: cakram arcet tadaucityād anucakraṃ tathānugam
children.translated_text: One should worship the cakra according to its propriety, and likewise the subsidiary cakra and the follower.

children.text: bahiḥ puṣpādināntaś ca gandhabhuktyāsavādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Externally, this is with flowers and the like; internally, with perfume, enjoyment, liquor, and so forth.

children.text: evam ānandasaṃdohitatacceṣṭocchalatsthitiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, when its activity is made abundant with bliss and rises up into manifestation,

children.text: anucakragaṇaś cakratādātmyād abhilīyate ||
children.translated_text: the group of subsidiary cakras is dissolved because of identity with the cakra.

children.text: nijanijabhogābhogapravikāsamayasvarūpaparimarśe
children.translated_text: In the reflective awareness of the nature of the moment of expansion of each one's own enjoyment and non-enjoyment,

children.text: kramaśo 'nucakradevyaḥ saṃviccakraṃ hi madhyamaṃ yānti ||
children.translated_text: the goddesses of the subsidiary cakras gradually go to the consciousness-cakra, which is central.

children.text: anucakradevatātmakamarīcigaṇapūraṇādhigatavīryam
children.translated_text: Having gained potency through the filling by the rays consisting of the deities of the subsidiary cakras,

children.text: tacchaktitadvadātmakam anyonyasamunmukhaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: it becomes that śakti and, like her, faces the other in mutual openness.

children.text: tadyugalamūrdhvadhāmapraveśasaspandajātasaṃkṣobham
children.translated_text: When that pair is agitated by the vibration born from entering the upper abode,

children.text: kṣubhnāty anucakrāṇy api tāni tadā tanmayāni na pṛthak tu ||
children.translated_text: it agitates the subsidiary cakras too; then they become of that nature and are not separate.

children.text: itthaṃ yāmalam etad galitabhidāsaṃkathaṃ yadaiva tadā
children.translated_text: Thus, whenever this yāmala is a conversation in which difference has melted away, then,

children.text: kramatāratamyayogāt saiva hi saṃvidvisargasaṃghaṭṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because of the connection of graded sequence, it is precisely the collision of consciousness and emission.

children.text: taddhruvadhāmānuttaram ubhayātmakajagad udāram ānandam
children.translated_text: Its fixed abode is the unsurpassed, the generous bliss that is the world having the nature of both.

children.text: no śāntaṃ nāpy uditaṃ śāntoditasūtikāraṇaṃ paraṃ kaulam ||
children.translated_text: It is not quiescent, nor arisen; it is the supreme kaula, the cause that gives birth to both the quiescent and the arisen.

children.text: anavacchinnapadepsus tāṃ saṃvidam ātmasātkuryāt
children.translated_text: One who desires the unbounded state should make that consciousness his own.

children.text: śāntoditātmakadvayam atha yugapad udeti śaktiśaktimatoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the pair whose nature is quiescent and arisen comes forth simultaneously from śakti and the possessor of śakti.

children.text: svātmānyonyāveśāt śāntānyatve dvayor dvayātmatvāt
children.translated_text: Because each self enters the other, and because in the otherness of the quiescent the two have a twofold nature,

children.text: śaktis tu tadvad uditāṃ sṛṣṭiṃ puṣṇāti no tadvān ||
children.translated_text: śakti, however, nourishes the arisen creation in that way; the possessor of śakti does not do so in that same manner.

children.text: tasyāṃ cāryaṃ kulam atha tayā nṛṣu proktayogasaṃghaṭṭān
children.translated_text: In her, then, the venerable kula exists; and through her, among human beings, from the conjunctions of yoga that have been taught,

children.text: atha sṛṣṭe dvitaye 'smin śāntoditadhāmni ye 'nusaṃdadhate ||
children.translated_text: those who, in this twofold creation, contemplate the abode that is quiescent and arisen,

children.text: prācyāṃ visargasattām anavacchidite pade rūḍhāḥ
children.translated_text: are rooted in the prior reality of emission, in the unbounded state.

children.text: uditaṃ ca mitho vaktrān mukhyād vaktre pragṛhyate ca bahiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And what has arisen is mutually received from mouth to mouth, from the chief mouth to another mouth, and outwardly.

children.text: tṛptaṃ devīcakraṃ siddhijñānāpavargadaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: The satisfied circle of goddesses becomes the giver of siddhi, knowledge, and liberation.

children.text: śāntābhyāse śāntaṃ śivam eti yad atra devatācakram ||
children.translated_text: In the practice of the quiescent, that circle of deities here reaches quiescent <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: śūnyaṃ nirānandamayaṃ nirvṛtinijadhāmato 'rghaṃ ca
children.translated_text: The argha is empty, made of no-bliss, from the innate abode of cessation;

children.text: raṇaraṇakarasān nijarasabharitabahirbhāvacarvaṇarasena ||
children.translated_text: through the savor of chewing the external state filled with one's own savor from the excited hum of rasa,

children.text: āntarapūrṇasamucchaladanucakraṃ yāti cakram atha tad api
children.translated_text: the cakra goes to the subsidiary cakra that surges up with inner fullness; and that too,

children.text: ucchalati prāgvad iti trividho 'nvartho visargo 'yam ||
children.translated_text: rises up as before. Thus this visarga has a threefold meaning.

children.text: etad visargadhāmani parimarśanatas tridhaiva manuvīryam
children.translated_text: In this abode of visarga, through reflective awareness, the potency of the mantra is precisely threefold.

children.text: tattatsaṃvidgarbhe mantras tattatphalaṃ sūte ||
children.translated_text: A mantra, held in the womb of each corresponding cognition, gives birth to each corresponding result.

children.text: koṇatrayāntarāśritanityoditamaṅgalacchade kamale
children.translated_text: In the lotus that rests within the three angles, whose covering is ever-risen auspiciousness,

children.text: nityāviyutaṃ nālaṃ ṣoḍaśadalakamalasanmūlam ||
children.translated_text: there is the stalk, never separated from the eternal one, whose true root is the sixteen-petalled lotus.

children.text: madhyasthanālagumphitasarojayugaghaṭṭanakramādagnau
children.translated_text: From the sequence of striking together the pair of lotuses bound by the middle stalk, in the fire,

children.text: madhyasthaśaśadharasundaradinakarakaraughasaṃghaṭṭāt ||
children.translated_text: from the collision of the streams of rays of the moon and the beautiful sun situated in the middle,

children.text: tridalāruṇavīryakalāsaṅgān madhye 'ṅkurasṛṣṭiḥ
children.translated_text: and from the conjunction of the red three-petalled virile kalā, the sprouting creation arises in the middle.

children.text: iti śaśadharavāsarapaticitraguṣaṃghaṭṭamudrayā jhaṭiti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the seal of the wondrous collision of the moon-bearer and the lord of day, immediately,

children.text: sṛṣṭyādikramam antaḥ kurvaṃs turye sthitiṃ labhate
children.translated_text: performing inwardly the sequence beginning with creation, one attains abiding in the fourth state.

children.text: etat khecaramudrāveśe 'nyonyaṃ svaśaktiśaktimatoḥ ||
children.translated_text: This occurs in the penetration of the <s>khecarīmudrā</s>, through the mutual relation of one's own śakti and the possessor of śakti.

children.text: pānopabhogalīlāhāsādiṣu yo bhaved vimarśamayaḥ
children.translated_text: In drinking, enjoyment, play, laughter, and the like, one who becomes full of reflective awareness,

children.text: avyaktadhvanirāvasphoṭaśrutinādanādāntaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: through indistinct sound, reverberation, bursting forth, heard tone, resonance, and the end of resonance,

children.text: avyucchinnānāhataparamārthair mantravīryaṃ tat
children.translated_text: through the uninterrupted, unstruck supreme realities: that is the potency of mantra.

children.text: gamanāgamaviśrāntiṣu karṇe nayane dvilakṣyasamparke ||
children.translated_text: In going, coming, and resting, at the ear and the eye, in the contact of the two objects,

children.text: tatsammīlanayoge dehāntākhye ca yāmale cakre
children.translated_text: in the union consisting in their closing together, and in the paired circle called the end of the body,

children.text: kucamadhyahṛdayadeśād oṣṭhānte kaṇṭhagaṃ yad avyaktam ||
children.translated_text: that which is indistinct, passing from the region of the heart between the breasts up to the lips and into the throat,

children.text: tac cakradvayamadhyagam ākarṇya kṣobhavigamasamaye yat
children.translated_text: when, situated between the two circles, it is heard at the moment when agitation ceases,

children.text: nirvānti tatra caivaṃ yo 'ṣṭavidho nādabhairavaḥ paramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there it becomes extinguished. Thus there is the supreme eightfold <s>Nādabhairava</s>.

children.text: jyotir dhvaniś ca yasmāt sā māntrī vyāptir ucyate paramā
children.translated_text: Because light and sound arise from it, that is called the supreme mantric pervasion.

children.text: karmaṇi karmaṇi viduṣaḥ syāj jīvato muktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the knower, in every action, there will be liberation while living.

children.text: tajjñaḥ śāstre muktaḥ parakulavijñānabhājanaṃ garbhaḥ
children.translated_text: One who knows that is liberated in the scripture; he is the womb, the vessel of knowledge of the supreme kula.

children.text: śūnyāśūnyālayaṃ kuryād ekadaṇḍe 'nalānilau ||
children.translated_text: He should make fire and wind rest in the single staff, the abode of emptiness and non-emptiness.

children.text: śūlaṃ samarasīkṛtya rase rasam iva sthitam
children.translated_text: Having made the trident one in equal savor, as flavor abides within flavor,

children.text: tyaktāśaṅko nirācāro nāham asmīti bhāvayan ||
children.translated_text: free from apprehension, beyond prescribed conduct, meditating, 'I am not the ego,'

children.text: dehasthā devatāḥ paśyan hlādodvegādi ciddhane
children.translated_text: seeing the deities established in the body, and delight, agitation, and the like within the mass of consciousness,

children.text: karṇākṣimukhanāsādicakrasthaṃ devatāgaṇam ||
children.translated_text: always seeing the host of deities stationed in the circles of the ears, eyes, mouth, nose, and so on as the perceiver,

children.text: grahītāraṃ sadā paśyan khecaryā sidhyati dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: he certainly attains success through <s>khecarī</s>.

children.text: śvabhre sudūre jhaṭiti svadehaṃ saṃpātayan vāsam asāhasena
children.translated_text: Swiftly casting his own body into a very distant ravine, yet without rashness,

children.text: ākuñcya hastadvitayaṃ prapaśyan mudrām imāṃ vyomacarīṃ bhajeta ||
children.translated_text: drawing in both hands and looking carefully, he should cultivate this <s>vyomacarī</s> mudrā.

children.text: ity eṣa yāmalayāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus this is the yāmala sacrifice.

children.text: uktavyāptike prāṇe viśvamaye proktasaṃvidvyāptyā tarpaṇānnagandhadhūpādisamarpaṇena upodbalanaṃ prāṇayāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the breath has the pervasion just described and is universal, strengthening it by the previously stated pervasion of consciousness, through offerings such as satisfaction, food, perfume, incense, and so on, is the prāṇa-sacrifice.

children.text: viśrāntirūḍhis tu saṃvidyāgaḥ prāg eva nirūpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the sacrifice of consciousness, as the firm establishment of repose, has already been explained earlier.

children.text: evam etebhyo yāgebhyo 'nyatamaṃ kṛtvā yadi tathāvidhanirvicikitsatāpacitritahṛdayaḥ śiṣyo bhavati tadā tasmai tadyāgadarśanapūrvakaṃ tilājyāhutipūrvakanirapekṣam eva pūrvoktavyāptyā anusaṃdhānakrameṇa avalokanayā dīkṣāṃ kuryāt parokṣadīkṣādike naimittikānte tu pūrva eva vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, after performing any one among these sacrifices, if the disciple has a heart variegated by such doubt-free intensity, then for him, after showing that sacrifice, and without dependence on sesame and ghee oblations, he should perform initiation simply through the previously stated pervasion, by the sequence of contemplation and by looking. In occasional rites such as initiation at a distance, the same earlier procedure applies.

children.text: kevalam etad yāgapradhānatayā iti ||
children.translated_text: Only, this is because of the predominance of that sacrifice.

children.text: guruśarīre saptamaḥ kulayāgaḥ sarvottamaḥ so 'pi prāg yāgasāhityena sakṛd eva kṛtaḥ sarvaṃ pūrayati iti śivam ||
children.translated_text: The seventh kulayāga, in the body of the guru, is the highest of all. That too, when performed just once together with the sacrifices taught before, fulfills everything. Thus auspiciousness.
